51-00-55-200-801Preventive MaintenancePDF p. 59

2. Preventive Maintenance

A. References

Reference Title 20-30-80-910-801 General Cleaning of Metal (Series 80) (P/B 201) 51-21-11 P/B 701 PAINT STRIPPING - CLEANING/PAINTING 51-21-31 P/B 701 CORROSION REMOVAL AND CONTROL - CLEANING/PAINTING 51-21-91 P/B 701 CORROSION INHIBITING COMPOUND - CLEANING/PAINTING 737 NDT Part 6, 51-00-00, Procedure 3 Investigation of Fire Damage on Aircraft Structure

B. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification B00081 Solvent - Trichloroethylene ASTM D4080

C. Preventive Maintenance

SUBTASK 51-00-55-020-001 (1) After the fire is out, do these steps: (a) Remove fire damaged interiors to expose structure. This includes interior trim, seats, passenger service units, linings, insulations, galleys, etc. Removal of tubing, cables, electrical wiring, etc., is not necessary if they are unaffected. (b) Screen or mask off areas not affected. (c) Open all drains, hatches and doors for drainage and ventilation. Use compressed air to blow dry all hidden recesses. SUBTASK 51-00-55-200-001 (2) Examine the structure for these items: (a) Heat damage, soot, fire extinguishing material residue and corrosion. 51-00-55 (b) Paint discoloration indicates temperature had exceeded 350°F (177°C). NOTE: Structural analysis required if temperature exceeds 350°F (177°C). (c) Look for acid contamination of the structure, control cables and wire bundles with litmus paper. NOTE: Products of combustion or decomposed fire extinguishants may combine with moisture to form corrosive chemicals. (d) Flush the structure with water when necessary to remove contamination. SUBTASK 51-00-55-030-001 (3) Remove and replace structure damaged beyond repair. NOTE: Use Investigation of Fire Damage on Aircraft Structure, 737 NDT Part 6, 51-00-00, Procedure 3 to determine any change in heat-treat of any suspect structure. SUBTASK 51-00-55-100-001 (4) Remove soot by washing affected areas with solvent, B00081, or an applicable solvent per TASK 20-30-80-910-801. Pressure gun application is suggested for flushing fay surface joints, such as stringers to body skins. An absorbent cloth held beneath the area will catch the contaminated solvent. SUBTASK 51-00-55-280-001 (5) Inhibit corrosion that could be caused by residue from the dry powder fire extinguisher by washing affected areas with a 10-percent-by-weight solution of sodium dichromate. The dichromate solution acts as a mild corrosion inhibitor. Thoroughly dry all treated surfaces before continuing with any other treatment. Repeat rinse and inhibition treatment if any white residue shows. NOTE: Any remaining liquid dichromate solution will weep through seams and fastener holes during cabin pressurization and could subsequently discolor the exterior paint finish. Forced hot air used to dry the area may be necessary before further flight if humidity is high. SUBTASK 51-00-55-211-001 (6) Look for remaining contamination behind clips, brackets, nutplates. SUBTASK 51-00-55-200-002 (7) After removal of contamination, do the steps in CORROSION REMOVAL AND CONTROL - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-31/701 when corrosion is found. SUBTASK 51-00-55-370-001 (8) When corrosion is removed, do the steps in PAINT STRIPPING - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-11/701. SUBTASK 51-00-55-600-001 (9) To apply the corrosion inhibiting compound, do the steps in CORROSION INHIBITING COMPOUND - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-91/701.

ATA 51-00-56 - Section

2 tasks
51-00-56-211-801Detection and Isolation of Alkaline Contaminated AreaPDF p. 61

2. Detection and Isolation of Alkaline Contaminated Area

A. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification G50305 Sheeting - Plastic, Polyethylene

B. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-00-56-211-001 (1) Do this step for detection of alkaline contamination: (a) Alkalines are clear and are not color detectable. 1) A white powdery deposit (aluminum oxide) would indicate corrosion on aluminum structure. NOTE: Around the top of nickel-cadmium battery cells, the alkaline electrolyte that has overflowed the vent caps reacts with the carbon dioxide in the air and produce a white powdery deposit. This white deposit is not corrosive and otherwise harmless but is an indication that electrolyte has spilled or otherwise escaped. SUBTASK 51-00-56-160-001 (2) On discovery of alkaline spills, steps should be taken to contain the contaminated area. The following precautions are advised: (a) Do not allow alkaline spills to spread to adjacent areas that will not be cleaned. (b) In battery areas, protection of equipment beneath using plastic sheeting, G50305 is advised. If equipment is operating, venting should be maintained. (c) Consider protecting uncontaminated areas by taping down protective material such as plastic sheeting, G50305.

51-00-56-100-801Alkaline Spillage CleanupPDF p. 62

3. Alkaline Spillage Cleanup

A. References

Reference Title 51-21-11 P/B 701 PAINT STRIPPING - CLEANING/PAINTING 51-21-31 P/B 701 CORROSION REMOVAL AND CONTROL - CLEANING/PAINTING 51-21-91 P/B 701 CORROSION INHIBITING COMPOUND - CLEANING/PAINTING

B. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification B00636 Acid, Acetic (Vinegar) (5%-10% Acetic Acid) Commercially available product G00116 Sponge - Synthetic G00215 Brush - Soft Bristle Fiber G01659 Swab - Cotton Or Rayon, (Disposable) G50256 Water, Regular G50305 Sheeting - Plastic, Polyethylene G50316 Cloth - Clean, Dry, Lint-free, White, Cotton

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-00-56-913-001 (1) If equipment is adjacent to the treatment area, use plastic sheeting, G50305 to cover the equipment to prevent inadvertent splashing of alkalines or treatment fluids SUBTASK 51-00-56-100-001 (2) Wipe up excess fluids with cotton cloth, G50316 and discard cloth into plastic container for disposal. SUBTASK 51-00-56-561-001 (3) Do these steps to neutralize alkaline contamination: (a) Neutralize the treatment area with a 5 percent acid, B00636 solution or full strength household vinegar applied with a brush, G00215, cotton cloth, G50316 or swab, G01659. (b) Continue to apply the solution until bubbles cease. Then allow the solution to remain on the surface for an additional 5 minutes. (c) Remove the neutralized mixture with a cotton cloth, G50316 or sponge, G00116. (d) Rinse the affected area with generous quantities of clean water, G50256. Occasionally agitate the surface with a brush, G00215. (e) Neutralization of the alkaline fluid should be determined with litmus paper. (f) Wipe dry with clean cotton cloth, G50316. SUBTASK 51-00-56-350-001 (4) After removal of contamination, do the steps in CORROSION REMOVAL AND CONTROL - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-31/701 when corrosion is found. SUBTASK 51-00-56-370-001 (5) When corrosion is removed, do the steps in PAINT STRIPPING - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-11/701, if necessary. 51-00-56 SUBTASK 51-00-56-600-001 (6) To apply the corrosion inhibiting compound, do the steps in CORROSION INHIBITING COMPOUND - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-91/701. SUBTASK 51-00-56-741-001 (7) Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition.

(b) In battery areas, protection of equipment beneath using plastic sheeting, G50305 is advised. 51-00-57-100-801Acid Spillage CleanupPDF p. 66

3. Acid Spillage Cleanup

A. References

Reference Title 51-21-11 P/B 701 PAINT STRIPPING - CLEANING/PAINTING 51-21-31 P/B 701 CORROSION REMOVAL AND CONTROL - CLEANING/PAINTING 51-21-91 P/B 701 CORROSION INHIBITING COMPOUND - CLEANING/PAINTING

B. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-419 Gloves - Rubber, Elbow Length STD-1392 Shield - Facial Protection STD-1393 Aprons STD-1394 Boots STD-1395 Head Gear STD-3904 Goggles - Safety

C. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification B00095 Compound - Sodium Bicarbonate ASTM D928 G00116 Sponge - Synthetic G00215 Brush - Soft Bristle Fiber G50256 Water, Regular G50305 Sheeting - Plastic, Polyethylene G50316 Cloth - Clean, Dry, Lint-free, White, Cotton

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-00-57-160-002 WARNING DO NOT GET THIS MATERIAL IN YOUR MOUTH, EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. PUT ON EYE PROTECTION (GOGGLES, OR OTHER APPROVED PROTECTION) AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE THIS MATERIAL. MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS SUFFICIENT AIRFLOW. THIS MATERIAL CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) T ake these precautions when you work with an acid spill condition: (a) Adequate protective clothing should be worn when handling or working in acid contaminated areas. 1) elbow length rubber gloves, STD-419 2) safety goggles, STD-3904 3) face shield, STD-1392 4) aprons, STD-1393 51-00-57 5) boots, STD-1394 6) head gear, STD-1395 (b) Wash hands after using acid neutralizing treatment solution and/or materials before eating or smoking. (c) Waste materials, solvents, chemical solutions, wiping rags, masking materials, etc., shall be collected and disposed of safely. SUBTASK 51-00-57-913-001 (2) If equipment is adjacent to the treatment area, use plastic sheeting, G50305 to cover the equipment to prevent inadvertent splashing of acids or treatment fluids SUBTASK 51-00-57-100-001 (3) Wipe up excess fluids with cotton cloth, G50316 and discard cloth into plastic container for disposal. SUBTASK 51-00-57-561-001 (4) Do these steps to neutralize acid contamination: (a) Neutralize the treatment area with a 20 percent sodium bicarbonate solution applied with a brush or cloth swab. Particular attention should be given to faying surface joints. Pressure application may be required to flush the joint thoroughly. NOTE: 16 oz (454 g) of compound, B00095 in 1.00 gal (3.79 l) of water, G50256 will give the desired mixture. (b) Continue to apply the solution until bubbles cease. Then allow the solution to remain on the surface for an additional 5 minutes. (c) Remove the neutralized mixture with a cotton cloth, G50316 or sponge, G00116. (d) Rinse the affected area with generous quantities of clean water, G50256. Occasionally agitate the surface with a brush, G00215. (e) Neutralization of the acidic fluid should be determined with litmus paper. (f) Wipe dry with clean cotton cloth, G50316. SUBTASK 51-00-57-350-001 (5) After removal of contamination, do the steps in CORROSION REMOVAL AND CONTROL - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-31/701 when corrosion is found. SUBTASK 51-00-57-370-001 (6) When corrosion is removed, do the steps in PAINT STRIPPING - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-11/701, if necessary. SUBTASK 51-00-57-600-001 (7) To apply the corrosion inhibiting compound, do the steps in CORROSION INHIBITING COMPOUND - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-91/701. SUBTASK 51-00-57-741-001 (8) Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition.

ATA 51-00-60 - Section

1 tasks
51-00-60-200-801Preventive MaintenancePDF p. 89

2. Preventive Maintenance

A. General

(1) The use of airplanes for bulk shipment of live animals necessitates periodic cleaning and deodorizing of the airplane. This provides an excellent opportunity to perform preventative maintenance because the cargo linings and insulation blankets are removed.

B. References

Reference Title 25-52-00 P/B 601 CARGO COMPARTMENT - INSPECTION/CHECK 25-52-00-100-801 Cargo Compartment Cleaning (P/B 701) 25-80-00 P/B 401 INSULATION BLANKET - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION 51-21-91-620-802 Application of Corrosion Inhibiting Compound (P/B 701) 51-41 AIRFRAME DRAINAGE 53-05-03 P/B 201 FUSELAGE - STRUCTURAL INSPECTIONS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-00-60-100-001 (1) When known animal waste spills have occurred, do this task: Cargo Compartment Cleaning, TASK 25-52-00-100-801. NOTE: Avoid spreading the spilled fluids through floor clearances. 51-00-60 SUBTASK 51-00-60-160-001 (2) Inspect the cargo compartments. (a) CARGO COMPARTMENT - INSPECTION/CHECK, PAGEBLOCK 25-52-00/601. (3) As necessary and when known spills have occurred, inspect the insulation blankets for indication of liquid in the area of the spill. (a) If blankets are dry and no indication of liquid is observed, then restore airplane. (b) If blankets contain liquid then continue with further inspection: 1) Check the inner skin surface and fuselage structure for signs of corrosion, refer to FUSELAGE - STRUCTURAL INSPECTIONS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES, PAGEBLOCK 53-05-03/201 for more details. 2) Make sure that all drains are unobstructed and that there are no trapped liquids (AIRFRAME DRAINAGE, SECTION 51-41). 3) Replace contaminated insulation blankets (INSULATION BLANKET - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 25-80-00/401). SUBTASK 51-00-60-600-001 (4) After the airplane has been cleaned and deodorized do these steps: (a) Apply corrosion inhibiting compound to the inner skin surface and structure (Application of Corrosion Inhibiting Compound, TASK 51-21-91-620-802) as necessary. NOTE: In the fuselage crown area, airplanes used for livestock transportation will require and receive more frequent preventive maintenance than recommended in Volume 2. (b) Install the equipment that you removed.

ATA 51-00-62 - Section

1 tasks
51-00-62-200-801Preventive MaintenancePDF p. 93

2. Preventive Maintenance

A. General

(1) The use of airplanes for shipment of fish requires periodic cleaning and deodorizing of the airplane using locally available supplies. As this requires removal of cargo lining and insulation blankets it also provides an excellent opportunity to perform corrosion preventive maintenance.

B. References

Reference Title 25-52-00-100-801 Cargo Compartment Cleaning (P/B 701) 25-80-00 INSULATION BLANKET 51-05-01 P/B 201 STRUCTURES - CORROSION INSPECTIONS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES 51-21-31 P/B 701 CORROSION REMOVAL AND CONTROL - CLEANING/PAINTING 51-21-91-620-802 Application of Corrosion Inhibiting Compound (P/B 701) 51-41 AIRFRAME DRAINAGE 53-42-11-100-801 Clean the Passenger Cabin and Cargo Compartment Track (P/B 701)

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-00-62-100-002 (1) When known spills have occurred, do this task: Cargo Compartment Cleaning, TASK 25-52-00-100-801. NOTE: Avoid spreading the spilled fluids through floor clearances. SUBTASK 51-00-62-100-001 (2) Do this task to clean spills on seat tracks: Clean the Passenger Cabin and Cargo Compartment Track, TASK 53-42-11-100-801. SUBTASK 51-00-62-160-001 (3) As necessary, inspect: (a) The inner skin surface and fuselage structure for signs of corrosion, refer to STRUCTURES - CORROSION INSPECTIONS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES, PAGEBLOCK 51-05-01/201 and CORROSION REMOVAL AND CONTROL - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-31/701 for more details. (b) Make sure that all drains are unobstructed and that there are no trapped liquids (AIRFRAME DRAINAGE, SECTION 51-41). (c) Condition of insulation blankets (INSULATION BLANKET , SUBJECT 25-80-00). 1) Replace soaked insulation blankets. SUBTASK 51-00-62-600-001 (4) After the airplane has been cleaned and deodorized do these steps: 51-00-62 (a) Apply corrosion inhibiting compound to the inner skin surface and structure (Application of Corrosion Inhibiting Compound, TASK 51-21-91-620-802) as necessary. (b) Install the equipment that you removed.

ATA 51-05-01 - Section

13 tasks
51-05-01-210-801737-6789 Basic Task DescriptionPDF p. 95

1. 737-6789 Basic Task Description NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. References

Reference Title 51-00-57 P/B 201 PROCEDURE AFTER ACID SPILLS (INCLUDING VACUUM WASTE SYSTEM SPILLS/LEAKS) - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES 51-00-58 STANDARD TREATMENT METHODS

B. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification C00174 Compound - Corrosion Preventive, Solvent Cutback, Cold Application MIL-PRF-16173 (Supersedes MIL-C-16173) C00915 Compound - Organic Corrosion Inhibiting, Advanced BMS3-29 G00009 Compound - Organic Corrosion Inhibiting BMS3-23

C. CPCP Basic Task

NOTE: Corrosion that was the result of a vacuum waste system spill/leak or other acidic spill, must be cleaned and neutralized (refer to PROCEDURE AFTER ACID SPILLS (INCLUDING VACUUM WASTE SYSTEM SPILLS/LEAKS) - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES, PAGEBLOCK 51-00-57/201) in all areas where the spill/leak has made contact with the structure. Make sure to clean and neutralize regions where the material can penetrate into structural joints. Also, make sure that the cause of the spill/leak is corrected. SUBTASK 51-05-01-210-022 (1) CPCP Basic T ask Item 1 is not applicable. SUBTASK 51-05-01-210-133 (2) Do the CPCP Basic T ask item 2 as follows: (a) Prior to inspection clean the area as required to accomplish CPCP Basic T ask Item 3. It is not necessary to remove normal amounts of sealant/leveling compound unless it has deteriorated to the point where moisture can penetrate down to the metal. A light uniform film of Corrosion Inhibiting Compound (CIC) that has not accumulated dirt or debris, will normally allow adequate inspection of the structure without removal. CIC may require removal if there are multiple layers and/or accumulations of dirt or debris. SUBTASK 51-05-01-210-024 (3) Do the CPCP Basic T ask Item 3 as follows: (a) Visually inspect all structure listed in the task description. The inspection method is as specified in each task description. Use Additional non-destructive inspections or visual inspections following partial disassembly if there are indications of hidden corrosion, such as bulging skins or corrosion running into splices, or under fittings, etc. In the task area, check the integrity of any sealant/leveling compound to determine if removal is required, and any corrosion inhibiting compound, particularly at faying surfaces, to determine if additional application is required per CPCP Basic T ask Item 6. 51-05-01 SUBTASK 51-05-01-210-025 (4) Do the CPCP Basic T ask item 4 as follows: (a) Remove all corrosion, evaluate damage and repair or replace all discrepant structure as required, including application of protective finishes per STANDARD TREATMENT METHODS, SUBJECT 51-00-58, or 737 Structural Repair Manual (SRM) D634A200, (-600), D634A201 (-700), D634A210 (-800), D634A211(-900), D634A333 (BBJ), or related service bulletin, as appropriate. Surface oxidation of ferrous metal fasteners may be handled by normal or existing maintenance practices. SUBTASK 51-05-01-210-026 (5) CPCP Basic T ask Item 5 is not applicable. SUBTASK 51-05-01-210-027 (6) Do the CPCP Basic T ask item 6 as follows: (a) Apply suitable approved water displacing / anti-corrosion compound as necessary. 1) The minimum requirement for all areas (except as noted in CPCP Basic T ask 6 (a) 3)) is single coat of water displacing / anti-corrosion compound that penetrates faying surfaces and displaces moisture, e.g. a single coat of compound, C00915 BMS 3-29 or corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 BMS 3-23, where the initial or previous coat has been disturbed or removed. 2) Not applicable 3) List of areas / items where water displacing/anti-corrosion compounds should not be applied: Water displacing / anti-corrosion compounds should not be applied in the following areas: • Cables, pulleys, wiring, plastics, elastomers, oxygen systems. • Lubricated or T eflon surfaces (E.g. greased joints, sealed bearings). • Over compound, C00174 Cosmoline 1058 (or Equivalent per MIL-C-16173 Grade 1). • Adjacent to tears / holes in insulation blankets (water repelling characteristics are diminished). • Areas with electrical arc potential. • Interior materials, including cargo liners (change of flammability properties). • Engine strut cavities, cowling panels or pod. • APU or any structure in direct contact with the APU. • Fiber-glass ducts where temperature exceeds 220 degrees F . • Fuel tank wet areas. • Selected areas noted in baseline program. SUBTASK 51-05-01-210-028 (7) CPCP Basic T ask Item 7 is not applicable.

Use Additional non-destructive inspections or visual inspections following partial disassembly if there are indications of hidden corrosion, such as bulging skins or corrosion running into splices, or under fittings, etc. In the task area, check the integrity of any sealant/leveling compound to determine if removal is required, and any corrosion inhibiting compound, particularly at faying surfaces, to determine if additional application is required per CPCP Basic T ask Item 6. SUBTASK 51-05-01-210-126 (1) Do the CPCP Basic T ask Item 1 as follows: (a) Remove all systems, equipment and interior furnishings, etc. (e.g. toilets, galleys, linings, installation) as necessary to accomplish CPCP Basic T ask Item 3. It is not necessary to remove bushings unless specified in the T ask Description, or if there is an indication of corrosion, or that the bushing has migrated. SUBTASK 51-05-01-210-127 (2) Do the CPCP Basic T ask Item 2 as follows: (a) Prior to inspection clean the area as required to accomplish CPCP Basic T ask Item 3. It is not necessary to remove normal amounts of sealant/leveling compound unless it has deteriorated to the point where moisture can penetrate down to the metal. A light uniform film of Corrosion Inhibiting Compound (CIC) that has not accumulated dirt or debris, will normally allow adequate inspection of the structure without removal. CIC may require removal if there are multiple layers and/or accumulations of dirt or debris. SUBTASK 51-05-01-210-128 (3) Do the CPCP Basic T ask Item 3 as follows: (a) Visually inspect all structure listed in the task description. The inspection method is as specified in each task description. Use Additional non-destructive inspections or visual inspections following partial disassembly if there are indications of hidden corrosion, such as bulging skins or corrosion running into splices, or under fittings, etc. In the task area, check the integrity of any sealant/leveling compound to determine if removal is required, and any corrosion inhibiting compound, particularly at faying surfaces, to determine if additional application is required per CPCP Basic T ask Item 6. SUBTASK 51-05-01-210-129 (4) Do the CPCP Basic T ask item 4 as follows: (a) Remove all corrosion, evaluate damage and repair or replace all discrepant structure as required, including application of protective finishes per STANDARD TREATMENT METHODS, AMM SUBJECT 51-00-58, or 737 Structural Repair Manual (SRM) D634A200, (-600), D634A201 (-700), D634A210 (-800), D634A211(-900), D634A333 (BBJ), or related service bulletin, as appropriate. Surface oxidation of ferrous metal fasteners may be handled by normal or existing maintenance practices. SUBTASK 51-05-01-210-130 (5) CPCP Basic T ask Item 5 is not applicable. SUBTASK 51-05-01-210-131 (6) Do the CPCP Basic T ask item 6 as follows: (a) Apply suitable approved water displacing / anti-corrosion compound as necessary. 1) The minimum requirement for all areas (except as noted in CPCP Basic T ask 6 (a) 3)) is single coat of water displacing / anti-corrosion compound that penetrates faying surfaces and displaces moisture, e.g. a single coat of compound, C00915 BMS 3-29 or corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 BMS 3-23, where the initial or previous coat has been disturbed or removed. 2) Not applicable 3) List of areas / items where water displacing/anti-corrosion compounds should not be applied: 51-05-01 Water displacing / anti-corrosion compounds should not be applied in the following areas: • Cables, pulleys, wiring, plastics, elastomers, oxygen systems. • Lubricated or T eflon surfaces (E.g. greased joints, sealed bearings). • Over compound, C00174 Cosmoline 1058 (or Equivalent per MIL-C-16173 Grade 1). • Adjacent to tears / holes in insulation blankets (water repelling characteristics are diminished). • Areas with electrical arc potential. • Interior materials, including cargo liners (change of flammability properties). • Engine strut cavities, cowling panels or pod. • APU or any structure in direct contact with the APU. • Fiber-glass ducts where temperature exceeds 220 degrees F . • Fuel tank wet areas. • Selected areas noted in baseline program. SUBTASK 51-05-01-210-132 (7) CPCP Basic T ask Item 7 is not applicable.

C. Prepare the surface

SUBTASK 51-21-00-100-001 (1) Before you apply finish to a surface, you must correctly prepare the surface, as follows: CAUTION DO NOT USE PAINT STRIPPER ON COMPOSITE MATERIALS. IF YOU USE PAINT STRIPPERS ON COMPOSITE MATERIALS, THE COMPOSITE MATERIALS WILL BE STRUCTURALLY DAMAGED. (a) To remove the damaged finish, do this task: Paint Stripping, TASK 51-21-11-150-801. 51-21-00 1) Use approved compounds to remove the damaged finishes. a) Solvents are used to remove paint from small areas. b) Stripping Compounds are used to remove paint from large areas or disassembled parts. c) Mechanical Strippers are used to remove paint from composite materials. (b) To remove the corrosion, do one of the following tasks: 1) for Aluminum and Aluminum Alloys, do this task: Removal and Control of Corrosion for Aluminum and Aluminum Alloys, TASK 51-21-31-350-801. 2) for Magnesium Alloys, do this task: Removal and Control of Corrosion for Magnesium Alloys, TASK 51-21-31-350-802. 3) for Carbon Steel, do this task: Removal and Control of Corrosion for Carbon Steel, TASK 51-21-31-350-803. 4) for Stainless Steel and Nickel-Chromium Alloys, do this task: Removal and Control of Corrosion for Stainless Steel and Nickel-Chromium Alloys, TASK 51-21-31-350-804. 5) for Titanium Alloys, do this task: Removal and Control of Corrosion for Titanium Alloys, TASK 51-21-31-350-805. 6) for Plated or Phosphated Surfaces, do this task: Removal and Control of Corrosion for Plated or Phosphated Surfaces, TASK 51-21-31-350-806. 7) Listed below are more than one approved method of corrosion removal: a) chemical treatments b) hand sanding with abrasive paper or metal wool c) mechanical sanding with abrasive mats d) dry abrasive blasting. 8) The procedures you use must agree with the type of material and the quantity of the corrosion. (c) Clean the surface with one or more of these approved methods: NOTE: To get satisfactory results, you must make sure the surface is fully clean before you apply paints or finishes. 1) Use solvent, B00184, or 2) Use cleaner, B00402, or NOTE: The following cleaners are optional to cleaner, B00402: Cee Bee 280 cleaner, B00005, Oakite 204 cleaner, B00008 and Calla 301A cleaner, B00015. 51-21-00 CAUTION BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU USE ABRADING MATERIAL. ABRADING MATERIAL CAN EXPOSE OR DAMAGE FIBERGLASS, ARAMID, OR GRAPHITE FIBERS. DAMAGED OR EXPOSED FIBERS WILL CAUSE THE COMPONENT TO BE REJECTED. 3) Use 150 grit or finer abrasive, G02088 by hand. NOTE: You can also do dry abrasive blasting with abrasive, G02222 if necessary. NOTE: For composites, the recommended abrasive is No. 240 Scotch-Brite. Use of alternative media blasting procedures for finish removal is structurally satisfactory. The procedure must agree with the requirements given in D6–55564, “Requirements for Alternative Paint Stripping Processes” or SAE MA4872 “Paint Stripping of Commercial Aircraft - Evaluation of Materials and Processes.” Refer to SOPM 20–30–02, or BAC5725 “Stripping Organic Materials” for more information on paint stripping with blast media. 4) Scrub the area thoroughly with a slurry of pumice abrasive, B00166 powder 4F and water. (d) Apply a conversion coating (on some surfaces). 1) Some conversion coatings are applied to make a protective layer on metal surfaces to prevent damage. 2) The layer is formed by a chemical procedure which will change the surface metal into an oxide layer. 3) Different conversion coating applications are used with different metals. 4) Chromic acid or an equivalent oxidizing agent will make a thin tight layer and prevent corrosion. SUBTASK 51-21-00-380-001 (2) To apply flame-sprayed aluminum, (SRM 51-70-14).

B. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-21-00-210-003 (1) Examine the condition of the aluminum surface: (a) Make sure that all areas that are to be electrically bonded are clean. (b) Remove oil, grease, dirt, and paint from the surface. (c) Make sure you remove all corrosion material from the surfaces or parts, if necessary. 1) Failure to remove all corrosion material can permit corrosion to start again. 2) For limits of corrosion removal, refer to the Structural Repair Manual. SUBTASK 51-21-00-160-004 (2) Do the abrasive cleaning for the aluminum surface as follows: (a) Select and use one of the abrasive materials that follow: 1) abrasive mat, G00251. 2) abrasive cloth, B00102. 3) 240 grit or finer abrasive paper, G50077. (b) Sand the surface with the abrasive in a circular motion. 1) Sand the surface until all surface finishes are removed. 2) Sand the surface until a bright aluminum bonding surface is visible throughout the required area. SUBTASK 51-21-00-160-005 (3) Do the final solvent cleaning for the aluminum bonding surface as follows: (a) Select one of the solvents that follow: 1) alcohol, B00067 2) solvent, B00148. 3) solvent, B00062 4) solvent, B00666. 5) solvent, B00184. 6) alcohol, B00130 7) solvent, B01054 8) solvent, B50085 (b) Add the solvent to a cotton wiper, G00034. (c) Rub surface to be cleaned with the solvent soaked wiper. 1) Replace the dirty wiper for a clean one if necessary. 51-21-00 (d) Immediately wipe dry with a clean, dry wiper. 1) Do not allow solvent to evaporate to dryness. NOTE: It may be necessary to remove residue with a second dry wipe when using slow-evaporating solvents. (e) Do the steps again until the wiper shows no soil.

51-21-11-370-801Prepare for Paint StrippingPDF p. 123

2. Prepare for Paint Stripping

A. General

(1) The purpose of alkaline cleaning is to prepare the painted surfaces of the aircraft for paint stripping. Paint strippers can be more effective if the aircraft surface is cleaned prior to paint stripping. 51-21-11 CAUTION DO NOT USE RESTRICTED-USE PAINT STRIPPERS ON HIGH-STRENGTH STEEL, OR MAGNESIUM COMPONENTS. THESE STRIPPERS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO COMPONENTS WITH THESE MATERIALS. (2) Restricted-use paint strippers are for removing organic finishes from metallic substrates but cannot be used on high-strength steel or magnesium.

(51 mm) wide. 2) Use a hand series squeegee applicator, STD-10211, to make sure the tape adheres to the surface. 3) Make sure the aluminum tape completely covers the masking tape. NOTE: This is to protect it from chemical paint strippers. a) Extend the aluminum tape over the masking tape to protect it from chemical paint strippers. SUBTASK 51-21-11-950-008 (11) Mask the lights and light bases listed below using the steps that follow: (a) Directional and warning fuselage lights. (b) Logo illumination lights. (c) Cover the lights and light bases with Scotch 427 Aluminum Foil T ape, G50737, or 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. 1) Use a hand series squeegee applicator, STD-10211, to make sure the tape adheres to the surface. (d) If the light is larger than the width of the aluminum foil tape, do the steps that follow: 1) Cover the surface with polyethylene film. a) Make sure that the polyethylene film is 4.0 mils (0.1 mm) to 7.0 mils (0.2 mm) thick and fire retardant. 2) Use Scotch 427 Aluminum Foil T ape, G50737, or 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291, to attach the film to the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-096 (12) Do the steps that follow to clean the area: (a) Remove the loose dirt, grease, and oil with MIL-PRF-680 degreasing solvent, B00074, or aliphatic naphtha solvent, B00083. NOTE: Be careful to not put solvent on a larger area than is necessary. (b) Clean the surface with a cotton wiper, G00034, paint brush, STD-1080, or a sponge, G00116, that is moist with MIL-PRF-680 degreasing solvent, B00074, or aliphatic naphtha solvent, B00083. 1) Rub the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034. (c) Remove all unwanted solvent. (d) Let the surface dry. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-097 (13) Do the steps that follow to clean the surface again: (a) Use a spray bottle to apply the aliphatic naphtha solvent, B00083, on the surface. (b) Clean the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, until you remove all large pieces of soil. 1) Use a soft bristle brush, G00215, to clean the surface, if necessary. (c) Clean the surface again with a new cotton wiper, G00034, until you can see no signs of soil on the cheesecloth. NOTE: It will be necessary to change the cheesecloth frequently when you clean the surface. 51-21-11 (d) Dry the area with a clean cotton wiper, G00034. 1) Make sure that you do not let drops of solvent dry on the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-11-580-002 (14) Dry the aircraft. (a) If the actuator components or bearings were cleaned, lubricate those components as necessary. 1) Make sure to lubricate the actuator components or bearings outside the paint hangar. NOTE: This is to avoid paint contamination.

51-21-11-150-801Paint StrippingPDF p. 134

3. Paint Stripping

A. General

(1) This task has the following steps: (a) Brush-on or paint-on paint stripping (b) A removal of the epoxy adhesives and adhesive primers (c) A removal of the rain erosion coating from fiberglass (d) Selection of paint strippers. CAUTION DO NOT LET PAINT STRIPPERS TOUCH FIBREGLASS, ACRYLIC WINDOWS, SEALANT FILLETS, TEFLON LINED SELF-LUBRICATED BEARINGS, ELECTRICAL TERMINAL PLUGS, NYLON COATED WIRES AND NYLON BUSHINGS. THE CHEMICAL COMPOUNDS IN THE PAINT STRIPPERS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE COMPONENTS. (2) Before you clean, you must protect the surfaces and parts which are easily damaged by paint strippers. (a) Make sure that the paint strippers do not fall on the joints. (b) Do not use paint strippers in the fuel tanks. (3) Before you remove the paint with the stripping procedure, make sure that the surface is clean and dry. (a) Make sure that the ambient temperature is between 50°F (10°C) and 100°F (38°C). 1) Do not use the stripping procedure in hot or wet weather. (b) Make sure that the paint stripping equipment are fully clean of chemical residue. NOTE: Refer to equipment manufacturer's instructions to clean paint stripping equipment. CAUTION DO NOT USE PAINT STRIPPER ON COMPOSITE MATERIALS. PAINT STRIPPERS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE STRUCTURE OF THE PART . (4) Brush-on or spray-on stripping methods with paint strippers or solvents can be used on metal surfaces. (a) You can use a pressure sprayer gun, STD-447, or a brush to apply the paint strippers. 1) The brush-on procedure is frequently used for line maintenance. CAUTION DO NOT USE THE SAME PUMPS AND HOSES WHEN MIXING DRUMS OF DIFFERENT PAINT STRIPPERS THROUGH RECIRCULATION. MIXING AND CROSS-CONTAMINATION CAN BE HIGHLY CORROSIVE TO METAL SURFACES. THIS CAN CAUSE SKIN PITTING DAMAGE. (b) Make sure that the components in the paint stripper are fully mixed. 1) Do not use the same pumps and hoses when drums of different paint strippers are mixed through recirculation. a) Use dedicated pump and hose for different paint stripper type when drums of paint striper are mixed through recirculation. 51-21-11 2) Keep the container of paint stripper fully closed when it is not being used. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY ACID-ACTIVATED STRIPPER ONTO ANY AIRPLANE SURFACE THAT HAS NOT HAD THE PEROXIDE-ACTIVATED STRIPPER COMPLETELY AND THOROUGHLY RINSED OFF WITH WATER AND VICE-VERSA. IF YOU MIX AND CROSS-CONTAMINATE, IT CAN BE HIGHLY CORROSIVE TO METAL SURFACES. THIS CAN CAUSE SKIN PITTING DAMAGE. (c) Do not mix strippers of different manufacturers. 1) Make sure that airplane is completely and thoroughly rinsed down with water to remove all residue of the initial paint stripper when using different paint stripper. 2) Do not apply acid-activated stripper onto any airplane surface that has not had the peroxide-activated stripper completely and thoroughly rinsed off with water and vise-versa. NOTE: If necessary, a mild alkaline cleaner solution can be used to neutralize the hydrogen-peroxide paint based stripper. You can use Super Bee 300LF cleaner, B50394 [CP2615] or other equivalent cleaners approved for aircraft exteriors to remove paint and stripper residue. (d) Strippers that you apply with a brush or with a spray gun contain agents that make a solution thick. 1) Apply these strippers on the vertical and horizontal surfaces. (e) Strippers that you apply with a cloth are used to remove temporary finishes, waxes, and oversprays. (f) specifications BAC5725 and BAC5771 provide procedures for paint stripping. (g) Restricted strippers are not compatible with high-strength steel and magnesium. When you use restricted strippers, make sure that all high-strength steel and magnesium parts are masked. (h) Acid strippers will discolor clad aluminum. (i) You can usually use a solvent to remove small quantities of paint. (j) Do not use paint strippers on the surfaces that follow: NOTE: Only use approved solvents on these materials. 1) Plastic laminates 2) Fiberglass 3) Aerodynamic smoother 4) Edges of metal bonds 5) Rubber parts 6) Lubricated parts 7) Composite surfaces or parts. (5) Abrasive stripping methods can be used on the surfaces that follow: (a) Ferrous Alloys (b) Titanium (c) Titanium Alloys (d) Titanium-Cadmium 51-21-11 (e) Nickel (f) Nickel Alloys (g) Magnesium Alloys (h) Magnesium (i) Aluminum Alloys (j) Cadmium (k) Zinc-Nickel (l) Chromium (m) Copper-Plating (n) Composite Parts.

D. Brush-on or Spray Paint Stripping

SUBTASK 51-21-11-150-022 (1) Prepare the surface for the paint stripping, do this task: Prepare for Paint Stripping, TASK 51-21-11-370-801. NOTE: The purpose of alkaline cleaning is to prepare the painted surfaces of the aircraft for paint stripping. Washing the aircraft may mitigate interactions between chemical strippers and enviormental contaminants such as salt. Paint strippers will be more effective if the aircraft surface is cleaned prior to paint stripping. SUBTASK 51-21-11-150-001 WARNING MANY ORGANIC FINISH STRIPPERS ARE FLAMMABLE, TOXIC OR CORROSIVE. REVIEW THE RELEVANT FIRE, INDUSTRIAL, HYGIENE, AND SAFETY PROCEDURES FOR SAFE OPERATION. AVOID PROLONGED OR REPEATED BREATHING OF THE STRIPPER AND SOLVENT VAPORS. WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND GOGGLES OR PLASTIC FACE SHIELDS. AVOID CONTACT WITH SKIN AND EYES. WASH IMMEDIATELY WITH WATER AND SEEK MEDICAL ATTENTION. (2) Do the paint stripping. NOTE: Strip only an area that can be worked at one time. (a) Refer to Table 701 for the approved stripping materials. (b) Make sure that you double-strip windows. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY ACID-ACTIVATED STRIPPER ONTO ANY AIRPLANE SURFACE THAT HAS NOT HAD THE PEROXIDE-ACTIVATED STRIPPER COMPLETELY AND THOROUGHLY RINSED OFF WITH WATER AND VICE-VERSA. IF YOU MIX AND CROSS-CONTAMINATE, IT CAN BE HIGHLY CORROSIVE TO METAL SURFACES. THIS CAN CAUSE SKIN PITTING DAMAGE. (c) Fully mix the strippers. NOTE: Refer to the manufacturer's instructions to mix the paint stripper. 1) Make sure that airplane is completely and thoroughly rinsed down with water to remove all residue of the initial paint stripper when using a different paint stripper. 2) Do not apply acid-activated stripper onto any airplane surface that has not had the peroxide-activated stripper completely and thoroughly rinsed off with water and vise-versa. NOTE: If necessary, a mild alkaline cleaner solution can be used to neutralize the hydrogen-peroxide paint based stripper. You can use Super Bee 300LF cleaner, B50394 [CP2615] or other equivalent cleaners approved for aircraft exteriors to remove paint and stripper residue. (d) Apply large quantities of the stripper on the paint. NOTE: Keep the surface wet with the stripper. 1) Put the stripper on with a natural bristle paint brush, STD-1080, or a non-atomizing spray. 2) If it is necessary, add more layers of the stripper. (e) Let the stripper stay on the surface a sufficient time for the finish to become soft and become wrinkled. 51-21-11 CAUTION DO NOT USE ABRASIVE PADS (SCOTCH-BRITE), OR ABRASIVE PAPER ON THE ALUMINUM SURFACE UNLESS THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS WERE MADE. ABRASIVE PADS CAN SMOOTH THE ALUMINUM SURFACE AND HIDE THE SCRIBE LINE MARKS. IF YOU USE ABRASIVE PADS TO REMOVE THE PAINT OR PRIMER BEFORE YOU DO THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS, YOU CAN BE REQUIRED TO DO REPEAT INSPECTIONS BASED ON THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTION SERVICE BULLETIN. CAUTION ONLY USE APPROVED SCRAPERS ON THE AIRPLANE SKIN. SCRAPERS THAT ARE NOT APPROVED CAN MAKE SCRATCHES ON THE SKIN, AND CAUSE FATIGUE CRACKS. (f) Remove the loosened material with a bristle paint brush, STD-1080, or with a sealant removal tool, COM-2481, with sealant removal tool handle, COM-4746, before the stripper becomes dry. NOTE: If you use abrasive pads before you do scribe line inspections, you can be required to do repeat inspections based on the scribe line inspection Service Bulletin 737-53A1289. (g) If it is necessary, apply the stripper again to remove all unwanted adhesive or the primer. (h) Rinse the surface with sponge, G00116, that is soaked with clean water. WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH, YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS ARE DANGEROUS MATERIALS. SOLVENTS CAN BE FLAMMABLE. OBEY THE MATERIAL SAFETY DATA SHEETS (MSDS) FOR SOLVENTS. OBEY LOCAL REGULATIONS FOR THE CORRECT PROCEDURES TO USE OR DISCARD SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . 1) As an alternative to water, you can use Series 84 solvent, B01004, to clean the surface. (i) Dry the surface with cotton wiper, G00034. 1) Make sure that the surface is fully dry.

E. Remove the Epoxy Adhesives and Adhesive Primers

SUBTASK 51-21-11-150-023 (1) Prepare the surface for paint striping, do this task: Prepare for Paint Stripping, TASK 51-21-11-370-801. SUBTASK 51-21-11-150-002 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU REFER TO THE MANUFACTURER'S INSTRUCTIONS WHEN YOU APPLY THE STRIPPER THE SURFACE. IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW THE MANUFACTURER'S INSTRUCTIONS, DAMAGE CAN OCCUR TO THE SURFACE. 51-21-11 (CAUTION PRECEDES) CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE STRIPPER DOES NOT TOUCH THE SURFACE FOR MORE THAN 2 HOURS. DAMAGE TO THE SURFACE CAN OCCUR IF THE STRIPPER TOUCHES THE SURFACE FOR A LONG TIME. (2) Do the epoxy adhesive and adhesive primer stripping. (a) Refer to Table 701 for the approved stripping materials. (b) Fully mix the strippers. NOTE: Refer to the manufacturer's instructions to mix the adhesive stripper. (c) Apply a small quantity of stripper on the adhesive or the primer with a paint brush, STD-1080. 1) Make sure to keep the surface wet with stripper. 2) Let the stripper absorb the adhesive or the primer for not more than 30 minutes. 3) Make sure that the stripper does not touch or fall on aluminum surfaces. CAUTION DO NOT USE ABRASIVE PADS (SCOTCH-BRITE), OR ABRASIVE PAPER ON THE ALUMINUM SURFACE UNLESS THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS WERE MADE. ABRASIVE PADS CAN SMOOTH THE ALUMINUM SURFACE AND HIDE THE SCRIBE LINE MARKS. IF YOU USE ABRASIVE PADS TO REMOVE THE PAINT OR PRIMER BEFORE YOU DO THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS, YOU CAN BE REQUIRED TO DO REPEAT INSPECTIONS BASED ON THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTION SERVICE BULLETIN. CAUTION ONLY USE APPROVED SCRAPERS ON THE AIRPLANE SKIN. SCRAPERS THAT ARE NOT APPROVED CAN MAKE SCRATCHES ON THE SKIN, AND CAUSE FATIGUE CRACKS. (d) Remove the stripper and loosened adhesive, or the primer with cotton wiper, G00034, or a sealant removal tool, COM-2481, with sealant removal tool handle, COM-4746. NOTE: If you use abrasive pads before you do scribe line inspections, you can be required to do repeat inspections based on the scribe line inspection Service Bulletin 737-53A1289. (e) If it is necessary, apply the stripper again to remove all unwanted adhesive or the primer. (f) Rinse the surface with sponge, G00116, that is soaked with clean water. WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH, YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS ARE DANGEROUS MATERIALS. SOLVENTS CAN BE FLAMMABLE. OBEY THE MATERIAL SAFETY DATA SHEETS (MSDS) FOR SOLVENTS. OBEY LOCAL REGULATIONS FOR THE CORRECT PROCEDURES TO USE OR DISCARD SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . 1) As an alternative to water, you can use Series 84 solvent, B01004, to clean the surface. (g) Dry the surface fully with a clean dry cotton wiper, G00034. 51-21-11 F . Remove the Rain Erosion Coating from Fiberglass SUBTASK 51-21-11-150-024 (1) Prepare the surface for the paint stripping, do this task: Prepare for Paint Stripping, TASK 51-21-11-370-801. SUBTASK 51-21-11-150-005 (2) Do the stripping to remove the rain erosion coating. WARNING TOLUENE THINNER IS AN AGENT THAT IS FLAMMABLE, EXPLOSIVE, POISONOUS, AND AN IRRITANT . MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS OBEY ALL OF THE PRECAUTIONS WHEN TOLUENE THINNER IS USED. • GAS/AIR MIXTURES MORE THAN THE LOWER EXPLOSIVE LIMIT (LEL) CAN CAUSE AN EXPLOSION IF HIGH HEAT , SPARKS, OR FLAMES SUPPLY IGNITION. • USE IN AN AREA OPEN TO THE AIR. • CLOSE THE CONTAINER WHEN NOT USED. • DO NOT GET TOLUENE THINNER IN THE EYES, ON THE SKIN, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. • DO NOT BREATHE THE GAS. (a) Make sure that you put on the following protection before using toluene solvent, B00094: 1) Protective splash goggles 2) Gloves. (b) Put clean cloths that are moist with toluene solvent, B00094, on the rain erosion coating. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE TOLUENE DOES NOT STAY ON THE FIBERGLASS FOR MORE THAN 2 HOURS. DAMAGE TO THE SURFACE CAN OCCUR IF THE STRIPPER STAYS ON THE SURFACE FOR MORE THAN 2 HOURS. (c) If it is necessary, add more toluene solvent, B00094, to keep the cloths moist. 1) Permit sufficient time to loosen the coating from the fiberglass (20 minutes to 1 hour). a) Make sure that the toluene does not stay on the fiberglass surface for more than 2 hours. CAUTION DO NOT USE ABRASIVE PADS (SCOTCH-BRITE), OR ABRASIVE PAPER ON THE ALUMINUM SURFACE UNLESS THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS WERE MADE. ABRASIVE PADS CAN SMOOTH THE ALUMINUM SURFACE AND HIDE THE SCRIBE LINE MARKS. IF YOU USE ABRASIVE PADS TO REMOVE THE PAINT OR PRIMER BEFORE YOU DO THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS, YOU CAN BE REQUIRED TO DO REPEAT INSPECTIONS BASED ON THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTION SERVICE BULLETIN. 51-21-11 (CAUTION PRECEDES) CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU ONLY USE APPROVED SCRAPERS ON THE AIRPLANE SKIN. SCRAPERS THAT ARE NOT APPROVED CAN MAKE SCRATCHES ON THE SKIN AND CAUSE FATIGUE CRACKS. (d) Remove the loosened rain erosion coating with a bristle brush, STD-133, or a sealant removal tool, COM-2481, with sealant removal tool handle, COM-4746, before toluene solvent, B00094, dries. NOTE: If you use abrasive pads before you do scribe line inspections, you can be required to do repeat inspections based on the scribe line inspection Service Bulletin 737-53A1289. (e) Lightly abrade (sand) the surface with abrasive cloth, B00102, or 240 grit (minimum) abrasive paper. (f) Clean the area with xylene solvent, B00344. (g) Dry the surface fully with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034.

(0.305 mm) thick and greater All other metals, including plated surfaces Composite parts EnviroStrip 12/30 wheat starch media, E50010 Nanocomposite Blasting *[6] Aluminum alloys with a gage thickness of 0.040 in. (1.016 mm) or greater Bonded aluminum honeycomb sandwich parts with facesheets 0.012 in. (0.305 mm)thick or greater Ferrous alloys Titanium and Titanium alloys Titanium-Cadmium, cadmium, nickel, zinc-nickel, chromium, and copper-plated parts Chemically treated or anodized magnesium Magic 1 Nanocomposite Abrasive Media *[7], Magic 2 Nanocomposite Abrasive Media *[7], Magic 3 Nanocomposite Abrasive Media *[7] 51-21-11 Table 701/51-21-11-993-801 SELECTION OF STRIPPERS (Continued) ORGANIC MATERIAL TO BE REMOVED SUBSTRATE MATERIAL APPROVED STRIPPER *[1] APPROVED RESTRICTED USE STRIPPER *[1] OPERATING TEMPERATURE Bonding adhesives, adhesive primers for bonding Aluminum Titanium All Stainless Steels BONDERITE S-ST 5351 AERO stripper (methylene chloride), E00002 - Thick (T .O. 1-1-8) Recommended: 65°F (18°C) to 80°F (27°C) Alternative: 50°F (10°C) to 100°F (38°C) ES-1 Stripper (methylene chloride), E50027 *[8] 50°F (10°C) to 80°F (27°C) *[1] Mixing or cross-contamination of acid-activated strippers with hydrogen peroxide-activated strippers can be highly corrosive to metal surfaces. Before applying any paint strippers, special attention must be taken to: 1) Thoroughly clean paint stripping equipment (spray guns, pots, pumps, pressure hoses, etc.) of any chemical residue from prior usage per equipment manufacturer’s instructions. It is recommended to recirculate water through the pump, hose, and spray gun at least 5X the volume of the hose and pump. After recirculation, check the pH of the rinsate to verify it is the same pH as the water source. Scrub clean inner diameter of pump/hose/gun from any material buildup and thoroughly clean outer diameter of spray gun. Clean squeegees and all tools contacting airplane surface. 2) Ensure stripper is homogeneous by agitating material for a minimum of 30 minutes** (e.g with a drum roller or recirculating material with cleaned pump/hose/gun). **this depends on if using a 55-gallon drum or a large tote. 3) If one type of paint stripper (e.g. peroxide-activated) is used on an aircraft and it is determined that a different type of stripper is required (e.g. acid-activated), then the aircraft must be completely and thoroughly rinsed down with water to remove all residue of the initial paint stripper. Do not apply acid-activated stripper onto any aircraft surface that has not had the peroxide-activated stripper completely and thoroughly rinsed off with water. *[2] Do not allow these peroxide-based strippers to come in contact directly with unpainted steel alloys. A thin layer of these paint strippers can cause corrosion. In using these strippers, expose paint chips and spent strippers to a fine spray of soap during clean-up after stripping, or rinse paint chips with water to remove paint stripper prior to packaging in vented containers before disposal. Dispense the stripper through plastic or stainless steel equipment. Collecting wastes in rusty drums, mixing conversion coating rinse water with stripper residues, or throwing rags, gloves, or other fabrics into the waste drum may cause combustion. Used material contaminated with paint flakes and organic materials may undergo spontaneous pressurization. The paint stripper produces water and oxygen during the paint removal process. This process will continue after the stripper is removed from the aircraft. To prevent pressure from building up in waste containers, do not cap containers for 24 hours after collecting the stripper residue and paint chips. *[3] Do not use this stripper on polysulfides. An example of a polysulfide is sealants. *[4] Not for use on high-strength steel or magnesium parts. Make sure that all high-strength steel and magnesium parts are masked. Restricted-used strippers are not compatible with high-strength steel and magnesium. Restricted-used strippers are not allowed on inspar wing surfaces. Restricted-used strippers will discolor clad aluminum. *[5] Maximum of five paint stripping cycles are allowed during the life of the airplane. *[6] Maximum of four paint stripping cycles are allowed during the life of the airplane. *[7] Complete removal of organic materials by abrasive methods damages conversion coatings and may remove plating. Strip conversion coatings and re-finish. Inspect plating (except chrome) for compliance with requirements and supplementary chromate treatment requirements and re-finish as required. *[8] This solution damages plating and conversion coating (for example, chemical conversion coating and anodized). Rinse as soon as possible after stripping to stop etching. Plating and conversion coating exposed to the stripper shall be stripped and refinished.

51-21-11-150-802Ferrous Alloys - Paint StrippingPDF p. 148

4. Ferrous Alloys - Paint Stripping

A. General

(1) This task gives paint stripping instructions using the abrasive stripping methods that follow: (a) Conventional Abrasive Blasting Method (b) Plastic Media Blasting Method (c) Wheat Starch Blasting Method (d) Nanocomposite Blasting Method. (2) For metal surfaces, you can remove paint by abrasive stripping, or by brush-on or paint-on with paint strippers or solvents. For procedures to remove paint with paint strippers or solvents, see Paint Stripping, TASK 51-21-11-150-801. (3) Make sure that the areas that follow are covered: (a) Lubricated parts (b) Rubber parts (c) Laminated plastic surfaces or parts (d) Fiberglass surfaces or parts (e) Aerodynamic smoothers (f) Metal bonded parts (g) Composite parts (h) Adjacent access doors, fairings, and wing Leading Edge (LE)s and Trailing Edge (TE)s (i) All areas adjacent to the area being stripped (j) Drain holes and vents (k) Pitot static probes and ports (l) Angle of Attack (AOA) vanes (m) Cargo door and entry door hinges and thresholds (n) Cooling air exhaust duct (o) Tires (p) Ram air inlets (q) Engines and the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) inlets and exhausts (r) Pressurized drain valves (s) Joints. (4) Make sure that the ambient temperature is between 50°F (10°C) and 100°F (38°C). NOTE: Do not use the stripping procedure in hot or wet weather.

B. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification B50268 Solvent - General Cleaning of Metals (AMM 20-30-80) - Series 80 E50010 Media - EnviroStrip 12/30 Wheat Starch Media E50011 Media - Plastic Media For Removal Of Organic Coatings (20/30 Mesh) MIL-P-85891 51-21-11 (Continued) Reference Description Specification E50012 Media - Magic II 30/60 Composite Blast Media (Type VIII) MIL-P-85891 G00034 Cotton Wiper - Process Cleaning Absorbent Wiper (Cheesecloth, Gauze) AMS3819 Class 1 Grade A or B Form 1 (Supersede BMS15-5 CL A) G00215 Brush - Soft Bristle Fiber G50822 Abrasive - Walnut Shells A-A-1722 Type II G50823 Abrasive - Apricot Pit Shells A-A-1722 Type I

C. Prepare to Strip the Surface

SUBTASK 51-21-11-150-007 (1) Prepare to strip the surface, do this task: Prepare for Paint Stripping, TASK 51-21-11-370-801. SUBTASK 51-21-11-110-003 (2) Clean the surface. (a) Remove loose soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, oil, and metal shavings using a cotton wiper, G00034. 1) Use an oil absorbing wiper to remove oil, if necessary. (b) Clean the surface with a cotton wiper, G00034, or brush, G00215, wet with a Series 80 solvent, B50268. (c) Immediately wipe the solvent from the surface using a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. 1) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. (d) Clean the surface again until the surface is free from all soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, oil, and metal shavings.

D. Paint Stripping - Conventional Abrasive Blasting Method

SUBTASK 51-21-11-950-011 (1) Make sure that the areas that will not be stripped are masked. SUBTASK 51-21-11-110-004 (2) Make sure that the areas that will be stripped are clean and dry. SUBTASK 51-21-11-120-001 (3) Abrasive blast the area to be stripped with apricot pit shell abrasive, G50823, or walnut shells abrasive, G50822. (a) Make sure that the nozzle air pressure is 90 psig (621 kPa) to 100 psig (689 kPa). (b) Make sure that the nozzle is approximately 6 in. (152 mm) from the surface. (c) Abrade the surface equally down to the primer surface. NOTE: It is not necessary to remove the primers for the reapplication of primer, enamels, or topcoat. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-002 (4) Clean the surface using clean, compressed air.

E. Paint Stripping - Plastic Media Blasting Method

SUBTASK 51-21-11-950-012 (1) Make sure that the areas that will not be stripped are masked. 51-21-11 SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-003 (2) Make sure that the areas that will be stripped are clean and dry. SUBTASK 51-21-11-120-002 (3) Plastic media blast using plastic media, E50011, Type V, Grade A, to strip the paint. (a) Screen the plastic media, E50011, to remove undersized media and contaminants. NOTE: Examples of contaminants are paint flakes, metallic particles, and degraded media. (b) Make sure that the nozzle air pressure is 20 psig (138 kPa) to 40 psig (276 kPa). (c) Make sure that the nozzle is approximately 6 in. (152 mm) or more away from the surface. (d) Make sure that the angle of the nozzle is at 45° to the surface. (e) Abrade the surface equally down to the primer surface. NOTE: It is not necessary to remove the primers for the reapplication of primer, enamels, or topcoat. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-004 (4) Clean the surface. (a) Rinse the surface with water. (b) Dry the surface with a clean, cotton wiper, G00034. F . Paint Stripping - Wheat Starch Blasting Method SUBTASK 51-21-11-950-013 (1) Make sure that the areas that will not be stripped are masked. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-005 (2) Make sure that the areas that will be stripped are clean and dry. SUBTASK 51-21-11-120-003 (3) Strip the surface using EnviroStrip 12/30 wheat starch media, E50010. NOTE: Complete removal of organic coatings by wheat starch media blasting can damage surface treatments on the base metal (for example: chemical conversion coating and anodized coating) and may remove plating. (a) Make sure that the nozzle air pressure is between 30 psig (207 kPa) and 50 psig (345 kPa). (b) Make sure that the nozzle is at least 6 in. (152 mm) from the surface. (c) Make sure that the nozzle angle is 20° to 60° from the surface. (d) If the conversion coating was damaged, remove the remaining coating and reapply, as necessary. (e) If the plating was removed, inspect the plating. 1) Make sure that the plating meets the requirements and re-finish, as necessary. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-006 (4) Clean the surface. (a) Rinse the surface with water. (b) Dry the surface with a clean, cotton wiper, G00034. 51-21-11

G. Paint Stripping - Nanocomposite Blasting Method

SUBTASK 51-21-11-950-014 (1) Make sure that the areas that will not be stripped are masked. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-007 (2) Make sure that the areas that will be stripped are clean and dry. SUBTASK 51-21-11-120-004 (3) Strip the surface using one of the nanocomposite abrasives that follow: (a) For general purpose stripping, use Magic 1 Nanocomposite Abrasive Media, 30/60 Mesh. (b) For an increased strip rate, use Magic II Composite Blast Media, E50012. (c) To remove cured sealant, use Magic 3 Nanocomposite Abrasive Media, 10/60 Mesh. (d) Make sure that the nozzle air pressure is less than 32 psig (221 kPa). (e) Make sure that the nozzle is at least 6 in. (152 mm) from the surface. (f) Make sure that the angle of the nozzle is 40° to 60° to the surface. (g) Abrade the surface equally down to the primer surface. NOTE: It is not necessary to remove the primers for the reapplication of primer, enamels, or topcoat. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-008 (4) Clean the surface. (a) Rinse the surface with water. (b) Dry the surface with a clean, cotton wiper, G00034.

SUBTASK 51-21-11-950-022 (1) Make sure that the areas that will not be stripped are masked. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-026 (2) Make sure that the areas that will be stripped are clean and dry. SUBTASK 51-21-11-120-012 (3) Plastic media blast using plastic media, E50011, Type V, Grade A, to strip the paint. (a) Screen the plastic media, E50011, to remove undersized media and contaminants. NOTE: Examples of contaminants are paint flakes, metallic particles, and degraded media. (b) Make sure that the nozzle air pressure is 20 psig (138 kPa) to 40 psig (276 kPa). (c) Make sure that the nozzle is approximately 6 in. (152 mm) or more away from the surface. (d) Make sure that the angle of the nozzle is at 45° to the surface. (e) Abrade the surface equally down to the primer surface. NOTE: It is not necessary to remove the primers for the reapplication of primer, enamels, or topcoat. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-027 (4) Clean the surface. (a) Rinse the surface with water. (b) Dry the surface with a clean, cotton wiper, G00034. 51-21-11

E. Paint Stripping - Wheat Starch Blasting Method

SUBTASK 51-21-11-950-023 (1) Make sure that the areas that will not be stripped are masked. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-028 (2) Make sure that the areas that will be stripped are clean and dry. SUBTASK 51-21-11-120-013 (3) Strip the surface using EnviroStrip 12/30 wheat starch media, E50010. NOTE: Complete removal of organic coatings by wheat starch media blasting can damage surface treatments on the base metal (for example: chemical conversion coating and anodized coating) and may remove plating. (a) Make sure that the nozzle air pressure is between 30 psig (207 kPa) and 50 psig (345 kPa). (b) Make sure that the nozzle is at least 6 in. (152 mm) from the surface. (a) Rinse the surface with water. (b) Dry the surface with a clean, cotton wiper, G00034. F . Paint Stripping - Nanocomposite Blasting Method SUBTASK 51-21-11-950-024 (1) Make sure that the areas that will not be stripped are masked. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-030 (2) Make sure that the areas that will be stripped are clean and dry. SUBTASK 51-21-11-120-014 (3) Strip the surface using one of the nanocomposite abrasives that follow: (a) For general purpose stripping, use Magic 1 Nanocomposite Abrasive Media, 30/60 Mesh. (b) For an increased strip rate, use Magic II Composite Blast Media, E50012. (c) To remove cured sealant, use Magic 3 Nanocomposite Abrasive Media, 10/60 Mesh. (d) Make sure that the nozzle air pressure is less than 32 psig (221 kPa). (e) Make sure that the nozzle is at least 6 in. (152 mm) from the surface. 51-21-11-150-810Aluminum Alloys - Paint StrippingPDF p. 172

12. Aluminum Alloys - Paint Stripping

A. General

(1) This task gives paint stripping instructions using the abrasive stripping methods that follow: (a) Plastic Media Blasting Method 1) This method is applicable to non-clad (bare) aluminum alloys with a gage thickness of 0.125 in. (3.175 mm). (b) Wheat Starch Blasting Method 1) This method is applicable to the following: a) Aluminum alloys with a gage thickness of 0.032 in. (0.813 mm) or greater, including both clad and non-clad (bare) alloys. b) Bonded honeycomb sandwich parts with aluminum facesheets 0.012 in. (0.305 mm) thick or greater. (c) Nanocomposite Blasting Method. 1) This method is applicable to the following: a) Aluminum alloys with a gage thickness of 0.040 in. (1.016 mm) or greater. b) Bonded honeycomb sandwich parts with aluminum facesheets 0.012 in. (0.305 mm) thick or greater. (2) For metal surfaces, you can remove paint by abrasive stripping, or by brush-on or paint-on with paint strippers or solvents. For procedures to remove paint, with paint strippers or solvents, see Paint Stripping, TASK 51-21-11-150-801. (a) Abrasions and scratches are satisfactory if a fingernail does not catch while pulled across the abrasion or scratch, and the abrasion or scratch is not less than 0.10 in. (0.25 cm) from a lap joint. 1) It is not necessary to do supplemental inspections or to record the location of the damage. (b) If the abrasion or scratch catches the fingernail at the two worst areas, make sure that the clad exists. If the clad exists, it is not required to do additional inspection or to record the location of the damage. (c) If the abrasion or scratch is not satisfactory, then refer to the Structural Repair Manual (SRM) for instruction. (3) Make sure that the areas that follow are covered: (a) Lubricated parts (b) Rubber parts (c) Laminated plastic surfaces or parts (d) Fiberglass surfaces or parts (e) Aerodynamic smoothers (f) Metal bonded parts (g) Composite parts (h) Adjacent access doors, fairings, and wing Leading Edge (LE)s and Trailing Edge (TE)s 51-21-11 (i) All areas adjacent to the area being stripped (j) Drain holes and vents (k) Pitot static probes and ports (l) Angle of Attack (AOA) vanes (m) Cargo door and entry door hinges and thresholds (n) Cooling air exhaust duct (o) Tires (p) Ram air inlets (q) Engines and the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) inlets and exhausts (r) Pressurized drain valves (s) Joints. (4) Make sure that the ambient temperature is between 50°F (10°C) and 100°F (38°C). NOTE: Do not use the stripping procedure in hot or wet weather.

C. Prepare to Strip the Surface

SUBTASK 51-21-11-150-015 (1) Prepare to strip the surface, do this task: Prepare for Paint Stripping, TASK 51-21-11-370-801. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-056 (2) Clean the surface. (a) Remove loose soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, oil, and metal shavings using a cotton wiper, G00034. 1) Use an oil absorbing wiper to remove oil, if necessary. (b) Clean the surface with a cotton wiper, G00034, or brush, G00215, wet with a Series 80 solvent, B50268. (c) Immediately wipe the solvent from the surface using a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. 1) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. (d) Clean the surface again until the surface is free from all soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, oil, and metal shavings. 51-21-11

D. Paint Stripping - Plastic Media Blasting Method

SUBTASK 51-21-11-950-035 (1) Make sure that the areas that will not be stripped are masked. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-057 (2) Make sure that the areas that will be stripped are clean and dry. SUBTASK 51-21-11-120-022 (3) Plastic media blast using plastic media, E50011, Type V, Grade A, to strip the paint. (a) Screen the plastic media, E50011, to remove undersized media and contaminants. NOTE: Examples of contaminants are paint flakes, metallic particles, and degraded media. (b) Make sure that the nozzle air pressure is 20 psig (138 kPa) to 40 psig (276 kPa). (c) Make sure that the nozzle is approximately 6 in. (152 mm) or more away from the surface. (d) Make sure that the angle of the nozzle is at 45° to the surface. (e) Abrade the surface equally down to the primer surface. NOTE: It is not necessary to remove the primers for the reapplication of primer, enamels, or topcoat. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-058 (4) Clean the surface. (a) Rinse the surface with water. (b) Dry the surface with a clean, cotton wiper, G00034.

E. Paint Stripping - Wheat Starch Blasting Method

SUBTASK 51-21-11-950-036 (1) Make sure that the areas that will not be stripped are masked. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-059 (2) Make sure that the areas that will be stripped are clean and dry. SUBTASK 51-21-11-120-023 (3) Strip the surface using EnviroStrip 12/30 wheat starch media, E50010. NOTE: Complete removal of organic coatings by wheat starch media blasting can damage surface treatments on the base metal (for example: chemical conversion coating and anodized coating) and may remove plating. (a) Make sure that the nozzle air pressure is between 30 psig (207 kPa) and 50 psig (345 kPa). (b) Make sure that the nozzle is at least 6 in. (152 mm) from the surface. (c) Make sure that the nozzle angle is 20° to 60° from the surface. (d) If the conversion coating was damaged, remove the remaining coating and reapply, as necessary. (e) If the plating was removed, inspect the plating. 1) Make sure that the plating meets the requirements and re-finish, as necessary. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-060 (4) Clean the surface. (e) If the plating was removed, inspect the plating. 1) Make sure that the plating meets the requirements and re-finish, as necessary. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-088 (4) Clean the surface. (a) Rinse the surface with water. 51-21-11 (b) Dry the surface with a clean, cotton wiper, G00034. F . Paint Stripping - Nanocomposite Blasting Method SUBTASK 51-21-11-950-049 (1) Make sure that the areas that will not be stripped are masked. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-089 (2) Make sure that the areas that will be stripped are clean and dry. SUBTASK 51-21-11-120-036 (3) Strip the surface using one of the nanocomposite abrasives that follow: (a) For general purpose stripping, use Magic 1 Nanocomposite Abrasive Media, 30/60 Mesh. (b) For an increased strip rate, use Magic II Composite Blast Media, E50012. (c) To remove cured sealant, use Magic 3 Nanocomposite Abrasive Media, 10/60 Mesh. (d) Make sure that the nozzle air pressure is less than 32 psig (221 kPa). (e) Make sure that the nozzle is at least 6 in. (152 mm) from the surface. (f) Make sure that the angle of the nozzle is 40° to 60° to the surface. (g) Abrade the surface equally down to the primer surface. NOTE: It is not necessary to remove the primers for the reapplication of primer, enamels, or topcoat. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-090 (4) Clean the surface. (a) Rinse the surface with water. (b) Dry the surface with a clean, cotton wiper, G00034.

51-21-11-150-815Composite Parts - Paint StrippingPDF p. 187

17. Composite Parts - Paint Stripping

A. General

(1) This task gives paint stripping instructions using the abrasive stripping methods that follow: (a) Conventional Abrasive Method (b) Wheat Starch Blasting Method. (2) For metal surfaces, you can remove paint by abrasive stripping, or by brush-on or paint-on with paint strippers or solvents. For procedures to remove paint with paint strippers or solvents, see Paint Stripping, TASK 51-21-11-150-801. (3) Make sure that the areas that follow are covered: (a) Lubricated parts (b) Rubber parts (c) Laminated plastic surfaces or parts (d) Fiberglass surfaces or parts (e) Aerodynamic smoothers (f) Metal bonded parts (g) Composite parts (h) Adjacent access doors, fairings, and wing Leading Edge (LE)s and Trailing Edge (TE)s 51-21-11 (i) All areas adjacent to the area being stripped (j) Drain holes and vents (k) Pitot static probes and ports (l) Angle of Attack (AOA) vanes (m) Cargo door and entry door hinges and thresholds (n) Cooling air exhaust duct (o) Tires (p) Ram air inlets (q) Engines and the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) inlets and exhausts (r) Pressurized drain valves (s) Joints. (4) Make sure that the ambient temperature is between 50°F (10°C) and 100°F (38°C). NOTE: Do not use the stripping procedure in hot or wet weather. (5) Definitions: (a) Light Soils: atmospheric soils and dust. (b) Moderate Soils: drawing or cutting oil and dust. (c) Heavy soils: grease or the soil on areas subjected to exhaust blast.

C. Prepare to Strip the Surface

SUBTASK 51-21-11-150-020 (1) Prepare to strip the surface, do this task: Prepare for Paint Stripping, TASK 51-21-11-370-801. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-091 (2) Clean the surface. (a) Remove loose soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, oil, and metal shavings using a cotton wiper, G00034. 1) Use an oil absorbing wiper to remove oil, if necessary. (b) Clean the surface with a cotton wiper, G00034, or brush, G00215, wet with a Series 80 solvent, B50268. (c) Immediately wipe the solvent from the surface using a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. 1) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. (d) Clean the surface again until the surface is free from all soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, oil, and metal shavings.

D. Paint Stripping - Conventional Abrasive Method

SUBTASK 51-21-11-950-050 (1) Make sure that the areas that will not be stripped are masked. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-092 (2) Make sure that the areas that will be stripped are clean and dry. SUBTASK 51-21-11-120-037 (3) Abrade the area to be stripped with 150 grit abrasive paper, G02428, or finer. (a) Abrade the surface equally down to the primer surface. NOTE: It is not necessary to remove the primers for the reapplication of primer, enamels, or topcoat. SUBTASK 51-21-11-120-038 (4) Abrade the area to be stripped with 240 grit or finer abrasive paper, G50077. (a) Make sure that you feather the primer and topcoat. (b) Make sure that you do not damage the fibers of the composite surface. (c) If the surface has conductive coating, do the steps that follow: 1) Remove all of the conductive coating. NOTE: This is to obtain uniform conductivity after re-application. 2) Re-apply the conductive coating. SUBTASK 51-21-11-160-093 (5) Clean the surface using clean, compressed air.

2. Repair the BMS14-4 Type I Corrosion Resistant Coating

A. References

Reference Title 20-30-84-910-801 Final Cleaning of Metal Prior to Painting (Series 84) (P/B 201) 51-21-99-300-801 Decorative Exterior Paint System Application (P/B 701)

B. Tools/Equipment

C. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification B00102 Abrasive - Aluminum Oxide Coated Cloth B01004 Solvent - Final Cleaning Of Metal Prior To Painting (AMM 20-30-84) - Series 84 C00250 Coating - Aluminum, Corrosion and Heat Resistant ,Thermosetting, Inorganic Binder AMS3126 (Supersedes BMS14-4 Type I) G00251 Abrasive - Mat, Non-Woven, Non-Metallic A-A-58054 G02222 Abrasive - Dry, Blasting BAC5748

D. Prepare the Surface

SUBTASK 51-21-12-120-001 (1) Dry abrasive blast the damaged area to bare, clean metal with a clean (preferably new) 80, 100, or 120 grit aluminum oxide abrasive, G02222. (a) Blow the area with clean dry air to remove the remaining abrasive material. (b) Do not touch the clean parts with your bare hands to prevent contamination of the surface. 51-21-12 (c) Protect the parts that were abrasive blasted until the parts are coated with coating, C00250. NOTE: The BMS14-4 Type I must be applied in less than four hours after the dry abrasive blast. SUBTASK 51-21-12-120-002 (2) Use abrasive cloth, B00102 or abrasive mat, G00251 to abrade (sand) the area to feather the edges of the damaged coating. (a) Scuff an area approximately 1/2 inch in width around the edge of the bare metal. SUBTASK 51-21-12-100-001 WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH OR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM SOLVENTS. PUT ON A RESPIRATOR, PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLES, AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE SOLVENTS. KEEP THE SOLVENTS AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . SOLVENTS ARE POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE. SOLVENTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (3) Clean the surface with Series 84 solvent, B01004 (TASK 20-30-84-910-801).

E. Apply the coating, BMS14-4, Type I

NOTE: Use spray painting equipment that continuously stirs the material to be sprayed and which is free from organic contaminates. Coat the parts with the BMS14-4, Type I material to get an equal, smooth, wet coating. SUBTASK 51-21-12-390-001 (1) Apply the coating, C00250 with a spray paint spray gun with interchangeable nozzles, STD-1133 or a paint brush, STD-1080. (a) Apply the coating to the surface with one of the steps that follow: 1) Apply the coating with one pass of the spray gun. 2) Apply two or three thin coats in 1 to 5 minutes of the other, at right angles to the previous pass. NOTE: This is necessary to prevent cracks or sags, and to keep the orange peel to a minimum. (b) The coating may be applied to the areas of the part that are not easy to spray paint with the items listed below followed immediately by spray coating the remaining areas of the part with the spray gun. 1) stencil gun 2) airbrush 3) hand brush. (c) Do not apply too much of the coating, C00250 because it will cause, runs, beads, drips, or curtains. 1) The conditions above can cause blistering, pitting, flaking, glazing, or heavy green discoloration during curing. (d) Make sure the coating is not too dry when it is applied because it will give a rough or sandy texture. 1) These rough areas are porous and can cause decreased corrosion protection and a decrease in the coating bond. 51-21-12 (e) Dry the parts coated with coating, C00250 for at least 15 minutes and then dry for 15 to 30 minutes at 175 ±25°F . 1) The coating must be smooth and not have any fish eyes. 2) The coating must have a smooth grey color after it is dry. 3) Cure the coating for 4 hours at 300 ±50°F . 4) You must see no lumps or runs in the cured coating. 5) The total coating must be 0.0015 to 0.0035 inches thick. NOTE: When is not at this specified thickness, you must apply more coats of the BMS14-4 Type I to get the specified thickness. (f) To apply the specified overcoat systems, do this task: Decorative Exterior Paint System Application, TASK 51-21-99-300-801.

PUT ON A RESPIRATOR, PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLES, AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE SOLVENTS. KEEP THE SOLVENTS AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . SOLVENTS ARE POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE. SOLVENTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Apply the coating, C00251 with a spray paint spray gun with interchangeable nozzles, STD-1133 or a paint brush, STD-1080 as follows. (a) Areas of the part that are not easy to spray paint can be done with a stencil gun, airbrush, or hand brush first. 1) Follow this immediately by spray coating the remaining areas of the part with a spray gun. (b) Do not apply too much of the coating, C00251 because it will cause, runs, beads, drips, or curtains. 1) The conditions above can cause blistering, pitting, flaking, glazing, or heavy green discoloration during curing. (c) Make sure the coating is not too dry when it is applied because it will produce a rough or sandy texture. 1) These rough areas are porous and can cause decreased corrosion protection and a decrease in the coating bond. (d) Dry the coated parts for 30 to 45 minutes at ambient temperature. 1) The coating must be smooth and not have any fish eyes. 2) The coating must have a equal gray color after it is dry. (e) Apply one coat of coating, C00251 catalyst to the coated area. 1) Let the catalyst cure for a minimum of 16 hours at ambient temperature. NOTE: Do not pre-mix the coating with the catalyst, and do not let the catalyst touch the adjacent surfaces. a) As an alternative, you can cure the catalyst for 4 hours at 300 ±50°F . 2) You must see no lumps or runs in the cured coating. 3) The total coating must be 0.0015 to 0.0035 inches thick. NOTE: When is not at the specified thickness, you must apply more coats to get the specified thickness.
