D. Clean the Surface

SUBTASK 51-21-21-110-001 (1) Do the steps that follow to clean the surface: NOTE: Use solvent, B00083, or solvent, B00074, for this step. WARNING DO NOT GET ALIPHATIC NAPHTHA OR DRY CLEANING SOLVENT IN YOUR MOUTH, YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THE ALIPHATIC NAPHTHA OR DRY CLEANING SOLVENT . PUT ON PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLES AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE ALIPHATIC NAPHTHA OR DRY CLEANING SOLVENT . KEEP ALIPHATIC NAPHTHA OR DRY CLEANING SOLVENT AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND TEMPERATURES ABOVE THE FLASH POINT . ALIPHATIC NAPHTHA OR DRY CLEANING SOLVENT IS A POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE SOLVENT WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (a) Remove the loose dirt, grease, and oil with cotton wiper, G00034, that is moist with solvent, B00074, or solvent, B00083. 1) Do not put solvent on an area that is larger than necessary. (b) Clean the surface with a cotton wiper, G00034, soft paint brush, STD-1080, or a sponge, G00116, that is moist with solvent, B00074, or solvent, B00083. 1) Rub the surface to remove all of the dirt. NOTE: You can use a spray gun to help clean the surface. (c) Flush the surface with clean solvent, B00074, or solvent, B00083. (d) Remove all unwanted solvent with a cotton wiper, G00034. 51-21-21 (e) Let the surface dry. (f) Attach the tags that follow to the left control wheel in the flight deck. 1) "PITOT PROBES COVERED" tag, G02447 2) "STATIC PORTS COVERED" tag, G02444 3) A red tag labeled “AOA SENSORS COVERED.” (g) Put a pitot probe cover, COM-1503, on the pitot probes. (h) Use Scotch Brand No.471 tape, G02219, and barricade tape, G02443, to cover the static ports. (i) Do the steps that follow to cover the Angle of Attack (AOA) sensors. 1) Cover the AOA sensors with PG-777 solvent-resistant masking tape. a) Apply PG-777 over the blade, plate, and blade-to-plate gap. NOTE: This is to allow easier removal of 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. 2) Cover the PG-777 solvent-resistant masking tape with 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. a) Shingle the 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291, from the blade-to-plate gap up to the blade tip until all of the masking tape is covered. SUBTASK 51-21-21-110-002 (2) Do the steps that follow to clean the area again: WARNING DO NOT GET ALIPHATIC NAPHTHA IN YOUR MOUTH, YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THE ALIPHATIC NAPHTHA. PUT ON PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLES AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE ALIPHATIC NAPHTHA. KEEP ALIPHATIC NAPHTHA AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND TEMPERATURES ABOVE THE FLASHPOINT . ALIPHATIC NAPHTHA IS A POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE SOLVENT WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . CAUTION YOU MUST FULLY CLEAN THE SURFACE BEFORE YOU APPLY PAINTS OR ADHESIVES. USE ALIPHATIC NAPHTHA IN THE LAST STEP OF THE PROCEDURE TO CLEAN THE SURFACE. DO NOT USE P-D-680 TYPE I FOR THE LAST STEP OF THE PROCEDURE TO CLEAN THE SURFACE. DAMAGE TO THE SURFACE CAN OCCUR IF P-D-680 TYPE I IS USED IN THE LAST STEP . (a) Use a spray bottle to apply the Aliphatic Naphtha solvent, B00083, to the surface. (b) Clean the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, until all large pieces of dirt are removed. NOTE: Use a soft bristle brush to clean if it is necessary. (c) Clean the surface again until no signs of the dirt are found on a clean cotton wiper, G00034. (d) Dry the area with a clean dry cotton wiper, G00034. 1) Do not let drops of solvent dry on the surface. 51-21-21

SUBTASK 51-21-21-150-002 (1) Prepare to remove the temporary finishes. CAUTION DO NOT USE PAINT STRIPPER ON COMPOSITE MATERIALS. PAINT STRIPPERS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE STRUCTURE OF THE PART . NOTE: You can use equivalent plastic sheeting that is resistant to paint strippers. 1) Use some of the materials that follow to protect the surface: a) Paper masking tape b) Plastic coated paper c) Plastic sheeting d) Wrapping paper, chemically neutral. (c) Attach the tags that follow to the left control wheel in the flight deck. 1) "PITOT PROBES COVERED" tag, G02447 2) "STATIC PORTS COVERED" tag, G02444 3) A red tag labeled “AOA SENSORS COVERED.” (d) Install the pitot probe cover, COM-1503, on the pitot probes. NOTE: This is to allow easier removal of 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. 2) Cover the PG-777 solvent-resistant masking tape with 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. a) Shingle the 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291, from the blade-to-plate gap up to the blade tip until all of the masking tape is covered. (0.051 mm) deep. 2) Areas with resin missing. 3) Other minor depressions that cannot be filled with the pinhole fillers. (f) Do the final cleaning of the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, that is moist with solvent, B00148, solvent, B00062, or alcohol. 51-21-21 (g) Fully dry the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, before the cleaner becomes dry. SUBTASK 51-21-21-370-003 (3) Prepare the internal non-decorative surfaces for paint. (a) Manually abrade (sand) the internal non-decorative surfaces with 150 grit or finer abrasive cloth, B00102. (b) Remove the sanding residue with the step that follows: 1) Clean the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, that is moist with solvent, B00148, solvent, B00062, or alcohol. (c) Examine the surface to determine if a surfacer is necessary. (d) Apply the Static Conditioner Filler 28-C-1 (or an applicable equivalent) to fill the pinholes if it is necessary. NOTE: Only use Static Conditioner Filler 28-C-1 (or an applicable equivalent) to fill the pinholes. 1) Do not apply a continuous layer of pinhole filler because it will cause an unsatisfactory paint bond. (e) If it is necessary, apply 825X466 primer-surfacer, A50597 (or an applicable equivalent) or Surfacer adhesive, A00028, to fill: NOTE: The surfacers are to be used only in the area of the pits in the surface or depression. Usually, surfacers are not used on the full part. 1) Pits in the surface. 2) Areas with resin missing. 3) Other minor depressions that cannot be filled with the pinhole fillers. (f) Do the final cleaning of the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, that is moist with solvent, B00148. (g) Fully dry the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, before the cleaner becomes dry.

D. Prepare For The Removal Of Corrosion

SUBTASK 51-21-31-160-002 (1) Make sure that all areas that are prepared for corrosion inhibiting compounds are clean. (2) Remove oil, grease, dirt, and paint from the surface or the part. (3) Make sure you remove all corrosion material from the surfaces or parts. Failure to remove all corrosion material can permit corrosion to start again. For limits of corrosion removal, refer to the Structural Repair Manual. (4) If you cannot immediately remove corrosion from an area, do this task: Surface Preparation for Corrosion Inhibiting Compound, TASK 51-21-91-620-801.

E. Procedure (Chemical)

SUBTASK 51-21-31-913-001 (1) Do the steps that follow to prepare the airplane for chemical corrosion removal from the external surface of the airplane: (a) If necessary, put the airplane in an area where you can fully flush all the surfaces with water, G50256 quickly. (b) Apply 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291 tape to hinges, mating surfaces, access doors and other openings that can allow the corrosion removing compound, E50003 to damage other metal types. NOTE: This can be the pitot static probes, static ports, angle of attack (AOA) vanes, and total air temperature (TAT) probe. (c) Apply 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291 to areas of magnesium, steel and cadmium plated parts. NOTE: This will prevent the accidental corrosion of different metal types. SUBTASK 51-21-31-150-001 (2) Do the steps that follow to remove aluminum corrosion from the external surface of the airplane with corrosion removing compound, E50003: 51-21-31 (a) Apply corrosion removing compound, E50003 with any of the items that follow: 1) Use a brush, G00268 to apply the compound. 2) Use a sponge, G00116 to apply the compound. 3) Use a lint-free cloth, G00834 to apply the compound. (b) Apply the compound at the lowest area and work up into a circular movement. NOTE: This will give a good layer and dwell time for the compound on the surface. (c) Let the compound to stay on the surface for approximately 12 minutes and do the step that follows: NOTE: Compound applied warm (140°F (60°C) maximum temperature) on the surface gives better results. 1) Rinse with water, G50256. 2) Do again this procedure to remove more corrosion, if necessary. 3) Dry the treated surface and do the steps in CHEMICAL CONVERSION COATING - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-41/701. SUBTASK 51-21-31-150-002 (3) Do the steps that follow, to remove small quantities of aluminum corrosion from the external surface of the airplane with acid, B00046: NOTE: This procedure is optional. (a) Fully flush the surface with water. WARNING DO NOT ADD WATER TO ACID. ALWAYS ADD ACID TO WATER. ACID IS EXPLOSIVE WHEN WATER IS ADDED TO IT . IF YOU ADD WATER TO ACID, INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (b) Add 1 part (by volume) of the corrosion remover, phosphoric acid, B00046 to 3 parts (by volume) of water, G50256. (c) Apply corrosion remover phosphoric acid, B00046 on the surface. (d) Fully flush all of the prepared area and the adjacent areas, with water, G50256. NOTE: Make sure that you flush out all the phosphoric acid corrosion remover from the areas that follow: the skin seams, and all openings or holes on the surface. (e) Do again this procedure to remove more corrosion, if necessary. (f) Dry the treated surface and do the steps in CHEMICAL CONVERSION COATING - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-41/701. F . Procedure (Mechanical Method) SUBTASK 51-21-31-913-002 (1) Do the steps that follow to prepare the airplane for mechanical corrosion removal from the external surface of the airplane: (a) If necessary, put the airplane in an area where you can fully flush all the surfaces with water, G50256 quickly. (b) Apply 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291 tape to hinges, mating surfaces, access doors and other openings that can allow the corrosion by-products to damage other metal types. 51-21-31 (c) Apply 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291 to areas of magnesium, steel and cadmium plated parts. SUBTASK 51-21-31-160-003 (2) Do any of the steps that follow to remove aluminum corrosion from the external surface of the airplane (Non-powered tools and materials): (a) Use a abrasive mat, G00251 to rub away corrosion. (b) Use a abrasive cloth, B00102 to rub away corrosion. (c) Use a 240 grit or finer abrasive paper, G50077 to rub away corrosion. (d) Use aluminum wool, G50590 to rub away corrosion. NOTE: Metallic wools are available in five grades, ranging from very fine to extra coarse. (e) Use a brush, G02414 to brush away corrosion. CAUTION DO NOT USE ABRASIVE PADS (SCOTCH-BRITE), OR ABRASIVE PAPER ON THE ALUMINUM SURFACE UNLESS THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS WERE MADE. ABRASIVE PADS CAN SMOOTH THE ALUMINUM SURFACE AND HIDE THE SCRIBE LINE MARKS. IF YOU USE ABRASIVE PADS TO REMOVE THE PAINT OR PRIMER BEFORE YOU DO THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS, YOU CAN BE REQUIRED TO DO REPEAT INSPECTIONS BASED ON THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTION SERVICE BULLETIN. 1) Remove the corrosion with a linear motion; do not crosshatch. This will unnecessarily damage the surface. 2) After wire brushing soft metal (such as aluminum or magnesium) the surface areas must be polished with a abrasive mat, G00251 or abrasive cloth, B00102. (f) Use pumice abrasive, B00166 to brush away corrosion. 1) Mix with water, G50256 and rub over the area with a soft cotton cloth, G50138. 2) After drying, the pumice abrasive, B00166 powder is wiped off. CAUTION DO NOT USE ABRASIVE PADS (SCOTCH-BRITE), OR ABRASIVE PAPER ON THE ALUMINUM SURFACE UNLESS THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS WERE MADE. ABRASIVE PADS CAN SMOOTH THE ALUMINUM SURFACE AND HIDE THE SCRIBE LINE MARKS. IF YOU USE ABRASIVE PADS TO REMOVE THE PAINT OR PRIMER BEFORE YOU DO THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS, YOU CAN BE REQUIRED TO DO REPEAT INSPECTIONS BASED ON THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTION SERVICE BULLETIN. CAUTION ONLY USE APPROVED SCRAPERS ON THE AIRPLANE SKIN. SCRAPERS THAT ARE NOT APPROVED CAN MAKE SCRATCHES ON THE SKIN, AND CAUSE FATIGUE CRACKS. (g) Scrapers are used primarily for the initial removal of heavy corrosion deposits in corners and crevices that cannot be reached with other equipment. 51-21-31 1) A sealant removal tool, COM-2481 and sealant removal tool handle, COM-4746 may be used on any metal surface. NOTE: If you use abrasive pads before you do scribe line inspections, you can be required to do repeat inspections based on the scribe line inspections Service Bulletin 737-53A1289. a) If necessary, do these steps to sharpen the scraper: <1> Sharpen the scraper with sandpaper, G50260 or finer by hand or by metal sharpening wheel (scraper sharpener, COM-4747). <2> If you sharpen the scraper by hand, rub the sharpened scraper on wiper, G50262 to remove loose sanding particles. <3> If you use a metal sharpening wheel, rub the sharpened scraper on sandpaper, G50261 or finer aluminum oxide paper to remove debris, and then rub it on wiper, G50262 to remove loose sanding particles. 2) Aluminum scrapers shall be used only on aluminum or magnesium surfaces. 3) Steel scrapers shall be used only on steel surfaces. SUBTASK 51-21-31-160-004 (3) After the removal of the corrosion, do the steps that follow: (a) Rinse with water, G50256. (b) Dry the treated surface and do the steps in CHEMICAL CONVERSION COATING - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-41/701.

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-21-31-350-003 WARNING SMALL PARTICLES AND FINE SHAVINGS OF MAGNESIUM START FIRES EASILY AND ARE EXTREMELY FLAMMABLE. MAGNESIUM DUST CAN CAUSE EXPLOSIONS. WATER IN CONTACT WITH BURNING MAGNESIUM IS A STEAM EXPLOSION HAZARD. EXTINGUISH FIRES WITH VERY DRY TALC, CALCIUM CARBONATE, SAND, OR GRAPHITE BY APPLYING THE POWDER TO A DEPTH OF 1/2 INCH OR MORE OVER THE BURNING METAL. DO NOT USE FOAM, WATER, CARBON TETRACHLORIDE, OR CARBON DIOXIDE TO EXTINGUISH FIRES OF MAGNESIUM. MAGNESIUM FIRES CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Do these steps to mechanically remove magnesium alloy corrosion from the airplane: (a) Make sure the metal is a magnesium alloy. (b) During the removal process, protect the surrounding area from the corrosion dust. (c) Remove any grease, oil, or paint from the area; do this task: Clean the Surface to be Painted, TASK 51-21-21-100-801. (d) Measure the corroded area to find the amount of corrosion damage. NOTE: Light corrosion will measure a maximum depth of 0.001 inch (0.025 mm). Moderate corrosion will measure a maximum depth of 0.010 inch (0.254 mm). Heavy corrosion will measure deeper than 0.010 inch (0.254 mm). (e) Remove loose corrosion with aluminum wool. (f) Remove the corrosion, based on the amount of damage: CAUTION DO NOT USE A CARBON STEEL BRUSH OR STEEL WOOL OR SILICONE CARBIDE ABRASIVE ON MAGNESIUM SURFACES. TINY DISSIMILAR METAL PARTICLES WILL CAUSE FURTHER CORROSION. 1) Remove light corrosion by hand sanding with an aluminum oxide abrasive cloth, B00102 or a garnet abrasive, B00137. 2) Remove light corrosion with pumice abrasive, B00166 paste. a) Mix the pumice abrasive, B00166 with water to make the paste. b) Use a clean cotton wiper, G00034 to apply and gently rub the pumice paste on the surface. c) When the pumice abrasive, B00166 is a dry, white powder, wipe off with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. d) Remove the remaining corrosion with #600 grit abrasive cloth, B00102 and water. 51-21-31 CAUTION DO NOT USE EXCESSIVE RUBBING. HEAVY , CONTINUOUS RUBBING (SUCH AS WITH POWER-DRIVEN WIRE BRUSHES) CAN MAKE ENOUGH HEAT TO CAUSE CHANGES IN METALLIC PROPERTIES. CHANGES IN METALLIC PROPERTIES CAN CAUSE MORE CORROSION. 3) Use one of these steps to remove moderate and heavy corrosion : a) #400 grit abrasive cloth, B00102 b) Use a brush, G02414 with bristles no more than 0.003 inch (0.076 mm) diameter and no less than 1.0 inch (25.4 mm) long. NOTE: After using the brush, polish the surface with #400 grit abrasive cloth, B00102 and then #600 grit abrasive cloth, B00102. CAUTION DO NOT USE TOO MUCH PRESSURE FOR ABRASIVE BLASTING. AIR PRESSURE FOR ABRASIVE BLASTING ON MAGNESIUM ALLOYS MUST BE 10 TO 35 PSI (69-241 KPA). TOO MUCH PRESSURE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO PARTS. c) Glass bead dry blasting abrasive, G02222 (170 to 400 grit). WARNING DO NOT GET CHROMIC ACID IN YOUR MOUTH, OR YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. PUT ON AN APRON, SPLASH GOGGLES, AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE CHROMIC ACID. CHROMIC ACID CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . WARNING DO NOT ADD WATER TO ACID. ALWAYS ADD ACID TO WATER. IF YOU ADD WATER TO ACID, YOU CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (g) After removing all corrosion that can be seen, apply a corrosion treating solution of chromium trioxide acid, C00167 or sodium dichromate with nitric acid, B00047, (SOPM 20-43-02). (h) Rinse the part well with clean water. (i) Smooth out repaired areas using Corrosion Damage and Rework Limits (SRM 51-10-02). (j) Clean the repaired area. (k) Measure the depth of the blends using Corrosion Damage and Rework Limits (SRM 51-10-02). (l) Treat the repaired area using Standard Treatment Methods (STANDARD TREATMENT METHODS, SUBJECT 51-00-58). SUBTASK 51-21-31-350-004 (2) Do the following steps to chemically remove the magnesium alloy corrosion from the external surface of the airplane: (a) Make sure the metal is a magnesium alloy. (b) Remove any grease, oil, and loose paint from the area, do this task: Clean the Surface to be Painted, TASK 51-21-21-100-801. (c) Protect the areas surrounding the corroded area. NOTE: Protect rubber parts, bearings, cast or pressed inserts, cracks, and plated steel. 51-21-31 WARNING DO NOT GET CHROMIC ACID IN YOUR MOUTH, OR YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. PUT ON AN APRON, SPLASH GOGGLES, AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE CHROMIC ACID. CHROMIC ACID CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . WARNING DO NOT ADD WATER TO ACID. ALWAYS ADD ACID TO WATER. IF YOU ADD WATER TO ACID, YOU CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (d) Prepare one of these chromic acid solutions according to manufacturer's directions, (SOPM 20-43-02): 1) Chromium trioxide acid, C00167, or 2) Sodium dichromate with nitric acid, B00047. (e) Apply with acid resistant medium nylon bristle brush, STD-3911. NOTE: Start from the lower surfaces and work upward to prevent runs and streaks. Apply with circular movement. (f) Keep the solution on the surface for 15 minutes. Wipe dry. NOTE: While the solution is on the surface, continue to brush over the surface again with a short fiber brush to prevent the solution from drying and streaking. (g) Rinse with water while scrubbing with brush. Wipe dry. NOTE: Repeat this sequence until the bright metallic color of the metal is shown. (h) Smooth out repaired areas using Corrosion Damage and Rework Limits (SRM 51-10-02). (i) Measure the depth of the repaired area using Corrosion Damage and Rework Limits (SRM 51-10-02). (j) Treat the repaired area using Standard Treatment Methods (STANDARD TREATMENT METHODS, SUBJECT 51-00-58).

Reference Description Specification B00046 Acid - Corrosion Removing, Metal Conditioning, Phosphoric MIL-C-10578 B00102 Abrasive - Aluminum Oxide Coated Cloth G02222 Abrasive - Dry, Blasting BAC5748 G02414 Brush - Stainless Steel 51-21-31

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-21-31-350-005 (1) Do these steps to mechanically remove corrosion from carbon steel parts of the airplane: NOTE: When the heat-treat value of a part is unknown, repair the part as if it was heat-treated over 220,000 psi (1516847 kPa). (a) Make sure the metal is carbon steel and find its heat treat value. (b) During the removal process, protect the surrounding area from the corrosion dust. (c) Remove any grease, oil, and loose paint from the area; do this task: Clean the Surface to be Painted, TASK 51-21-21-100-801. WARNING YOU SHOULD BE VERY CAREFUL WHEN USING TOOLS ON HIGH STRENGTH STEEL SO THAT THE STEEL SURFACE DOES NOT GET TOO HOT . HOT STEEL CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS. (d) Remove corrosion by any of these methods: NOTE: Hand-held power tools must mot be used on high strength steels heat-treated to 220,000 psi (1516847 kPa) and above. 1) Use a brush, G02414 with bristles no larger than 0.010 inch (0.254 mm) in diameter, NOTE: After using the brush, polish the surface with #400 grit abrasive cloth, B00102 and then #600 grit abrasive cloth, B00102. 2) Grinding with an abrasive wheel, CAUTION AIR PRESSURE MUST BE 40 TO 70 PSI (276-483 KPA) FOR ABRASIVE BLASTING ON CARBON STEEL HEAT-TREATED TO 220,000 PSI (1516847 KPA) AND ABOVE. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . 3) Glass bead dry blasting abrasive, G02222, or 4) Motor-driven wire brush. (e) Make sure all corrosion is removed. (f) Smooth out repaired areas using Corrosion Damage and Rework Limits (SRM 51-10-02). (g) Measure the depth of the repaired areas using Corrosion Damage and Rework Limits (SRM 51-10-02). (h) Treat the repaired area using Standard Treatment Methods (STANDARD TREATMENT METHODS, SUBJECT 51-00-58). SUBTASK 51-21-31-350-006 (2) Do the following steps to chemically remove corrosion from carbon steel parts of the airplane: NOTE: When the heat-treat value of a part is unknown, repair the part as if it was heat-treated over 220,000 psi (1516847 kPa). NOTE: The use of acid can cause hydrogen embrittlement on steel parts heat-treated above 220,000 psi (1516847 kPa). The use of acid is not allowed on steel parts heat-treated above 220,000 psi (1516847 kPa). (a) Make sure the metal is carbon steel and find its heat treat value. (b) During the removal process, protect the surrounding area from the corrosion dust. 51-21-31 (c) Remove any grease, oil, and loose paint from the area, do this task: Clean the Surface to be Painted, TASK 51-21-21-100-801. (d) Remove heavy rust by hand using a chipper or a brush, G02414. WARNING DO NOT GET PHOSPHORIC ACID IN YOUR MOUTH, OR YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. WEAR AN APRON, GOGGLES, AND ACID RESISTANT GLOVES WHEN YOU USE PHOSPHORIC ACID. PHOSPHORIC ACID CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . WARNING DO NOT ADD WATER TO ACID. ALWAYS ADD ACID TO WATER. IF YOU ADD WATER TO ACID, YOU CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (e) Use one of the following methods for chemical removal of corrosion: 1) Inhibited phosphoric acid, B00046 - (Brush-on Method) NOTE: Acid type removers are used for removing rust or black oxide. 2) Inhibited phosphoric acid, B00046 - (Soak-in Method) NOTE: Acid type removers are used for removing rust or black oxide. NOTE: This method is used for removing heavy rust from parts removed from the airplane and where the corroded area can be put fully into the acid base. WARNING THE ALKALI RUST REMOVER IS HIGHLY ALKALINE AND HARMFUL TO SKIN AND EYES. WEAR RUBBER GLOVES, APRONS, AND GOGGLES WHEN WORKING WITH THIS MATERIAL. MAKE SURE THAT THE AREA WHERE YOU WILL USE THIS MATERIAL HAS GOOD AIRFLOW. THE ALKALI RUST REMOVER CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . 3) Alkali Type Rust Remover - (Soak-in Method) NOTE: Alkali type removers are used for removing red rust. (f) If there is any remaining corrosion, do the rust removing method again. (g) Smooth out repaired areas using Corrosion Damage and Rework Limits (SRM 51-10-02). (h) Measure the depth of the repaired areas using Corrosion Damage and Rework Limits (SRM 51-10-02). (i) Treat the repaired area using Standard Treatment Methods (STANDARD TREATMENT METHODS, SUBJECT 51-00-58).

51-21-31-350-804Removal and Control of Corrosion for Stainless Steel and Nickel-Chromium AlloysPDF p. 228

5. Removal and Control of Corrosion for Stainless Steel and Nickel-Chromium Alloys (Table 701, Table 702)

A. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-21-31-350-007 CAUTION ABRASIVE BLASTING OR GRINDING SHALL NOT BE USED ON THIN WALL TUBES OR THIN WEBS LESS THAN 0.0625 INCH (1.5875 MM) THICK. THESE METHODS CAN DAMAGE THE STRUCTURE. (1) Remove corrosion mechanically by using the same general procedures as for carbon steel; do this task: Removal and Control of Corrosion for Carbon Steel, TASK 51-21-31-350-803. SUBTASK 51-21-31-350-008 (2) Remove corrosion chemically by using the same general procedures as for carbon steel; do this task: Removal and Control of Corrosion for Carbon Steel, TASK 51-21-31-350-803. NOTE: Only use chemical removers on stainless steel and nickel-chromium alloys in very corroded areas and where the chemicals will not be trapped in cracks, lap joints, crevices, and other such areas.

A. References

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-21-31-350-009 WARNING SMALL CHIPS OR SLIVERS OF A TITANIUM ALLOY , CAUSED BY A MACHINING PROCESS ARE VERY FLAMMABLE. EXTINGUISH THESE FIRES WITH VERY DRY TALC, CALCIUM CARBONATE, SAND, OR GRAPHITE. DO NOT USE WATER, CARBON DIOXIDE, CARBON TETRACHLORIDE OR THE ORDINARY CHEMICAL FIRE EXTINGUISHER. TITANIUM FIRES CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Remove corrosion mechanically from a titanium alloy by these steps: (a) Make sure the metal is a titanium alloy. 51-21-31 (b) Remove any grease, oil, or paint from the area, do this task: Clean the Surface to be Painted, TASK 51-21-21-100-801. (c) Apply aluminum polish by hand with a cotton wiper, G00034. Do this until all corrosion is removed. (d) Remove the polish with a clean cotton wiper, G00034. (e) Treat repaired area using Standard Treatment Methods (STANDARD TREATMENT METHODS, SUBJECT 51-00-58). SUBTASK 51-21-31-350-010 (2) Removal of corrosion by chemicals is not allowed on titanium alloys. NOTE: Titanium can become brittle when exposed to acid solutions. Chemical removers are not allowed.

51-21-31-350-806Removal and Control of Corrosion for Plated or Phosphated SurfacesPDF p. 229

7. Removal and Control of Corrosion for Plated or Phosphated Surfaces (Table 701, Table 702)

A. References

Reference Title 51-00-58 STANDARD TREATMENT METHODS 51-21-21-100-801 Clean the Surface to be Painted (P/B 701)

B. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification B00046 Acid - Corrosion Removing, Metal Conditioning, Phosphoric MIL-C-10578 C00167 Acid, Chromic (Chromium Trioxide) A-A-55827 G02414 Brush - Stainless Steel

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-21-31-350-011 (1) Remove corrosion from cadmium plated surfaces by the following steps: (a) During the removal process, protect the surrounding area from the corrosion dust and contamination. (b) Remove any grease, oil, or paint from the area, do this task: Clean the Surface to be Painted, TASK 51-21-21-100-801. (c) If corrosion is only on the plated surface, repair as follows (if corrosion has gone through the plated surface, refer to steps below): 1) Rub gently with stainless steel wool. NOTE: Removal work on plated surfaces should be kept to a minimum. This will make sure of the preservation of the adjacent plating. WARNING DO NOT GET CHROMIC ACID IN YOUR MOUTH, OR YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. PUT ON AN APRON, SPLASH GOGGLES, AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE CHROMIC ACID. CHROMIC ACID CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . 51-21-31 (WARNING PRECEDES) WARNING DO NOT ADD WATER TO ACID. ALWAYS ADD ACID TO WATER. IF YOU ADD WATER TO ACID, YOU CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . 2) Apply the solution of chromic acid, C00167 and allow to stay on the corroded surface for 30 to 60 seconds. NOTE: The solution strength shall be 4 ounces (.12 liter) of chromium trioxide to 1 U.S. gallon (3.8 liters) of water. 3) Rinse part with clean water and air dry. (d) If corrosion has gone through the plated surface, repair as follows: 1) Decide if the part should be repaired or replaced. 2) If the part can be repaired, identify the base metal and remove corrosion according to the base metal's applicable procedure. (e) Treat repaired area using Standard Treatment Methods (STANDARD TREATMENT METHODS, SUBJECT 51-00-58). SUBTASK 51-21-31-350-012 (2) Remove corrosion from plated surfaces (that are NOT cadmium plated) by the following steps: (a) During the removal process, protect the surrounding area from the contaminants. (b) Remove any grease, oil, and loose paint from the area, do this task: Clean the Surface to be Painted, TASK 51-21-21-100-801. (c) Remove heavy rust by hand using a chipper or a brush, G02414 . WARNING DO NOT GET PHOSPHORIC ACID IN YOUR MOUTH, OR YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. PUT ON AN APRON, SPLASH GOGGLES, AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE PHOSPHORIC ACID. PHOSPHORIC ACID CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . WARNING DO NOT ADD WATER TO ACID. ALWAYS ADD ACID TO WATER. IF YOU ADD WATER TO ACID, YOU CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (d) Apply phosphoric acid, B00046 to corroded area. NOTE: Allow the acid solution to stay on the corroded surface only long enough to remove the corrosion. NOTE: Mix the acid on a 1:1 ratio. (e) Rinse the part with clean water and air dry. (f) Treat repaired area using Standard Treatment Methods (STANDARD TREATMENT METHODS, SUBJECT 51-00-58). SUBTASK 51-21-31-350-013 (3) To repair phosphated cadmium surfaces refer to the procedures for cadmium plated surfaces. D. Prepare the Surface for Coating

SUBTASK 51-21-41-950-001 (1) Apply masking tape, G51270, or 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291, to all adjacent areas. NOTE: Do not let the chemical conversion coating solution fall on surfaces that have no tape. NOTE: Do not apply tape on anodized surfaces. (a) Attach the tags that follow to the left control wheel in the flight deck. 1) "PITOT PROBES COVERED" tag, G02447 2) "STATIC PORTS COVERED" tag, G02444 3) A red tag labeled “AOA SENSORS COVERED”. (b) Put a pitot probe cover, COM-1503, on the pitot probe. (c) Apply masking tape, G51270, or 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291, on the static ports. (d) Do the steps that follow to cover the Angle of Attack (AOA) sensors. 1) Cover the angle-of-attack sensors with solvent resistant masking tape, G51270. a) Apply solvent resistant masking tape, G51270, over the blade, plate, and blade-to-plate gap. NOTE: This is to allow easier removal of 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. 2) Cover the solvent resistant masking tape, G51270, with 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. 51-21-41 a) Shingle the aluminum foil tape from the blade-to-plate gap up to the blade tip until all of solvent resistant masking tape, G51270, is covered. SUBTASK 51-21-41-110-005 (2) For polished surfaces, do these steps: (a) Do these steps until a water-break free condition is achieved: 1) Clean surface with cotton wiper, G00034, sponge, G00116, or cleaning pad, G51318, moist with a dilute alkaline cleaner, B50094. 2) Use cotton wiper, G00034, or sponge, G00116, soaked with water to remove alkaline cleaner, B50094, residue. 3) Apply a film of water to the part surface and inspect for a water-break free condition. (b) Dry the surface prior to conversion coating. (c) Continue directly with the topic: Procedure - Apply Bonderite M-CR 1001 Solution. SUBTASK 51-21-41-390-001 (3) Seal all holes and clearances on assemblies that have honeycomb or foam plastic. (a) Use the applicable sealing or caulking material or use rubber plugs to prevent entrance of Bonderite M-CR 1001 Aero coating, C50015, solution. SUBTASK 51-21-41-140-001 (4) Clean the surface with alkaline cleaner, B50094. (a) Use a clean soft bristle brush, STD-123, or cotton wiper, G00034. (b) Dry the surface with warm air or rub it. SUBTASK 51-21-41-100-001 (5) Make sure that there are no particles and corrosion materials on the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-41-140-002 (6) Use abrasive mat, G00251, or abrasive cloth, B00102, to clean the area to be conversion coated. NOTE: The repair area must be free of organic, inorganic, and hydraulic fluid resistant finishes. SUBTASK 51-21-41-110-001 WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH, YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS ARE DANGEROUS MATERIALS. SOLVENTS CAN BE FLAMMABLE OR CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENVIRONMENT . REFER TO THE MATERIAL SAFETY DATA SHEETS (MSDS) AND THE LOCAL SAFETY PRECAUTIONS. (7) Rub the surface with cotton wiper, G00034. NOTE: It is permitted to flush the remaining particles and residue with water. (a) Make cotton wiper, G00034, moist (not soaked) with Series 88 solvent, B01008 (TASK 20-30-88-910-801), or with solvent, B00151. (b) Clean the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, until no remaining particles and residue are found. SUBTASK 51-21-41-110-003 (8) Apply a film of water, G50256, to the part surface. (a) Inspect the part for a water break-free surface. 51-21-41 SUBTASK 51-21-41-910-001 (9) Let the surface dry. SUBTASK 51-21-41-100-002 (10) For information on the installation of sealant in the integral fuel tanks (SRM 51-20-05).

E. Procedure - Apply Bonderite M-CR 1001 Aero Solution

NOTE: In areas where the chemical conversion coating may come in contact with BMS 10-20 primer, only Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862, should be used. NOTE: Keep the room temperature above 65°F (18.3°C). Do not apply in direct sunlight. NOTE: Before you apply Bonderite M-CR 1001 Aero coating, C50015, you must mix with water to create a solution. SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-022 WARNING DO NOT GET CHEMICAL CONVERSION COATING SOLUTION IN YOUR MOUTH, IN YOUR EYES, ON YOUR SKIN, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THIS MATERIAL. AIR MUST FLOW FREELY THROUGH THE WORK AREA. USE THE NECESSARY RESPIRATORY PROTECTION. KEEP THIS MATERIAL AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THIS MATERIAL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) To prepare Bonderite M-CR 1001 Aero coating, C50015 solution, refer to the manufacturers instructions for the correct mixture ratios. SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-002 WARNING DO NOT GET CHEMICAL CONVERSION COATING SOLUTION IN YOUR MOUTH, IN YOUR EYES, ON YOUR SKIN, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THIS MATERIAL. AIR MUST FLOW FREELY THROUGH THE WORK AREA. USE THE NECESSARY RESPIRATORY PROTECTION. KEEP THIS MATERIAL AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THIS MATERIAL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (2) Apply Bonderite M-CR 1001 Aero coating, C50015, solution with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, medium nylon bristle brush, STD-3911, cellulose sponge, or a mop (cotton). (a) Keep the part wet with Bonderite M-CR 1001 Aero coating, C50015, for 15-30 seconds before the color to be produced. NOTE: Do not let the papers or cloths dry after you apply chemical conversion coating solutions. They can cause a fire when they are dry. After you use the cloths or paper soak them in water before you discard them. NOTE: If the solution breaks up into beads, or if a powdery layer occurs, lightly sand area with 600-grit paper and apply the coating again. SUBTASK 51-21-41-170-001 (3) Flush the surface with water or, if parts could catch water, use a cloth or sponge that is moist with water. NOTE: Be careful when you rub or dry the surface. Do not remove the coating or cause scratches on the surface. 51-21-41 SUBTASK 51-21-41-910-002 CAUTION DO NOT TOUCH THE PART UNTIL IT IS FULLY DRY . THE WET CHEMICAL CONVERSION COATING SOLUTION IS EASILY DAMAGED. (4) Air dry the surface. (a) Touch the dry parts or surface with clean rubber gloves, STD-1086, and keep parts or surface dry and clean to prevent surface contamination.

D. Prepare the Surface for Coating

SUBTASK 51-21-41-950-002 (1) Apply Scotch Flatback Masking T ape 250, G00270, to all adjacent areas. (a) Do not let the chemical conversion coating solution fall on surfaces that have no tape. (b) Attach the tags that follow to the left control wheel in the flight deck. 1) "PITOT PROBES COVERED" tag, G02447 2) "STATIC PORTS COVERED" tag, G02444 3) A red tag labeled “AOA SENSORS COVERED”. (c) Put a pitot probe cover, COM-1503, on the pitot probe. (d) Apply Scotch Flatback Masking T ape 250, G00270, on the static ports. (e) Do the steps that follow to cover the Angle of Attack (AOA) sensors. 1) Cover the AOA sensors with PG-777 solvent-resistant masking tape. a) Apply PG-777 over the blade, plate, and blade-to-plate gap. NOTE: This is to allow easier removal of 3M 425 aluminum tape. 2) Cover the PG-777 solvent-resistant masking tape with 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. 51-21-41 a) Shingle the aluminum foil tape from the blade-to-plate gap up to the blade tip until all of the masking tape is covered. SUBTASK 51-21-41-110-002 WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH, YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS ARE DANGEROUS MATERIALS. SOLVENTS CAN BE FLAMMABLE. (2) Clean the surface, do the following steps: (a) Rub the surface with a cotton wiper, G00034. 1) Make the cotton wiper, G00034, moist (not soaked) with Series 88 solvent, B01008 (TASK 20-30-88-910-801), or with solvent, B00151. 2) Clean the surface again with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, until no remaining particles or residue are found. (b) Let the surface dry for a minimum of 15 minutes. (c) Apply a thin film of water, G50256, to part surface and inspect for a water break-free surface.

E. Prepare Coating

NOTE: In areas where the chemical conversion coating may come in contact with BMS 10-20 primer, only Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862, must be used. NOTE: Keep the room temperature above 65°F (18.3°C). SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-004 WARNING DO NOT GET CHEMICAL CONVERSION COATING SOLUTION IN YOUR MOUTH, IN YOUR EYES, ON YOUR SKIN, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THIS MATERIAL. AIR MUST FLOW FREELY THROUGH THE WORK AREA. USE THE NECESSARY RESPIRATORY PROTECTION. KEEP THIS MATERIAL AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THIS MATERIAL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Put Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862, Bonderite M-CR ALCRM1200 Aero coating, C50357, or Bonderite M-CR 1200S Aero coating, C50005, on paper and use a roller to make the powder smooth. SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-005 (2) Mix the solution in a stainless steel container (1 gal) (4 Liter), STD-1118, or acid resistant container, STD-1052. NOTE: Do not use lead or glass. SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-006 (3) For Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862, add 3 oz (85 g) of powder to water for each 1 gal (3.8 l) of final solution. (a) Stir until the powder is dissolved. (b) Add up to 2% by volume of Bonderite M-AD 22 Toner Aero surface treatment, C50358, ammonium hydroxide, or nitric acid as required to adjust the pH to between 1.5 and 2.0. 51-21-41 SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-007 (4) For Bonderite M-CR ALCRM1200 Aero coating, C50357, add 3 oz (85 g) of powder to water for each 1 gal (3.8 l) of final solution. (a) Stir until the powder is dissolved. (b) Keep the pH in the range of 1.50 - 1.90. (c) Adjust the pH down with nitric acid or adjust the pH up with ammonium hydroxide. SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-021 (5) For Bonderite M-CR 1200S Aero coating, C50005, add 1.9 oz (54 g) - 2.1 oz (60 g) of powder to water for each 1 gal (3.8 l) of final solution. SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-008 (6) Fully mix the solution until the powder is dissolved. (a) Ignore small quantities of material that do not dissolve. SUBTASK 51-21-41-910-003 (7) Allow to stand for 1 hour before use. NOTE: Prepare the solution in small quantities. Discard the solution after you use it if a brush, sponge, or wiper was put into it or if contamination gets into the solution. Do not add wetting agents or other materials to this solution. F . Procedure - Apply Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero, Bonderite M-CR ALCRM 1200 Aero, or Bonderite M-CR 1200S Aero. NOTE: In areas where the chemical conversion coating may come in contact with BMS 10-20 primer, only Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862, must be used. SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-009 WARNING DO NOT GET CHEMICAL CONVERSION COATING SOLUTION IN YOUR MOUTH, IN YOUR EYES, ON YOUR SKIN, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THIS MATERIAL. AIR MUST FLOW FREELY THROUGH THE WORK AREA. USE THE NECESSARY RESPIRATORY PROTECTION. KEEP THIS MATERIAL AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THIS MATERIAL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Apply Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862, Bonderite M-CR ALCRM1200 Aero coating, C50357, or Bonderite M-CR 1200S Aero coating, C50005, equally with a medium nylon bristle brush, STD-3911, or a clean cotton wiper, G00034, or a cellulose sponge, or mop (cotton). (a) Start from the bottom. SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-010 (2) Let the solution stay on the surface until a given color is found (approximately 2 - 3 minutes). NOTE: Do not let the Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862, Bonderite M-CR ALCRM1200 Aero coating, C50357, or Bonderite M-CR 1200S Aero coating, C50005, solution dry until the color of the surface changes. NOTE: If the color does not come, if the solution breaks up into beads, or if a powdery layer occurs, lightly sand area with 600-grit paper and apply the coating again. (a) Keep the area wet. (b) Apply small quantities of solution with a cotton wiper, G00034. 51-21-41 SUBTASK 51-21-41-140-005 (3) Carefully flush the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, that is moist with water. NOTE: Do not let Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862, Bonderite M-CR 1200S Aero coating, C50005, Bonderite M-CR 600RTU Aero coating, C50356, or Bonderite M-CR 1201 Aero coating, C50355, solution dry until the color of the surface changes. (a) Start from the bottom. SUBTASK 51-21-41-140-006 (4) Lightly rub the surface with a clean dry cotton wiper, G00034, to remove unwanted liquid. (a) Rub the surface until the liquid is gone. SUBTASK 51-21-41-100-003 (5) Immediately after use, fully clean the cloths in water and keep them in a container filled with water. SUBTASK 51-21-41-910-004 (6) Dry the surface with air that is a temperature of 120°F (49°C) (recommended) with a maximum of 130°F (54°C) (maximum). SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-011 (7) Apply the last finish or start adhesive bonding (Chapter 51 of the Structural Repair Manual). (a) Touch the parts or surface with clean rubber glove, STD-1086, and keep the parts or surface dry and clean to prevent surface contamination.

SOLVENTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (a) Clean the surface with a cotton wiper, G00034, soft paint brush, STD-1080, or a sponge, G00116, that is moist with solvent, B00074, or solvent, B00083. NOTE: A spray gun can be used to help clean the surface. 1) Be careful not to put solvent on an area that is larger than is necessary. (b) Flush the surface with clean solvent, B00074, or solvent, B00083. (c) Clean the surface again with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, until no remaining particles or residue are found. (d) Let the surface dry for a minimum of 15 minutes. (e) Apply a thin film of water, G50256, to part surface and inspect for a water break-free surface.

D. Bonderite M-CR 1132 Aero Application Process

SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-012 (1) Remove cap. Hold Bonderite M-CR 1132 Aero coating, C50079, with applicator tip downwards. SUBTASK 51-21-41-840-001 (2) Activate the Bonderite M-CR 1132 Aero coating, C50079, pen by pressing tip against a firm surface. This will open the valve allowing Bonderite M-CR 1132 Aero coating, C50079, to reach applicator tip. A new unit should charge in 15 to 30 seconds. When the Bonderite M-CR 1132 Aero coating, C50079 wets the tip, release pressure. Unit is ready for use. SUBTASK 51-21-41-200-001 (3) Ensure that surface to be coated is dry before proceeding. SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-013 (4) Apply Bonderite M-CR 1132 Aero coating, C50079, to the part surface in smooth even strokes. Fifty percent overlap of strokes usually gives proper coating weight. Do not allow the Bonderite M-CR 1132 Aero coating, C50079, to puddle. Puddling will increase the time required for drying, and thick uneven areas in the coating cause performance failures. 51-21-41 SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-014 (5) Apply the second coat within 5 minutes after the first Bonderite M-CR 1132 Aero coating, C50079, dries and repeat the application in a cross hatch pattern. Do not wipe. Do not water rinse. Water rinse degrades corrosion resistance and paint adhesion. SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-015 (6) Ambient air dry or force air dry coating at 130°F (54°C) maximum sufficiently to evaporate water.

D. Prepare the Surface for Coating

SUBTASK 51-21-41-950-003 (1) Apply Scotch Flatback Masking T ape 250, G00270 to all adjacent areas. Do not let the coating fall on surfaces that have no tape. (a) Attach the tags that follow to the left control wheel in the flight deck. 1) "PITOT PROBES COVERED" tag, G02447 2) "STATIC PORTS COVERED" tag, G02444 3) A red tag labeled “AOA SENSORS COVERED” (b) Put a pitot probe cover, COM-1503 on the pitot probe. (c) Apply Scotch Flatback Masking T ape 250, G00270 on the static ports. (d) Do the steps that follow to cover the angle-of-attack (AOA) sensors. 1) Cover the angle-of-attack sensors with PG-777 solvent-resistant masking tape. a) Apply PG-777 over the blade, plate, and blade-to-plate gap. NOTE: This is to allow easier removal of 3M 425 aluminum tape. 2) Cover the PG-777 solvent-resistant masking tape with 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. a) Shingle the aluminum foil tape from the blade-to-plate gap up to the blade tip until all of the masking tape is covered. (2) Clean surface in accordance with one of the following: (a) solvent clean in accordance with SOPM 20-30-03, or (b) vapor degreasing in accordance with SOPM 20-30-03, or (c) emulsion clean in accordance with SOPM 20-30-03, or (d) manual clean in accordance with SOPM 20-30-03, or (e) alkaline clean in accordance with SOPM 20-30-03. (3) Wet abrade with a pneumatic sander or hand wet abrade to a dull finish with abrasive pads (Table 702, see below for definition), and water. Abrade lap and butt splices too if they are to be subsequently painted. Abrade with caution to meet the surface integrity requirements of D6–9002. (4) Do not abrade surfaces that will not be subsequently painted. (5) After abrading the wetted surface, flush with ample water. Do not allow the surface to dry before rinsing. (6) After wet abrade, it is optional to alkaline clean in accordance with SOPM 20-30-03. 51-21-41 (7) Check for a water-break-free surface on all surfaces in accordance with Table 703 (see below). If water breaks occur, abrade or alkaline clean again. NOTE: When the aluminum surface is not water-break-free, the surface is not clean. NOTE: Formation of chemical conversion coating only occurs on a clean surface. NOTE: Formation of chemical conversion coating is necessary for in-service paint durability. (8) Apply sol-gel coating, C50157 within 8 hours after manual abrasive pre-treatment. Table 702/51-21-41-993-805 Section 5.2.1.2: Abrasive Pads A) Scotch-Brite General Purpose hand Pad 7447, very fine, maroon color, aluminum oxide, non-woven, resin bonded, 3M Company. NOTE: All sizes are permitted. The UPC code for the 9 1/4 inch by 3 2/3 inches size is 48011–27693. B) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, grade A, maroon color, aluminum oxide, non-woven, resin bonded, 3M Company. NOTE: All sizes are permitted. The UPC code for the 6 inches disc size is 48011–00661. C) Scotch-Brite General Purpose Hand Pad 7447 Pro, very fine, maroon color, aluminum oxide, non-woven, resin bonded, 3M Company. NOTE: All sizes are permitted. The UPC code for the 9 1/4 inch by 3 2/3 inches size is 48011–27693. D) Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, maroon color, aluminum oxide, Saint Gobain Abrasives, Inc. Table 703/51-21-41-993-806 Section 12.2: Water-Break-Free Test The water-break-free surface check is as follows: a) Flush surface with water. b) If surface is clean (free of oils), water will make an unbroken layer and sheet off. If surface is not clean, water will bead on the surface (droplets) or appear as patchy and non-uniform. c) After curtains of water have stopped flowing, measure the time that the water is continuous. The surface is water-break-free if the water is continuous for approximately 30 seconds.

E. Prepare the coating.

SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-016 (1) Prepare the sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119 according to the manufacturer's kitting procedures. (a) The kit should be used within 1 year of the date of manufacture on the kit. (b) Do not treat surfaces with the sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119 before the 30-minute induction time. (c) Do not treat surfaces with the sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119 after the 24-hour application time has expired. (d) Make sure the temperature of the surface you will be treating and the air temperature are at least 55°F (13°C). Table 704/51-21-41-993-808 Recommended Volume of BMS10-128 Model Volume of BMS10–128 to be mixed by model (gallon) Minimum volume to be applied to the aircraft skin (gallon) 737–700 4 2.9 51-21-41 Table 704/51-21-41-993-808 Recommended Volume of BMS10-128 (Continued) Model Volume of BMS10–128 to be mixed by model (gallon) Minimum volume to be applied to the aircraft skin (gallon) 737–800 5 3.5 737–900ER 6 3.8 NOTE: One gallon of BMS10–128 will cover approximately 800–1200 square feet of surface, when applied with a single wet coat or two light coats. F . Apply the coating. NOTE: Do not apply BMS10–128 when the surface and the surrounding temperature is below 55°F (13°C). NOTE: Make sure that the surface is dry before applying BMS10–128. SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-017 (1) Use a high volume, low pressure paint sprayer, STD-623 or pressure sprayer, STD-818 to apply the sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119. NOTE: Once the sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119 has been applied and dried, primer should be applied to the airplane within 24 hours. (a) Start at the bottom of the area you will be treating. Apply sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119 from the bottom to the top of the surface. (b) Apply a continuous layer to sufficiently wet the substrate. It is acceptable to apply a single wet coat or two light coats. (c) Make sure no water-breaks occur on the surface you are treating. CAUTION DO NOT USE ABRASIVE PADS (SCOTCH-BRITE), OR ABRASIVE PAPER ON THE ALUMINUM SURFACE UNLESS THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS WERE MADE. ABRASIVE PADS CAN SMOOTH THE ALUMINUM SURFACE AND HIDE THE SCRIBE LINE MARKS. IF YOU USE ABRASIVE PADS TO REMOVE THE PAINT OR PRIMER BEFORE YOU DO THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS, YOU CAN BE REQUIRED TO DO REPEAT INSPECTIONS BASED ON THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTION SERVICE BULLETIN. 1) If water-breaks occur, use an abrasive pad (Scotch-Brite) to rework the area. Clean the area and re-apply the sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119. SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-018 (2) Allow the coated surface to drain until excess solution no longer drips. SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-019 (3) After the surface has drained, use filtered, compressed air to remove surplus sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119 that accumulated in crevices, pockets, drip edges, or fastener holes. (a) If necessary, a cotton wiper, G00034 can be used to soak up the sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119. Do not rub the wiper on the surface. 51-21-41 SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-020 (4) Allow the sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119 to dry until the surface is visually dry. NOTE: Until it cures and hardens, sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119 can be damaged by contact such as touching, wiping, and rubbing and by such means as water rinsing, solvent flushing, and masking tape application. Depending on the cure conditions, the sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119 can cure for more than six hours. (a) Do not apply masking tape to surfaces treated with sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119. (b) Make sure sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119 has fully dried before applying primer. NOTE: Uneven drying of the sol-gel coating, C50157 or AC-131-CB metal conversion coating, C50119 can leave dark areas on the surface. The dark areas are acceptable.

C. Apply the Conversion Coating

SUBTASK 51-21-51-120-001 WARNING MAGNESIUM POWDER CAN CAUSE A FIRE. INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (1) Rub the surface with an emery cloth, G00744, #240 grit. SUBTASK 51-21-51-100-001 (2) Clean the surface as follows: (a) Remove all loose particles from the surface with a soft bristle brush, STD-123 or rub the surface with clean cotton wiper, G00034 CAUTION PROTECT ALL SURFACES THAT YOU DO NOT WANT TO CLEAN. CLEANER CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO CADMIUM OR ALUMINUM FINISHES. (b) Apply protection to all areas that you do not want to clean. NOTE: Use a material that will resist cleaning and conversion coating solutions. (c) To prepare the cleaning solution, mix 10 volumes of water to 1 volume of Kelite 28. 51-21-51 CAUTION DO NOT LET THE CLEANING SOLUTION INTO FAYING SURFACES. DAMAGE TO THE FAYING SURFACES CAN OCCUR IF YOU PERMIT THE CLEANING SOLUTION TO STAY ON THE SURFACE. (d) Apply the cleaning solution to the surface using a cotton wiper, G00034, soft bristle brush, STD-123, or a sponge, G00116 NOTE: Let the solution soak for five minutes. NOTE: Do not let the cleaner dry on the surface. (e) Thoroughly flush the surface with a clean wet sponge, G00116 or cotton wiper, G00034 to completely remove cleaner residue. (f) Apply a thin film of water to part surface and inspect for a water break-free surface. NOTE: A water break-free surface will have a continuous layer of water for 30 seconds. (g) Clean the surface with a mixture of magnesium oxide and water to remove the water break. (h) Dry the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034. (i) Flush the surface again with a clean wet cotton wiper, G00034 or sponge, G00116. SUBTASK 51-21-51-110-001 (3) Mix the Dow 19 conversion coating as follows: (a) In a clean 1 gallon (3.8 liters) glass or polyethylene container: 1) add 9/10 gallon (3.4 liters) water, 2) add 1 1/3 ounce (0.04 liter) chromic acid, 3) add 1 ounce (0.03 liter) calcium sulfate, and 4) add water to fill the container to the 1 gallon (3.8 liter) level. (b) Mix the solution for a minimum of 15 minutes. NOTE: Let the particles in the solution go to the bottom of the container. NOTE: The solution must be free of all particles when it is applied. (c) Measure the 'pH' of the solution and check that it is between 1.2 and 1.6. (d) If the 'pH' is not correct, do the following: 1) Use sulfuric acid to lower the 'pH'. 2) Use sodium hydroxide to increase the 'pH'. SUBTASK 51-21-51-110-002 (4) Apply the conversion coating solution. (a) Apply a sufficient quantity of the solution to wet the metal surface until the surface is gold to dark brown in color. (b) Flush the surface with clean cold water. (c) Dry the surface with air that is no more than 180 degrees F (82.2 C). (d) Make sure that all of the surface is coated. (e) Make sure there are no scratches, powder or lines on the surface. (f) If there is any scratches or powder on the surface do the following: 1) Rub the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034 and apply the conversion coating again. 51-21-51 SUBTASK 51-21-51-370-001 (5) As soon as possible, apply the correct protective finish to prevent contamination of the surface or the start of corrosion.

NOTE: The following cleaners are optional to Cee Bee 280 cleaner, B00005: cleaner, B00402, Oakite 204 cleaner, B00008, and Calla 301A cleaner, B00015. NOTE: Make sure the area is clean. 3) Clean the area again if it is not fully clean. (c) For all other surfaces: 1) Fully clean the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with solvent, B00083. 2) Before the solvent dries, rub dry the surface with a clean dry cotton wiper, G00034. 3) Clean the area again if it is not fully clean. SUBTASK 51-21-61-350-001 (3) Repair all the damaged hydraulic fluid resistant finish. E. Prepare (Mix) the Hydraulic Fluid Resistant Finish

SUBTASK 51-21-61-390-001 CAUTION USE CLEAN SOLVENT-RESISTANT CONTAINERS WHEN YOU MIX THE HYDRAULIC-FLUID-RESISTANT FINISH. DO NOT USE CONTAINERS THAT CONTAIN ORGANIC COATINGS. DIRTY CONTAINERS AND ORGANIC COATINGS CAN CAUSE CONTAMINATION OF THE MIXTURE. (1) Fully mix 1 part (by volume) of the Catalyst (X-310) to 2 parts (by volume) of the base (683-3-2) to make coating, B00571. (a) Mix the base component continuously, when you add the catalyst. (b) Immediately after you mix the compound, identify the container with a label. NOTE: The compound has a application time of 4 hours at 70°F (21.1°C). Do not use the compound when its application time has ended. The use of the compound when its application time has ended, will decrease its performance. NOTE: Keep the materials that were not mixed, at a temperature between 40°F and 90°F (4.4-32.2°C). You can keep the materials that were not mixed for 12 months from the date of manufacture. 1) Write the date and the hour when the compound was mixed, 2) Write the date and hour when the application time ends. F . Apply the Hydraulic Fluid Resistant Finish SUBTASK 51-21-61-350-002 (1) Do the steps that follow to Apply the Hydraulic Fluid Resistant Finish: (a) Before you apply the hydraulic fluid resistant finish on sealants, permit the sealant to become fully dry. (b) Make sure the surface is fully clean before you apply the hydraulic fluid resistant finish. 51-21-61 (c) Apply the hydraulic fluid resistant finish with a spray gun or brush until the finish is 1 to 2 mils (0.001 to 0.002 inch) (0.025-0.051 mm) thick. NOTE: The temperature must be more than 65°F (18.3°C) and the relative humidity must be less than 85 percent for best results. (d) Apply the hydraulic fluid resistant finish on the decals. 1) Make sure you apply a 1/4 inch (6.35 mm) overlap of sealant to the decal. a) A 1/4 inch (6.35 mm) overlap of sealant to the decal will seal the edges of the decal. (e) Make sure the hydraulic fluid resistant finish is bonded to all applicable surfaces. SUBTASK 51-21-61-390-002 (2) Let the hydraulic fluid resistant finish dry for 4 hours at 65°F (18.3°C) (minimum), before you move the airplane to an open area. NOTE: A time of 14 days at 65°F (18.3°C) (minimum) is necessary before the hydraulic fluid resistant finish is fully cured.

SUBTASK 51-21-71-100-001 WARNING DO NOT GET PAINT MATERIALS AND SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH, IN YOUR EYES, ON YOUR SKIN, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THESE MATERIALS. THESE MATERIALS ARE POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Do this task: Airplane Surface Preparation for Application of Finish, TASK 51-21-00-100-801. SUBTASK 51-21-71-370-001 CAUTION DO NOT USE BMS10-21, TYPE III ON THE RADOME OR THE FIBERGLASS PANEL FOR THE HF ANTENNA. YOU CAN ONLY USE BMS10-21, TYPE IV ON THESE. (2) Prepare the BMS 10-21 Type III conductive coating, C00767, with the steps as follows: (a) Refer to the manufacturer's instructions to mix the conductive coating. (b) Fully shake each conductive coating component before you mix it. NOTE: The conductive coating is supplied in two component kits. The kits have a base component and a catalyst. (c) Put a label on the container with, the data that follows, immediately after it is mixed: 1) The date and time it was mixed, 2) The application time expiration time is as follows: a) 4 hours if the temperature is less than 81°F (27°C) b) 2 hours if the temperature is 81°F (27°C) - 100°F (38°C). (d) Do not use the conductive coating for a minimum of 30 minutes after it is mixed. 51-21-71 SUBTASK 51-21-71-370-002 (3) Apply the BMS 10-21 Type III conductive coating, C00767, compound with a paint spray gun with interchangeable nozzles, STD-1133, or paint brush, STD-1080. (a) Be sure that the temperature for the application of the coating, C00767, must be 40°F (4°C) - 100°F (38°C). NOTE: The recommended temperature is 50°F (10°C) - 90°F (32°C). (b) The dry film thickness after it has been cured must be 0.0006 ±0.0002 in. (0.0152 ±0.0051 mm). SUBTASK 51-21-71-370-003 (4) Cure the BMS 10-21 Type III conductive coating, C00767, with one of the steps that follow: (a) Let the conductive coating that is in fastener holes cure for at least 20 minutes at 70°F (21°C) - 90°F (32°C) before you install the fasteners. (b) Air dry the surface of the conductive coating for 2 hours at 60°F (16°C). (c) To cure the conductive coating quickly, apply a minimum temperature of 140°F (60°C) before you do the resistivity measurements (Figure 701). NOTE: The increased drying time as shown in Figure 701 is not a full cure. 1) The flash-off time necessary before the higher temperature cure is 15 minutes minimum at 75 ±15°F (24 ±8°C). 2) The cool-off time necessary before subsequent processing the cure is 15 minutes minimum at 75 ±15°F (24 ±8°C). SUBTASK 51-21-71-700-001 (5) Do the steps that follow to measure the resistivity of the conductive coating (Fastener-to-Conductive Surface Test Method): NOTE: The resistivity of the conductive coating after it is cured must be no more than 300,000 ohms/square. NOTE: Let the conductive coat cure for the specified time as shown in Figure 701 before you measure the conductivity. (a) If the bonding surface and the head of the fastener are covered with a finish, do the steps as follows (Figure 702): 1) Remove a sufficient quantity of the outer coating or paint to let the probes touch the conductive finish. NOTE: If it is necessary, you can push the probes through the outer coating. 2) Put the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, with the film resistance measure probe, SPL-10361, in direct contact with the bonding fastener and the conductive finish. a) Put the film resistance measure probe, SPL-10361, as shown in Figure 702. 3) Make a record of the value of the resistivity shown on the multimeter. a) The maximum permitted resistivity is 300,000 Ohms/Square. SUBTASK 51-21-71-700-002 (6) Do the steps that follow to measure the resistivity of the conductive coating on uninstalled panels (Fastener-to-Fastener Test Method): NOTE: The resistivity of the conductive coating after it is cured must be no more than 300,000 ohms/square (a) Make sure the conductive coating shows in the fastener location. 51-21-71 (b) Clean the area with solvent, B00083. (c) Install one temporary fastener at each fastener location to be measured (Figure 702). NOTE: This procedure can be used for measuring electrical resistivity of panels with covered (painted) conductive coatings when the ground fastener locations show. (d) Connect the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, probes at the two fastener locations as shown in Figure 702. (e) Measure the resistivity with the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793. 1) The maximum permitted resistivity is 300,000 Ohms/Square. (f) Remove the temporary fasteners from the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-71-700-003 (7) Use one of the procedures that follow to measure the resistivity of the conductive coating (Square Test Method) (Figure 703). NOTE: The term ohms/square is used to give the resistance in ohms of current passing from one side of a square region to the opposite side, regardless of the size of the square. NOTE: Do not use this procedure to measure the resistivity of conductive finishes when the surface is covered (painted). (a) If the surface resistivity measurement probe, SPL-7885, is used on the conductive coating surface, do the steps that follow: 1) Put the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, with the surface resistivity measurement probe, SPL-7885, in direct contact with the conductive coating surface. 2) Measure the resistivity the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793. a) The measured value multiplied by 10 gives the value of resistivity in ohms/square. NOTE: The term ohms/square is used because it gives the resistance in ohms of current passing from one side of a square region to the opposite side, regardless of the size of the square. NOTE: The maximum permitted resistivity is 300,000 Ohms/square. (b) If the 3M 1181 copper foil tape, G50630, is used on the conductive coating surface, do the steps that follow: 1) Put two pieces of 3M 1181 copper foil tape, G50630, (of equal length (L)) parallel to each other on the conductive coating surface. 2) The two strips of 3M 1181 copper foil tape, G50630, must be put parallel to each other a distance of one tenth the length of the two strips (0.1L ±5 percent). 3) Push the two strips of 3M 1181 copper foil tape, G50630, against the conductive coating. 4) Measure the resistivity with the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793. a) The measured value multiplied by 10 gives the value of resistivity in ohms/square. NOTE: The term ohms/square is used because it gives the resistance in ohms of current passing from one side of a square region to the opposite side, regardless of the size of the square. NOTE: The maximum permitted resistivity is 300,000 Ohms/square. 5) The measured value multiplied by 10 gives the value of resistivity in ohms/square. 51-21-71 6) Remove the 3M 1181 copper foil tape, G50630, from the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-71-370-004 (8) Do the steps that follow if the resistivity of the conductive coating is more than 300,000 ohms/square: (a) Use 240 grit or finer abrasive cloth, B00102, paper to remove the conductive coating. NOTE: If the abrasive cloth, B00102, is not available, use a abrasive mat, G00251, or 240 grit or finer abrasive paper, G50077, as an alternate. (b) Remove the remaining particles with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, that is moist with solvent, B00083. (c) Dry the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, before the solvent is dry. (d) Do the steps to apply a new layer of conductive coating. (e) Do the steps to cure the conductive coating. (f) Do the steps to measure the resistivity of the new layer of conductive coating.

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-21-71-100-003 WARNING DO NOT GET THIS MATERIAL IN YOUR MOUTH, EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. CLEAN BARE SKIN FULLY AFTER YOU USE THIS MATERIAL. THIS MATERIAL CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Do this task: (Airplane Surface Preparation for Application of Finish, TASK 51-21-00-100-801). SUBTASK 51-21-71-370-010 (2) Prepare the BMS 10–21 Type IV conductive coating, C50219, with the steps as follows: (a) Refer to the manufacturer's instructions to mix the conductive coating. (b) Fully shake each conductive coating component before you mix it. NOTE: The conductive coating is supplied in two component kits. The kits have a base component and a catalyst. SUBTASK 51-21-71-370-011 (3) Apply the BMS 10–21 Type IV conductive coating, C50219, compound with a paint spray gun with interchangeable nozzles, STD-1133, or paint brush, STD-1080. (a) Be sure that the temperature for the application of the coating, C50219, must be 40°F (4°C) to 100°F (38°C). The preferred temperature is 50°F (10°C) to 90°F (32°C). (b) The dry film thickness after it has been cured must be 0.0008 ±0.0002 in. (0.0203 ±0.0051 mm). SUBTASK 51-21-71-370-012 (4) Cure the BMS 10–21 Type IV conductive coating, C50219, with the steps that follow: (a) Allow the conductive coating that is in fastener holes cure for at least 20 minutes at 70°F (21°C) to 90°F (32°C) before you install the fasteners. (b) Heat-cure the anti-static coating before taking resistivity measurements or overcoating. 1) The flash-off time necessary before the higher temperature cure is 15 minutes minimum at 75 ±15°F (24 ±8°C). 2) Apply heat to cure the conductive coating before you do the resistivity measurements as shown in (Figure 701). NOTE: The increased drying time as shown in Figure 701 is not a full cure. a) Do not cure above 160°F (71°C). b) Do not cure at temperatures of 120°F (49°C) or above for longer than 2 hours. 3) The cool-off time necessary before subsequent processing the cure is 15 minutes minimum at 75 ±15°F (24 ±8°C). 51-21-71 SUBTASK 51-21-71-700-007 (5) Do the steps that follow to measure the resistivity of the conductive coating (Fastener-to-Conductive Surface Test Method): NOTE: The resistivity of the conductive coating after it is cured must be no less than 1 Megohm/square or more than 100 Megohms/square. NOTE: Let the conductive coat cure for the specified time as shown in (Figure 701) before you measure the conductivity. (a) If the bonding surface and the head of the fastener are covered with a finish, (Figure 702) do the steps as follows: 1) Remove a sufficient quantity of the outer coating or paint to let the probes touch the conductive finish. NOTE: If it is necessary, you can push the probes through the outer coating. 2) Put the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, with the film resistance measure probe, SPL-10361, in direct contact with the bonding fastener and the conductive finish. a) Put the film resistance measure probe, SPL-10361, as shown in Figure 702. 3) Make a record of the value of the resistivity shown on the multimeter. a) The minimum permitted resistivity is no less than 1 Megohm/square. b) The maximum permitted resistivity is 100 Megohms/square. SUBTASK 51-21-71-700-008 (6) Do the steps that follow to measure the resistivity of the conductive coating on uninstalled panels (Fastener-to-Fastener Test Method): NOTE: The resistivity of the conductive coating after it is cured must be no less than 1 Megohm/square or more than 100 Megohms/square. (a) Make sure the conductive coating shows in the fastener location. (b) Clean the area with solvent, B00083. (c) Install one temporary fastener at each fastener location to be measured. (Figure 702). NOTE: This procedure can be used for measuring electrical resistivity of panels with covered (painted) conductive coatings when the ground fastener locations show. (d) Connect the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, probes at the two fastener locations as shown in (Figure 702). (e) Measure the resistivity with the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793. 1) The minimum permitted resistivity is no less than 1 Megohm/square. 2) The maximum permitted resistivity is 100 Megohms/square. (f) Remove the temporary fasteners from the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-71-700-009 (7) Use one of the procedures that follow to measure the resistivity of the conductive coating (Square Test Method): (Figure 703) NOTE: The term ohms/square is used to give the resistance in ohms of current passing from one side of a square region to the opposite side, regardless of the size of the square. NOTE: Do not use this procedure to measure the resistivity of conductive finishes when the surface is covered (painted). 51-21-71 (a) If the surface resistivity measurement probe, SPL-7885, is used on the conductive coating surface, do the steps that follow: 1) Put the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, with the surface resistivity measurement probe, SPL-7885 in direct contact with the conductive coating surface. 2) Measure the resistivity the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793. a) The measured value multiplied by 10 gives the value of resistivity in ohms/square. NOTE: The term ohms/square is used because it gives the resistance in ohms of current passing from one side of a square region to the opposite side, regardless of the size of the square. NOTE: The minimum resistivity is no less than 1 Megohm/square or a maximum resistivity of 100 Megohms/square. (b) If the 3M 1181 copper foil tape, G50630, is used on the conductive coating surface, do the steps that follow: 1) Put two pieces of 3M 1181 copper foil tape, G50630, (of equal length (L)) parallel to each other on the conductive coating surface. 2) The two strips of 3M 1181 copper foil tape, G50630, must be put parallel to each other a distance of one tenth the length of the two strips (0.1L ±5 percent). 3) Push the two strips of 3M 1181 copper foil tape, G50630, against the conductive coating. 4) Measure the resistivity with the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793. a) The measured value multiplied by 10 gives the value of resistivity in ohms/square. NOTE: The term ohms/square is used because it gives the resistance in ohms of current passing from one side of a square region to the opposite side, regardless of the size of the square. NOTE: The minimum resistivity is no less than 1 Megohm/square or a maximum resistivity of 100 Megohms/square. 5) The measured value multiplied by 10 gives the value of resistivity in ohms/square. 6) Remove the 3M 1181 copper foil tape, G50630, from the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-71-370-013 (8) Do the steps that follow if the resistivity of the conductive coating is less than 1 Megohm/Square: (a) Use 240 grit or finer abrasive cloth, B00102, paper to remove the conductive coating. NOTE: If the abrasive cloth, B00102, is not available, use a abrasive mat, G00251, or 240 grit or finer abrasive paper, G50077, as an alternate. (b) Remove the remaining particles with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, that is moist with solvent, B00083. (c) Dry the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, before the solvent is dry. (d) Do the steps to apply a new layer of conductive coating. (e) Do the steps to cure the conductive coating. (f) Do the steps to measure the resistivity of the new layer of conductive coating. 51-21-71 SUBTASK 51-21-71-370-014 (9) Do the steps that follow if the resistivity of the conductive coating is more than 100 Megohms/Square: (a) Cure at 140°F (60°C) to 160°F (71°C) for 60 to 70 minutes. (b) Remeasure resistivity. (c) If the resistivity is more then 100 Megohms/Square, do the steps that follow: 1) Use 240 grit or finer abrasive cloth, B00102, paper to remove the conductive coating. NOTE: If the abrasive cloth, B00102, is not available, use a abrasive mat, G00251, or 240 grit or finer abrasive paper, G50077, as an alternate. 2) Remove the remaining particles with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, that is moist with solvent, B00083. 3) Dry the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034, before the solvent is dry. 4) Do the steps to apply a new layer of conductive coating. 5) Do the steps to cure the conductive coating. 6) Do the steps to measure the resistivity of the new layer of conductive coating.

E. Prepare to Apply the BMS10-79 Primer

SUBTASK 51-21-72-950-001 (1) Mask all areas that will not be coated with BMS10-79 primer. (a) Attach the tags that follow to the left control wheel in the flight deck. 51-21-72 1) "PITOT PROBES COVERED" tag, G02447 2) "STATIC PORTS COVERED" tag, G02444 3) A red tag labeled “AOA SENSORS COVERED”. (b) Put a pitot probe cover, COM-1503, on the pitot probe. (c) Apply Scotch Flatback Masking T ape 250, G00270, on the static ports. (d) Do the steps that follow to cover the Angle of Attack (AOA) sensors: 1) Cover the AOA sensors with masking tape, G51270. a) Apply masking tape, G51270, over the blade, plate, and blade-to-plate gap. NOTE: This is to allow easier removal of 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. 2) Cover the masking tape, G51270, with 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. a) Shingle the 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291, from the blade-to-plate gap up to the blade tip until all of the masking tape, G51270, is covered. SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-009 (2) Prepare unsealed anodized aluminum with the steps that follow: (a) Remove small amounts of contamination that is oily with the steps that follow: 1) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with water. 2) Dry the surface with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. (b) Remove small amounts of oily contamination with the steps that follow: 1) Solvent clean the surface. a) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with Series 84 solvent, B01004. b) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. <1> Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-010 (3) Prepare sealed anodized aluminum with the steps that follow: (a) If the surface becomes contaminated, solvent clean the surface. 1) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with Series 84 solvent, B01004. 2) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-023 (4) If other than anodized aluminum, do steps that follow: (a) If the surface becomes contaminated, solvent clean the surface. 1) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with Series 84 solvent, B01004. 2) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-021 (5) Prepare surfaces with paint with one of the methods listed in Table 701.
