Table 703/51-21-72-993-801 BMS10-79, Type II and Type III, Primer Dry Film Thickness Requirements SUBSTRATE NUMBER OF COATS MINIMUM DRY FILM THICKNESS (MILS) MAXIMUM DRY FILM THICKNESS (MILS) MAXIMUM DRY FILM THICKNESS FOR LOCALIZED AREAS OF REWORK, OVERLAP , AND OVERSPRAY (MILS) Metal 1 0.5 1.0 2.0 2 1.1 2.1 3.0 Composite or Plastic 1 0.3 *[1] 0.8 -- 2 0.7 *[1] 1.7 -- *[1] For optimum coating performance, the recommended target thickness for one coat is 0.3 mil. 1) If the dry film thickness exceeds the limits in Table 703, do the steps that follow: a) Sand the areas where the dry film thickness exceeds the limits in Table 703 with one of the steps that follow: 51-21-72 <1> 220-grit or finer sandpaper, G50260, silicone-free abrasive <2> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220, very fine, aluminum oxide <3> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish abrasive pad, G51319, very fine, Grade A, aluminum oxide <4> Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose abrasive hand pad, G51193, very fine, aluminum oxide <5> Sand the surface until the thickness is within the limits in Table 703. b) Solvent clean the area. <1> Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. <2> Immediately wipe the surface with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. <a> Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface.

G. Minor Rework

SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-015 (1) For areas that have minor damage and the substrate is not exposed, do the steps that follow: (a) Solvent clean the area. 1) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. 2) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. (b) Sand the surface where the area is damaged with one of the abrasive materials that follow: 1) 220-grit or finer sandpaper, G50260, silicone-free abrasive 2) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220, very fine, aluminum oxide 3) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish abrasive pad, G51319, very fine, Grade A, aluminum oxide 4) Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose abrasive hand pad, G51193, very fine, aluminum oxide. (c) Solvent clean the area to remove sanding dust. 1) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. 2) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. (d) Apply the primer to the area. (e) Dry and cure the primer. SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-016 (2) For areas with minor damage and the composite or plastic substrate is exposed, do the steps that follow: (a) Solvent clean the area. 1) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. 2) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. (b) Sand the surface where the area is damaged with one of the abrasive materials that follow: 51-21-72 1) 220-grit or finer sandpaper, G50260, silicone-free abrasive 2) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220, very fine, aluminum oxide 3) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish abrasive pad, G51319, very fine, Grade A, aluminum oxide 4) Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose abrasive hand pad, G51193, very fine, aluminum oxide. (c) Solvent clean the area to remove sanding dust. 1) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. 2) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. (d) Apply the primer to the area. (e) Dry and cure the primer. SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-017 (3) For areas with minor damage and the metal substrate is exposed, do the steps that follow: (a) For pretreated Titanium or Corrosion Resistant Steel (CRES) surfaces, and aluminum surfaces with chemical conversion coating, do the steps that follow: 1) Solvent clean the area. a) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. b) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. <1> Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. 2) Sand the surface where the area is damaged with one of the abrasive materials that follow: a) 220-grit or finer sandpaper, G50260, silicone-free abrasive b) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220, very fine, aluminum oxide c) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish abrasive pad, G51319, very fine, Grade A, aluminum oxide d) Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose abrasive hand pad, G51193, very fine, aluminum oxide. 3) Solvent clean the area to remove sanding dust. a) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. b) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. <1> Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. 4) Apply the primer. 5) Dry and cure the primer. (b) For anodized areas that are less than 5% of the required coating area for the part, do the steps that follow: 1) Solvent clean the area. a) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. b) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. <1> Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. 51-21-72 2) Sand the surface where the area is damaged with one of the abrasive materials that follow: a) 220-grit or finer sandpaper, G50260, silicone-free abrasive b) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220, very fine, aluminum oxide c) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish abrasive pad, G51319, very fine, Grade A, aluminum oxide d) Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose abrasive hand pad, G51193, very fine, aluminum oxide. 3) Solvent clean the area to remove sanding dust. a) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. b) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. <1> Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. 4) Apply Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862, to bare areas (TASK 51-21-41-370-802). 5) Immediately before applying the primer, wipe the surface with a new tack rag, G50123. 6) Apply the primer. 7) Dry and cure the primer.

H. Major Rework

SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-018 (1) For major rework of composite or plastic surfaces, do the steps that follow: NOTE: Major rework requires the removal of the primer. (a) Sand the surface to remove the primer with one of the abrasive materials that follow: 1) 220-grit or finer sandpaper, G50260, silicone-free abrasive 2) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220, very fine, aluminum oxide 3) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish abrasive pad, G51319, very fine, Grade A, aluminum oxide 4) Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose abrasive hand pad, G51193, very fine, aluminum oxide. (b) Solvent clean the area. 1) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with Series 87 solvent, B01007. 2) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. (c) Prepare the surface, if necessary (TASK 51-21-21-100-802). (d) Immediately before applying the primer, wipe the surface with a new tack rag, G50123. (e) Apply the primer. (f) Dry and cure the primer. SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-019 (2) For major rework of metal parts, do the steps that follow: (a) Sand the surface to remove the primer with one of the abrasive materials that follow: 1) 220-grit or finer sandpaper, G50260, silicone-free abrasive 51-21-72 2) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220, very fine, aluminum oxide 3) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish abrasive pad, G51319, very fine, Grade A, aluminum oxide 4) Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose abrasive hand pad, G51193, very fine, aluminum oxide. (b) Solvent clean the area. 1) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with Series 87 solvent, B01007. 2) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. (c) Prepare the surface, if necessary (TASK 51-21-21-100-802). (d) Immediately before applying the primer, wipe the surface with a new tack rag, G50123. (e) Apply the primer. (f) Dry and cure the primer.

51-21-72-370-802BMS10-103, Type 1, Primer - ApplicationPDF p. 283

3. BMS10-103, Type 1, Primer - Application

A. General

(1) This procedure has steps to do the following: (a) Prepare to apply the BMS10-103, Type 1, Primer (b) Apply the BMS10-103, Type 1, Primer (c) Minor re-work for composite surfaces (substrate exposed) (d) Minor re-work for titanium and CRES surfaces (substrate exposed) (e) Major re-work for composite surfaces (f) Major re-work for titanium and CRES surfaces. (2) recommends you apply the BMS10-103, Type 1, primer when the ambient air temperature is between 40°F (4°C) and 100°F (38°C). (a) Contact the paint manufacturer for guidance if you will apply the paint outside the recommended temperature range.

B. References

Reference Title 51-21-41 P/B 701 CHEMICAL CONVERSION COATING - CLEANING/PAINTING

C. Tools/Equipment

NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. E. Prepare to Apply the BMS10-103, Type 1, Primer

SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-004 (1) Mask all areas that will not be coated with the primer. (a) Attach the tags that follow to the left control wheel in the flight deck. 1) "PITOT PROBES COVERED" tag, G02447 2) "STATIC PORTS COVERED" tag, G02444 3) A red tag labeled “AOA SENSORS COVERED”. (b) Put a pitot probe cover, COM-1503, on the pitot probe. (c) Apply Scotch Flatback Masking T ape 250, G00270, on the static ports. (d) Do the steps that follow to cover the Angle of Attack (AOA) sensors. 1) Cover the angle-of-attack sensors with PG-777 solvent-resistant masking tape. a) Apply PG-777 over the blade, plate, and blade-to-plate gap. NOTE: This is to allow easier removal of 3M 425 aluminum tape. 2) Cover the PG-777 solvent-resistant masking tape with 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. a) Shingle the aluminum foil tape from the blade-to-plate gap up to the blade tip until all of the masking tape is covered. SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-001 (2) For bare exterior composite or plastic surfaces, do the steps that follow. NOTE: These steps are not applicable to BMS8-267 or BMS8-341, Type II, Form 2, surfaces. 51-21-72 (a) Abrade the surface with 100-grit or finer aluminum oxide, silicone free, abrasive paper or cloth. 1) Use a pneumatic sander to abrade the surface. (b) Abrade the surface with one of the abrasive pads that follow and a pneumatic sander. 1) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 2) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide 3) Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide. (c) Remove sanding residue with compressed air, if necessary. (d) Solvent clean the surface. 1) Wipe the surface to remove loose soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, or oil, if necessary. 2) Use one of the methods that follow to solvent clean the surface. a) Wet a cotton wiper, G00034, or equivalent with Series 87 solvent, B01007, and wipe the surface. b) Wipe the surface with a pre-saturated cloth, G51951, with Series 87 solvent, B01007. NOTE: Pre-saturated wipers are only approved if you will paint after final cleaning. c) Immediately wipe the surface with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034, to remove excess solvent. <1> Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-002 (3) For BMS10-79 or BMS10-103 primed surfaces that have dried for less than 48 hours, do the steps that follow. (a) If the surface becomes contaminated, solvent clean the area. NOTE: If the contamination is particulate, you can use clean, compressed air or a new tack rag, G50123. 1) Wipe the surface to remove loose soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, or oil, if necessary. 2) Use one of the methods that follow to solvent clean the surface. a) Wet a cotton wiper, G00034, or equivalent with Series 85 solvent, B01005, and wipe the surface. b) Wipe the surface with a pre-saturated cloth, G51951, with Series 85 solvent, B01005. c) Wipe the surface with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034, to remove excess solvent. <1> Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-003 (4) For BMS10-79 or BMS10-103 primed surfaces that have dried for more than 48 hours, or if the primer has been force-dried for any amount of time, use one of the methods that follow. (a) Method 1: BMS10-79 or BMS10-103 1) Solvent clean the surface. a) Wipe the surface to remove loose soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, or oil. 51-21-72 b) Use one of the methods that follow to solvent clean the surface. <1> Wet a cotton wiper, G00034, or equivalent with Series 81 solvent, B01001, and wipe the surface. <2> Wipe the surface with a pre-saturated cloth, G51951, with Series 81 solvent, B01001. <3> Wipe the surface with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034, to remove excess solvent. <a> Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. 2) Sand the surface with one of the abrasive pads or abrasive paper that follow. a) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 b) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide c) Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide d) An abrasive cloth, B00102, 100-grit or finer, wet or dry. 3) Wipe the surface to remove loose soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, or oil, if necessary. 4) Use one of the methods that follow to solvent clean the surface. NOTE: This is to remove sanding dust. a) Wet a cotton wiper, G00034, or equivalent, or brush, G00215, with Series 85 solvent, B01005, and wipe the surface. b) Use one of the methods that follow to solvent clean the surface. <1> Wet a cotton wiper, G00034, or equivalent, or brush, G00215 with Series 85 solvent, B01005, and wipe the surface. <2> Wipe the surface with a pre-saturated cloth, G51951, with Series 85 solvent, B01005. NOTE: Pre-saturated wipers are only approved if you will paint after final cleaning. <3> Immediately wipe the surface with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034, to remove excess solvent. <a> Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. 5) Use compressed air or a new tack rag, G50123, if necessary. 6) If the assembly has bare titanium fastener heads or bare CRES fastener heads, to the steps that follow. a) Wipe the surface with a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with alcohol, B50073 (ASTM D770). b) Wipe the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034. c) Apply conversion coating to the bare fastener heads (CHEMICAL CONVERSION COATING - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-41/701). NOTE: It is acceptable if the conversion coating touches the adjacent surfaces. 51-21-72 F . Apply the BMS10-103, Type 1, Primer SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-004 (1) Immediately before applying the primer, wipe the surface with a new tack rag, G50123, or use clean, compressed air. NOTE: This is to remove any particulate contamination. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-006 (2) Apply the BMS10-103, Type 1, primer, C00766, in a continuous coat that is free of runs, wrinkles, and pinholes. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-008 (3) Dry the BMS10-103, Grade A primer using Table 704. (a) Air dry the BMS10-103, Grade A primer for a minimum of 30 minutes at a minimum of 65°F (18°C) before over-coating or re-coating. Table 704/51-21-72-993-803 BMS10-103, Grade A, Dry Times TEMPERATURE MINIMUM DRY TIME BEFORE MASKING MINIMUM DRY TIME BEFORE HANDLING MAXIMUM FORCE DRYING TIME 65°F (18°C) minimum air dry 2 hours 6 hours N/A 75°F (24°C) minimum air dry 2 hours 4 hours N/A SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-009 (4) Dry the BMS10-103, Grade E, primer using Table 705. (a) Air dry the BMS10-103, Grade E primer for a minimum of 30 minutes at a minimum of 65°F (18°C). Table 705/51-21-72-993-804 BMS10-103, Grade E, Dry Times TEMPERATURE MINIMUM DRY TIME BEFORE MASKING MINIMUM DRY TIME BEFORE HANDLING MAXIMUM FORCE DRYING TIME 65°F (18°C) minimum air dry 5 hours 7.5 hours N/A 75°F (24°C) minimum air dry 3 hours 5 hours N/A SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-007 (5) Make sure that the dry film thickness is within the limits in Table 706. (a) Measure the dry film thickness after the coating has dried beyond the minimum time before masking (Table 704, Table 705). G. Minor Re-Work for Composite Surfaces (Substrate Exposed)

SUBTASK 51-21-72-110-001 (1) Solvent clean the damaged area. (a) Wipe the surface to remove loose soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, or oil. (b) Use one of the methods that follow to solvent clean the surface. 51-21-72 1) Wet a cotton wiper, G00034, or equivalent with Series 83 solvent, B01003, and wipe the surface. 2) Wipe the surface with a pre-saturated cloth, G51951, with Series 83 solvent, B01003. 3) Wipe the surface with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034, to remove excess sealant. SUBTASK 51-21-72-120-001 (2) Sand the solvent with one of the abrasives that follow. (a) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 (b) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide (c) Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide (d) An abrasive cloth, B00102, 100-grit or finer, wet or dry. SUBTASK 51-21-72-110-002 (3) Solvent clean the surface to remove sanding dust. (a) Wipe the surface to remove loose soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, or oil. (b) Use one of the methods that follow to solvent clean the surface. 1) Wet a cotton wiper, G00034, or equivalent with Series 87 solvent, B01007, and wipe the surface. 2) Wipe the surface with a pre-saturated cloth, G51951, with Series 87 solvent, B01007. 3) Wipe the surface with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034, to remove excess sealant. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-005 (4) Immediately before applying the primer, use a tack rag, G50123, or compressed air. NOTE: This is to remove particulate contamination. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-010 (5) Prepare the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-011 (6) Apply the primer to the damaged area.

H. Minor Re-Work for Titanium and CRES Surfaces (Substrate Exposed)

SUBTASK 51-21-72-110-003 (1) Solvent clean the damaged area. (a) Wipe the surface to remove loose soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, or oil. (b) Use one of the methods that follow to solvent clean the surface. 1) Wet a cotton wiper, G00034, or equivalent with Series 80 solvent, B50268, and wipe the surface. 2) Wipe the surface with a pre-saturated cloth, G51951, with Series 80 solvent, B50268. 3) Wipe the surface with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034, to remove excess sealant. SUBTASK 51-21-72-120-002 (2) Sand the solvent with one of the abrasives that follow. (a) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 51-21-72 (b) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide (c) Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide (d) An abrasive cloth, B00102, 100-grit or finer, wet or dry. SUBTASK 51-21-72-110-004 (3) Solvent clean the surface to remove sanding dust. (a) Wipe the surface to remove loose soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, or oil. (b) Use one of the methods that follow to solvent clean the surface. 1) Wet a cotton wiper, G00034, or equivalent with Series 84 solvent, B01004, and wipe the surface. 2) Wipe the surface with a pre-saturated cloth, G51951, with Series 84 solvent, B01004. 3) Wipe the surface with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034, to remove excess sealant. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-012 (4) Apply the conversion coating (CHEMICAL CONVERSION COATING - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-41/701). SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-006 (5) Immediately before applying the primer, use a tack rag, G50123, or compressed air. NOTE: This is to remove particulate contamination. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-013 (6) Apply the BMS10-103, Type 1, primer, C00766, to the damaged area. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-014 (7) Dry and cure the primer.

I. Major Re-Work for Composite Surfaces

SUBTASK 51-21-72-120-003 (1) Sand the solvent with one of the abrasives that follow. (a) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 (b) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide (c) Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide (d) An abrasive cloth, B00102, 100-grit or finer, wet or dry SUBTASK 51-21-72-110-005 (2) Solvent clean the surface or use compressed air or a tack rag, G50123. (a) Wipe the surface to remove loose soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, or oil. (b) Use one of the methods that follow to solvent clean the surface. 1) Wet a cotton wiper, G00034, or equivalent with Series 87 solvent, B01007, and wipe the surface. 2) Wipe the surface with a pre-saturated cloth, G51951, with Series 87 solvent, B01007. 3) Wipe the surface with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034, to remove excess sealant. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. 51-21-72 SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-007 (3) Immediately before applying the primer, wipe the surface with a new tack rag, G50123, or use compressed air. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-015 (4) Apply the BMS10-103, Type 1, primer, C00766. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-016 (5) Dry and cure the primer.

J. Major Re-Work for Titanium and CRES Surfaces

SUBTASK 51-21-72-120-004 (1) Sand the solvent with one of the abrasives that follow. (a) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 (b) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide (c) Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide (d) An abrasive cloth, B00102, 100-grit or finer, wet or dry. SUBTASK 51-21-72-110-006 (2) Solvent clean the surface or use compressed air or a tack rag, G50123. (a) Wipe the surface to remove loose soil, excess grease, hydraulic fluid, or oil. (b) Use one of the methods that follow to solvent clean the surface. 1) Wet a cotton wiper, G00034, or equivalent with Series 84 solvent, B01004, and wipe the surface. 2) Wipe the surface with a pre-saturated cloth, G51951, with Series 84 solvent, B01004. 3) Wipe the surface with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034, to remove excess sealant. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-008 (3) Immediately before applying the primer, wipe the surface with a new tack rag, G50123, or use compressed air. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-017 (4) Apply the BMS10-103, Type 1, primer, C00766. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-018 (5) Dry and cure the primer.

51-21-72-370-803BMS10-72 Primer - ApplicationPDF p. 290

4. BMS10-72 Primer - Application

A. General

(1) This procedure has steps to do the following: (a) Prepare to apply BMS10-72 primer. (b) Apply BMS10-72 primer. (2) recommends that you apply BMS10-72 primer when the ambient air temperature is between 65°F (18°C) and 95°F (35°C). 51-21-72 (a) Contact the paint manufacturer for guidance if you will apply BMS10-72 primer outside the recommended temperature range. (3) recommends that you apply BMS10-72 primer when the relative humidity is less than 70%. (a) Contact the paint manufacturer for guidance if you will apply BMS10-72 primer when the relative humidity is more than 70%.

D. Prepare to the BMS10-72 Primer Application

SUBTASK 51-21-72-950-002 (1) Mask the surface adjacent to the area you will apply primer. (a) Attach the tags that follow to the left control wheel in the flight deck: 1) "PITOT PROBES COVERED" tag, G02447 2) "STATIC PORTS COVERED" tag, G02444 3) A red tag labeled “AOA SENSORS COVERED”. (b) Put a pitot probe cover, COM-1503, on the pitot probe. (c) Apply Scotch Flatback Masking T ape 250, G00270, on the static ports. (d) Do the steps that follow to cover the Angle-Of-Attack (AOA) sensors: 1) Cover the AOA sensors with PG-777 solvent-resistant masking tape. a) Apply PG-777 over the blade, plate, and blade-to-plate gap. NOTE: This is to allow easier removal of 3M 425 aluminum tape. 2) Cover the PG-777 solvent-resistant masking tape with 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. a) Shingle the aluminum foil tape from the blade-to-plate gap up to the blade tip until all of the masking tape is covered. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-019 (2) Mix the BMS10-72, Type VIII primer coating, C50084, or BMS10-72, Type IX primer coating, C50085, or BMS10-72, Type X primer coating, C50318, using the manufacturer's instructions (Table 707). NOTE: The BMS10-72, Type VIII primer has a base component and a curing solution component. NOTE: The BMS10-72, Type IX and Type X primers have a base component, a curing solution component, and a thinner component. Table 707/51-21-72-993-806 BMS10-72 Primer Mixing MATERIAL DESIGNATION RATIO PARTS BY VOLUME INDUCTION PERIOD POT LIFE PRC-DeSoto BMS10-72, Type VIII Base: CA7700AX Curing Solution: CA7700BE 1 1 *[1] 60 minutes at T ≥ 65°F (18°C) 90 minutes at T ≤ 65°F (18°C) 3 hours at T ≤ 80°F (27°C) *[2] PRC-DeSoto BMS10-72, Type VIII Base: CA7700AX Curing Solution: CA7700BX 1 1 *[1] 60 minutes at T ≥ 65°F (18°C) 90 minutes at T ≤ 65°F (18°C) 4 hours at T ≤ 80°F (27°C) *[3] 51-21-72 Table 707/51-21-72-993-806 BMS10-72 Primer Mixing (Continued) Akzo Nobel BMS10-72, Type IX and Type X, Composition C Base: 10P20-44M Curing Solution: EC-291 Thinner: TR-114 2 1 1 None 4 hours at T ≤ 80°F (27°C) *[3] PRC-DeSoto BMS10-72, Type VIII, Type IX and Type X, Composition NC Base: CA 7502A Curing Solution: CA 7502B Thinner: CA 7502C 4 4 1 60 minutes at T ≥ 69°F (21°C) 120 minutes at T ≤69°F (21°C) 4 hours at T ≤ 80°F (27°C) *[3] Akzo Nobel BMS10-72, Type X, Composition NC2 *[4] Base: 2111P001 Curing Solution: CS6018 Thinner: TR-114 2 1 1 15 minutes 4 hours at T ≤ 80°F (27°C) *[3] *[1] Use entire kits when mixing. *[2] The pot life is 1.5 hours when the temperature is between 81°F (27°C) and 95°F (35°C). *[3] The pot life is 2 hours when the temperature is between 81°F (27°C) and 95°F (35°C). *[4] Approved for use only under the basecoat clearcoat paint system. (a) Add the curing solution component with the steps that follow (Table 707): 1) Add the curing solution component while continuously mixing. 2) Add the curing solution component at a rate less than 15 seconds per gallon. (b) If you are mixing BMS10-72, Type IX or Type X primer, do the steps that follow: 1) Immediately after adding the curing solution component, add the thinner component (Table 707). a) Add the thinner component while continuously stirring. b) Add the thinner component at a rate less than 15 seconds per gallon. (c) Mix the primer solution every 30 minutes before you apply the primer.

SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-020 (1) Spray apply the BMS10-72, Type VIII primer coating, C50084, or BMS10-72, Type IX primer coating, C50085, or BMS10-72, Type X primer coating, C50318. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-021 (2) Cure the primer in accordance with Table 708. Table 708/51-21-72-993-807 BMS10-72 Primer Curing Temperatures and Times MATERIAL DESIGNATION DRY TIME TO RECOAT OR OVERCOAT*[2] RECOMMENDED DRY TIME TO TAPE*[1] PRC-DeSoto BMS10-72, Type VIII Base: CA7700AX Curing Solution: CA7700BE 2 hours minimum to 48 hours maximum *[3]*[4] 2 hours and 30 minutes at 77°F (25°C) 51-21-72 Table 708/51-21-72-993-807 BMS10-72 Primer Curing Temperatures and Times (Continued) PRC-DeSoto BMS10-72, Type VIII Base: CA7700AX Curing Solution: CA7700BX 2 hours minimum to 48 hours maximum *[3]*[4] 2 hours and 30 minutes at 77°F (25°C) Akzo Nobel BMS10-72, Type IX and Type X, Composition C Base: 10P20-44M Curing Solution: EC-291 Thinner: TR-114 2 hours minimum to 48 hours maximum between 75°F (24°C) and 120°F (49°C) 2 hours and 30 minutes at 77°F (25°C) PRC-DeSoto BMS10-72, Type VIII, Type IX and Type X, Composition NC Base: CA 7502A Curing solution: CA 7502B Thinner: CA 7502C Curing Solution: CA 7502B Thinner: CA 7502C 2 hours minimum to 24 hours maximum between 65°F (18°C) and 89°F (32°C) *[5]*[6] 2 hours and 30 minutes at 77°F (25°C) Akzo Nobel BMS10-72, Type X, Composition NC2 Base: 2111P001 Curing Solution: CS6018 Thinner: TR-114 2 hours minimum to 48 hours maximum between 75°F (24°C) and 120°F (49°C) 2 hours and 30 minutes at 77°F (25°C) *[1] Dry-to-tape times are approximate. T ape after removal shall have no visible effects on the primer film. *[2] If the maximum dry time is exceeded, reactivate the surface. *[3] If the primer is dried at temperatures warmer than 120°F (49°C), reactivate the surface. *[4] Cure primer at a minimum temperature of 95°F (35°C) for at least 60 minutes within 2 hours of primer application. *[5] The overcoat time can be reduced to 30 minutes at 65°F (18°C) to 95°F (35°C) for small areas. *[6] If the primer has been dried for more than 60 minutes at temperatures 90°F (32°C) to 104°F (40°C), then the overcoat time is 1.5 to 24 hours. If monocoat is to be applied, and the primer has been dried for 1 to 4 hours at 105°F (41°C) to 120°F (49°C), then the total time allowed at temperatures 65°F (18°C) to 89°F (32°C) is 12 hours. If basecoat is to be applied, and the primer has been dried for 1 to 2 hours at 105°F (41°C) to 120°F (49°C), then the total time allowed at temperatures 65°F (18°C) to 89°F (32°C) is 24 hours. (a) Within 2 hours of the application of primer, cure the primer at a minimum of 95°F (35°C) for a minimum of 60 minutes. (b) If the dry time to recoat or overcoat is more than the requirements in Table 708, do the steps that follow to reactivate the surface: 1) Solvent clean the surface, if necessary to remove contamination. a) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, or one of the abrasives that follow wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005: <1> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 <2> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide <3> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide. b) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. <1> Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. 2) Sand the surface. a) Start sanding with one of the abrasives that follow: 51-21-72 <1> Aluminum oxide/zirconium oxide abrasive paper, stearate-free, 100-grit to 220-grit <2> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220, 100-grit to 220-grit <3> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide, 100-grit to 220-grit <4> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide, 100-grit to 220-grit. b) Finish sanding with one of the abrasives that follow: <1> Aluminum oxide/zirconium oxide abrasive paper, stearate-free, 220-grit or finer <2> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220, 220-grit or finer <3> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide, 220-grit or finer <4> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide, 220-grit or finer. 3) Solvent clean the surface, if it is necessary to remove contamination. NOTE: This is to remove sanding dust. a) Use a wiper, G50262, or one of the abrasives that follow wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005: <1> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 <2> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide <3> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide. b) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry wiper, G50262. <1> Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. 4) Wipe the surface with a tack rag, G50123. 5) Apply a coat of BMS10-72, Type VIII primer coating, C50084, or BMS10-72, Type IX primer coating, C50085, or BMS10-72, Type X primer coating, C50318, to the surface. (c) If the temperature for drying to recoat or overcoat is warmer than 120°F (49°C), do the steps that follow to reactivate the surface: 1) Solvent clean the surface, if necessary to remove contamination. a) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, or one of the abrasives that follow wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005: <1> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 <2> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide <3> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide. b) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. <1> Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. 2) Sand the surface. a) Start sanding with one of the abrasives that follow: 51-21-72 <1> Aluminum oxide/zirconium oxide abrasive paper, stearate-free, 100-grit to 220-grit <2> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220, 100-grit to 220-grit <3> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide, 100-grit to 220-grit <4> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide, 100-grit to 220-grit. b) Finish sanding with one of the abrasives that follow: <1> Aluminum oxide/zirconium oxide abrasive paper, stearate-free, 220-grit or finer <2> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220, 220-grit or finer <3> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide, 220-grit or finer <4> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide, 220-grit or finer. 3) Solvent clean the surface, if it is necessary to remove contamination. NOTE: This is to remove sanding dust. a) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, or one of the abrasives that follow wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005: <1> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 <2> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide <3> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide. b) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. <1> Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. 4) Wipe the surface with a tack rag, G50123. 5) Apply a coat of BMS10-72, Type VIII primer coating, C50084, or BMS10-72, Type IX primer coating, C50085, or BMS10-72, Type X primer coating, C50318, to the surface.

5. BMS10-11 Primer - Application

A. General

(1) This task gives instructions to do the following. (a) Prepare to Apply the BMS10-11 Primer (b) Apply the BMS10-11 Primer (2) recommends that you apply the BMS10-11 chemical- and solvent-resistant finish when the finish temperature is warmer than 50°F (10°C). (a) Contact the paint manufacturer for guidance if the finish temperature is colder than 50°F (10°C). (3) recommends that you apply the BMS10-11 chemical- and solvent-resistant finish when the relative humidity is less than 85%. 51-21-72 (a) Contact the paint manufacturer for guidance if the relative humidity is more than 85%.

E. Apply the BMS10-11 Primer

SUBTASK 51-21-72-160-022 (1) Immediately before you apply the BMS10-11 primer, use a tack rag, G50123 to remove loose dust and lint. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-026 (2) Spray or brush apply the BMS10-11 primer, C00259. (a) Apply the finish in a continuous coat. (b) Make sure that the coat is free of solids, runs, sags, fish eyes, blisters, and non-adherent overspray. SUBTASK 51-21-72-370-027 (3) Cure the primer. (a) If the primer is applied to surfaces other than tungsten base metal, use Table 710, and Figure 703 to cure the primer. Table 710/51-21-72-993-809 BMS10-11 Primer Dry Times and Conditions DRY/CURE FINISH SYSTEM TIMES AND CONDITIONS *[1] Flash off before accelerated dry/cure BMS10-11, Type I, Grade A 3 minutes minimum at room temperature before convective force drying Flash off before accelerated dry/cure BMS10-11, Type I, Grade B 3 minutes minimum at room temperature Flash off before accelerated dry/cure BMS10-11, Type I, Grade E 15 minutes minimum at room temperature Flash off in fastener holes before fastener installation with corrosion preventive compounds or sealants BMS10-11, Type I, Grade A 5 minutes minimum Flash off in fastener holes before fastener installation with corrosion preventive compounds or sealants Grade E (water reduction step is optional) 15 minutes minimum without water reduction; 20 minutes minimum with water reduction Flash off between coats BMS10-11, Type I No flash-off time is required between coats of BMS10-11, Type I primer. SUBTASK 51-21-73-160-020 (3) Use one of the methods that follow to prepare the surface (TABLE). (a) Method 1 1) If there is no surface contamination and the primer will be applied immediately, no surface preparation is necessary. 2) If there is surface contamination, solvent clean the surface. a) Use a wiper, G50262 or one of the abrasives that follow wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. <1> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 <2> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide <3> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide 3) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry wiper, G50262. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. (b) Method 2 1) Solvent clean the surface. a) Use a wiper, G50262 or one of the abrasives that follow wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. <1> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 <2> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide <3> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide 2) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry wiper, G50262. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. 3) Sand the surface. a) Start sanding with one of the abrasives that follow. <1> Aluminum oxide/zirconium oxide abrasive paper, stearate-free, 100-grit to 220-grit <2> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220, 100-grit to 220-grit <3> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide, 100-grit to 220-grit <4> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide, 100-grit to 220-grit b) Finish sanding with one of the abrasives that follow. <1> Aluminum oxide/zirconium oxide abrasive paper, stearate-free, 220-grit or finer <2> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220, 220-grit or finer 51-21-73 <3> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide, 220-grit or finer <4> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide, 220-grit or finer 4) Solvent clean the surface to remove sanding dust. a) Use a wiper, G50262 or one of the abrasives that follow wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. <1> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 <2> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide <3> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide 5) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry wiper, G50262. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. (c) Method 3 1) If the surface is contaminated, do the steps that follow. a) Sand the surface. <1> Start sanding with aluminum oxide/zirconium oxide abrasive paper, stearate-free, 100-grit to 220-grit. <2> Finish sanding with one of the abrasives that follow. <a> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220, 220-grit or finer <b> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide, 220-grit or finer <c> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide, 220-grit or finer <d> Aluminum oxide/zirconium oxide abrasive paper, stearate-free, 220-grit or finer b) Use a wiper, G50262 or one of the abrasives that follow wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. <1> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 <2> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide <3> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide c) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry wiper, G50262. d) Apply Sur-Prep AP-1 (Chemical Reactivator Application, TASK 51-21-73-370-802). (d) Method 4 1) Solvent clean the surface. a) Use a one of the abrasives that follow wet with aliphatic naphtha solvent, B00083 or a 70/30 mixture by volume of methyl propyl ketone solvent, B00666/methyl ethyl ketone solvent, B00148. <1> Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 <2> Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide 51-21-73 <3> Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide 2) Alkaline clean the surface with an abrasive pad with one of the cleaners that follow, diluted with seven parts water, by volume. a) Ardrox 160-B b) Pace B-82 alkaline cleaner, B00017 c) Pace MF-30 cleaner, B50172 d) Turco 4215 e) Ridoline 909, B50052 f) Super Bee 300LF 3) Rinse the surface with large amounts of water. 4) Check for a water-break-free surface. a) If water breaks occur, alkaline clean the surface again and rinse with more water. 5) Dry the surface. T ape after removal shall have no visible effects on the film. *[2] When maximum dry times are exceeded, or if topcoat has been heat cured at temperatures warmer than 110°F (43°C), reactivate the surface. *[3] Some colors may require longer or shorter overcoat time due to cure characteristics, temperature, and humidity. *[4] Measurement does not include primer thickness. *[5] CA8000C1 or CA8000C2 may be substituted for CA8000C for accelerated curing. The thinner blend in the paint mix must not contain both CA8000C1 and CA8000C2 at the same time. Use of thinners containing CA8000C1 or CA8000C2 thinner may only be used on areas where the reduced wet edge and time between coats does not adversely affect the final appearance of the topcoat, including but not limited to rotation areas, speed stripers, door bands, and outdoor work areas. *[6] CA8000C4 or CA8000C5 may be substituted 1:1 for CA8000C for accelerated curing. CA8000C4 or CA8000C5 may only be used for outdoor touch-up or repair. CA8000C4 and CA8000C5 may not be used if the outside air temperature is warmer than 60°F (16°C). *[7] TR-111, TR-112, TR-113, or TR-128 may be substituted for TR-109 for accelerated curing. The thinner blend in the paint mix must not simultaneously contain some combination of TR-111, TR-112, TR-113, and TR-128. Thinners containing TR-111, TR-112, TR-113, or TR-128 thinner may only be used on areas where the reduced wet edge and time between coats does not adversely affect the final appearance of the topcoat, including but not limited to rotation areas, speed stripes, door bands, and outdoor work areas. *[8] Paint mixed with TR-128 may be heat cured at 90°F (32°C) for 4 hours if subsequent colors are to be applied over the base coat. *[9] TR-109 may be blended with TR-112 to achieve a 4-6 hour cure at 90°F (32°C). *[10] TR-141 alternate thinner may be substituted 1:1 for TR-109 standard thinner. It is intended to increase wet edge time when the ambient air temperature is 85°F (29°C) to 100°F (38°C). SUBTASK 51-21-73-950-001 (3) After the final coat of BMS10-72 is applied, but while the enamel is still wet, remove the masking tape from the edge of the bottom paint line. NOTE: This is to reduce the sharp paint edge and build-up which can be more easily corroded. (4) See Table 704 for recommended dry times. SUBTASK 51-21-73-370-005 (5) See Figure 701 for additional information on recommended dry-to-tape times for BMS10-72, Type VIII. SUBTASK 51-21-73-370-006 (6) See Figure 702 for additional information on recommended dry-to-tape times for BMS10-72, Type IX.

3. BMS10-60 Topcoat Application

A. General

(1) This procedure has steps for the following. (a) Prepare the surface (b) Apply BMS10-60 (2) recommends that you apply the BMS10-60 topcoat when the outside air temperature is between 65°F (18°C) and 95°F (35°C). (a) Contact the paint manufacturer for guidance if you will apply the paint outside the recommended temperature range. (3) recommends you apply the BMS10-60 topcoat when the relative humidity is less than 70%. (a) If the relative humidity is more than 70%, you can force cure the coating at temperatures between 120°F (49°C) and 160°F (71°C).

5. Chemical Reactivator Application

A. General

(1) This procedure has steps for the following. (a) Prepare to apply the Sur-Prep AP-1 chemical reactivator. (b) Apply the Sur-Prep AP-1 chemical reactivator. (2) recommends that you apply Sur-Prep AP-1 when the ambient air temperature is between 65°F (18°C) and 90°F (32°C). (a) Contact the paint manufacturer for guidance if you will apply Sur-Prep AP-1 outside the recommended temperature range. (3) recommends that you apply Sur-Prep AP-1 when the relative humidity is less than 70%. (a) Contact the paint manufacturer for guidance if you will apply Sur-Prep AP-1 when the relative humidity is more than 70%. D. Prepare to Apply the Sur-Prep AP-1 Chemical Reactivator

SUBTASK 51-21-73-370-007 (1) Mix the Sur-Prep AP-1 using the manufacturer's instructions. (a) Make sure that the ambient air temperature is between 65°F (18°C) and 90°F (32°C). (b) Make sure that no liquid water or moisture mixes with the chemical reactivator. NOTE: Liquid water or moisture mixed with the chemical reactivator can cause a white precipitate and can affect the bond between topcoats. SUBTASK 51-21-73-950-003 (2) Mask the areas that will not be coated with Sur-Prep AP-1. (a) Attach the tags that follow to the left control wheel in the flight deck. 1) "PITOT PROBES COVERED" tag, G02447 2) "STATIC PORTS COVERED" tag, G02444 3) A red tag labeled “AOA SENSORS COVERED” (b) Put a pitot probe cover, COM-1503 on the pitot probe. (c) Apply Scotch Flatback Masking T ape 250, G00270 on the static ports. (d) Do the steps that follow to cover the angle-of-attack (AOA) sensors. 1) Cover the angle-of-attack sensors with PG-777 solvent-resistant masking tape. a) Apply PG-777 over the blade, plate, and blade-to-plate gap. NOTE: This is to allow easier removal of 3M 425 aluminum tape. 2) Cover the PG-777 solvent-resistant masking tape with 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. a) Shingle the aluminum foil tape from the blade-to-plate gap up to the blade tip until all of the masking tape is covered. SUBTASK 51-21-73-160-017 (3) If there is surface contamination, do the steps that follow to clean the surface. (a) Solvent clean the surface. 1) Use a wiper, G50262 wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. 2) Immediately wipe the surface with a clean, dry wiper, G50262. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. (b) Sand the surface, if necessary to remove contamination. 1) Use one of the abrasives that follow. a) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 b) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide c) Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide (c) If you sand the surface, solvent clean the surface to remove sanding dust. 1) Use a wiper, G50262 wet with Series 85 solvent, B01005. 51-21-73 2) Immediately wipe the surface with a clean, dry wiper, G50262. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-73-370-008 (4) Make sure that the conditions in Figure 706 are met.

E. Apply the Sur-Prep AP-1 Chemical Reactivator

SUBTASK 51-21-73-370-009 (1) Spray apply the Sur-Prep AP-1 using one of the tools that follow. (a) High volume, low pressure (HVLP) gun (b) Air assisted airless spray gun (c) Electrostatic spray equipment SUBTASK 51-21-73-370-010 (2) Make sure that all necessary areas are coated with a thin, wet film. (a) If there is overspray of Sur-Prep AP-1 onto surfaces that do not need to be reactivated and that have not been masked, do the steps that follow. 1) Use a wiper, G50262 or one of the abrasives that follow wet with methyl propyl ketone (MPK) solvent, B00666 or a 70/30 mixture of MPK solvent, B00666/methyl ethyl ketone (MEK) solvent, B00148. a) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 b) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide c) Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide 2) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry wiper, G50262. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. SUBTASK 51-21-73-370-011 (3) Keep the Sur-Prep AP-1 on the surface for 30 minutes to 24 hours in the conditions in Figure 706 before applying topcoat. (a) If the Sur-Prep AP-1 is not dry after 30 minutes, let the Sur-Prep AP-1 dry for a longer time. SUBTASK 51-21-73-160-018 (4) If the chemical reactivator has runs or if there are very wet areas after you apply the Sur-Prep AP-1, do the steps that follow. (a) Dry the defect area with clean, compressed air. (b) Solvent clean the defect area. NOTE: This is to remove the dried powder. 1) Use a wiper, G50262 or one of the abrasives that follow wet with methyl propyl ketone (MPK) solvent, B00666 or a 70/30 mixture, by volume, of MPK solvent, B00666/methyl ethyl ketone (MEK) solvent, B00148. a) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 b) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide c) Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide (c) Re-apply the Sur-Prep AP-1 51-21-73 SUBTASK 51-21-73-370-012 (5) If the Sur-Prep AP-1 is on the surface for more than 24 hours or if there is contamination, debris, contact with water, or rubbing with materials, do the steps that follow. (a) Remove the Sur-Prep AP-1. 1) Use a wiper, G50262 or one of the abrasives that follow wet with methyl propyl ketone (MPK) solvent, B00666 or a 70/30 mixture of MPK solvent, B00666/methyl ethyl ketone (MEK) solvent, B00148. a) Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G50220 b) Scotch-Brite Clean and Finish, very fine, aluminum oxide c) Norton Bear-T ex 747 General Purpose Hand Pad, very fine, aluminum oxide 2) Immediately wipe the surface dry with a clean, dry wiper, G50262. a) Make sure that the solvent does not dry on the surface. 3) Wipe the surface with a tack rag, G50123. 4) Re-apply the Sur-Prep AP-1.

ABRASIVE PADS CAN SMOOTH THE ALUMINUM SURFACE AND HIDE THE SCRIBE LINE MARKS. IF YOU USE ABRASIVE PADS TO REMOVE THE PAINT OR PRIMER BEFORE YOU DO THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS, YOU CAN BE REQUIRED TO DO REPEAT INSPECTIONS BASED ON THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTION SERVICE BULLETIN. (c) Remove all unwanted material from the surface. Use an approved sealant removal tool, COM-2481 with sealant removal tool handle, COM-4746 to clean around fasteners, seams, and lap joints. NOTE: If you use abrasive pads before you do scribe line inspections, you can be required to do repeat inspections based on the scribe line inspections Service Bulletin 737-53A1289. NOTE: An abrasive mat, G00251 or abrasive cloth, B00102 may be used instead of the scraper. (d) Clean the surface again with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with the solvent. (e) Dry the surface with a clean cotton wiper, G00034 before the solvent dries.

51-21-91-620-801Surface Preparation for Corrosion Inhibiting CompoundPDF p. 347

2. Surface Preparation for Corrosion Inhibiting Compound

A. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification B00074 Solvent - Degreasing MIL-PRF-680 (Supersedes P-D-680) B00093 Solvent - T etrachloroethylene (Perchloroethylene) ASTM D4081 B00316 Solvent - Aliphatic Naphtha (For Organic Coatings) TT-N-95 Type I, ASTM D-3735 Type I B00634 Solvent - Stabilized Limonene Cleaner BMS11-10 Type 1, 2, or 3 51-21-91 (Continued) Reference Description Specification G00034 Cotton Wiper - Process Cleaning Absorbent Wiper (Cheesecloth, Gauze) AMS3819 Class 1 Grade A or B Form 1 (Supersede BMS15-5 CL A) G00270 T ape - Scotch Flatback Masking 250 ASTM D6123 (Supersedes A-A-883) G50305 Sheeting - Plastic, Polyethylene

B. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-21-91-620-001 (1) Do these steps to prepare the surface for the corrosion inhibiting compound. (a) Do these steps to clean the surfaces: 1) Vacuum the surfaces as necessary to remove moisture and other excessive foreign material. 2) Wipe the surfaces with a cloth (cotton wiper, G00034) as necessary to remove additional moisture or other foreign materials. WARNING DO NOT GET THE SOLVENT IN YOUR MOUTH, EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE IN THE FUMES FROM THE SOLVENT . MAKE SURE TO PUT ON PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLES AND GLOVES WHEN USING THE SOLVENT . KEEP THE SOLVENT AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAMES AND HEAT . THE SOLVENT IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY OR DAMAGE IF NOT HANDLED PROPERLY . (b) When the area is very dirty, clean the surface with one of these applicable solvents: NOTE: You must fully clean the surface to help the corrosion inhibiting compound get on the surface and in the mating surfaces. 1) solvent, B00074. 2) solvent, B00093. 3) solvent, B00316. 4) Limonene solvent, B00634 SUBTASK 51-21-91-600-003 (2) Apply Scotch Flatback Masking T ape 250, G00270 and plastic sheeting, G50305 to the area where you will not apply the corrosion preventive compound. SUBTASK 51-21-91-600-002 WARNING DO NOT APPLY THE CORROSION-INHIBITING COMPOUNDS IN THE AREAS THAT HAVE OXYGEN SYSTEM COMPONENTS. THE MIXTURE OF CORROSION-INHIBITING COMPOUNDS, AND OXYGEN CAN CAUSE AN EXPLOSION. AN EXPLOSION CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (3) Make sure you keep all corrosion inhibiting compounds out of the oxygen system components that follow: NOTE: Masking tape is not sufficient. Use plastic sheets or equivalent covers to fully seal these components from the compound. 51-21-91 (a) Bottles. (b) Pressure metering equipment. (c) Indicating equipment. (d) Connections. SUBTASK 51-21-91-280-001 (4) Do not apply corrosion inhibiting compound to the areas that follow: (a) Near the engines. (b) Cowlings. (c) Areas of high temperature or where firewall sealant is used. NOTE: High temperature causes deterioration in corrosion preventive compounds. (d) Electrical ground strap/surface interfaces to make sure you have a sufficient ground path. (e) Bare surfaces that get a layer of primer and paint. NOTE: It is not easy to apply a primer and paint on the corrosion preventive compound. The corrosion preventive compound gets in the surface and can bleed-out. This can cause the primer and paint to have a unsatisfactory bond. 1) Let the primer and enamel dry for a minimum of 8 hours before you apply the corrosion preventive compound. (f) Sliding pins and other mechanical joints in a sliding surface contact. (g) Actuator rods. NOTE: Corrosion preventive compound such as BMS 3-23 or all other hydrocarbons can cause damage to the seals that are used with BMS 3-11 hydraulic fluid. SUBTASK 51-21-91-600-001 (5) The areas that follow must be shielded or protected to make sure the corrosion inhibiting compound is not applied: (a) Control cables and pulleys. (b) Wire bundles, coax connectors. (c) Mechanical silicone seals. (d) Insulation blankets. (e) Bushing and bearings. (f) Cam surfaces. (g) Lubricated components. (h) Pneumatic ducts with surface temperatures that are more than 200°F (93°C) during normal operations. (i) Applicable drain valves. (j) Areas that will be painted or sealed. (k) High visual items such as doorways, hatches, and window frames.

51-21-91-620-802Application of Corrosion Inhibiting CompoundPDF p. 350

3. Application of Corrosion Inhibiting Compound

A. General

WARNING THE BMS3-23 AND BMS3-29 ARE HAZARDOUS MATERIALS. WHEN YOU SPRAY THESE COMPOUNDS IN A CLOSED AREA, A GAS CONCENTRATION OF 500 PPM (PARTS PER MILLION) IS THE MAXIMUM COMFORTABLE AND SAFE WORKING LIMIT . AT THIS CONCENTRATION, A PERSON CAN WORK FOR 8 HOURS. GAS LEVELS MORE THAN 500 PPM ARE NOT FULLY HAZARDOUS, BUT YOU MUST SUPPLY A FLOW OF AIR TO KEEP THE AREA COMFORTABLE AND SAFE. IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW THESE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR. WARNING ALIPHATIC NAPHTHA IS THE RECOMMENDED SOLVENT AND IS ALSO POISONOUS. IF YOU USE NAPHTHA IN A CONFINED SPACE, MECHANICAL VENTILATION IS MANDATORY . RESPIRATORY DEVICES AND SKIN PROTECTION ARE NECESSARY . IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW THESE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR. (1) This procedure gives instructions to apply the water-displacing corrosion preventive compound. We recommended that you apply the compound periodically. NOTE: Each airline must know it's aircraft's environment, the corrosion inhibiting compounds they use, and when it was applied. If not, the corrosion protection can be unsatisfactory. recommends BMS3-23, BMS3-26, BMS3-29 and BMS3-35 and has made them a standard for organic corrosion inhibitors. But, there are other water-displacing corrosion inhibiting compounds that are satisfactory for use. WARNING KEEP BMS3-23 AWAY FROM SURFACES THAT CAN BE 150 DEGREES F (66 DEGREES C) OR MORE DURING USE. THE DRY FILM FLASH POINT IS 500 DEGREES F(260 DEGREES C). THE BMS 3-23 CAN CAUSE A FIRE OR AN EXPLOSION. (2) The corrosion preventive compound is not satisfactory for surfaces that can be more than 150°F (66°C) because it contains wax compounds.

B. Consumable Materials

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-21-91-620-002 (1) Apply the corrosion inhibiting compound. (a) Clean surface with solvent, B00083, or citra-safe solvent, B50226. (b) Apply the corrosion inhibiting compound to a thickness as shown in COATING THICKNESS RANGES Corrosion Inhibiting CompoundCoating Thickness DryCoating Thickness Wet(BMS3-23)Continuous Coat, No Minimum ThicknessContinuous Coat, No Minimum Thickness(BMS3-26, Type I)0.00/Table 701. Table 701/51-21-91-993-801 COATING THICKNESS RANGES Corrosion Inhibiting Compound Coating Thickness Dry Coating Thickness Wet corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 (BMS3-23) Continuous Coat, No Minimum Thickness Continuous Coat, No Minimum Thickness compound, C00755 (BMS3-26, Type I) 0.002 ±0.001 in. (0.051 ±0.026 mm) 0.004 ±0.002 in. (0.102 ±0.051 mm) compound, G50346 (BMS3-26, Type II) 0.005 ±0.001 in. (0.127 ±0.025 mm) 0.010 ±0.002 in. (0.254 ±0.051 mm) compound, C00915 (BMS3-29) 0.004 ±0.001 in. (0.102 ±0.026 mm) 0.008 ±0.002 in. (0.203 ±0.051 mm) compound, G50071 (BMS3–35) 0.002 ±0.001 in. (0.051 ±0.026 mm) 0.004 ±0.002 in. (0.102 ±0.051 mm) (c) The application temperature for BMS3-23, BMS3-26 Type I and BMS3-29, must be between 40°F (4°C) and 100°F (38°C). (d) The application temperature for BMS3-26 Type II must be between 50°F (10°C) and 100°F (38°C). (e) The application temperature for BMS3-35 must be between 32°F (0°C) and 86°F (30°C). (f) Spray or brush the BMS3-23 compound to get a continuous coat. (g) Spray or brush either the BMS3-26, BMS3-29 or BMS3-35 compound to get a bubble free coat (after it is dry), with a wet or dry thickness as specified in Table 701. NOTE: When the BMS3-26, BMS3-29 and BMS3-35 compound is not sprayed, shake or mix the compound before it is used. (h) When the compound is applied to parts where it cannot be sprayed or brushed (e.g. slotted tracks), do the step that follows: 1) Fill the area with the compound, and then drain the compound which will give a protective coat. (i) When BMS3-29 is specified as an optional material to BMS3-23, use the same specifications as for the BMS3-29. (j) Use a cloth (cotton wiper, G00034) to remove the puddles of too much of the compound if the puddles cause a blockage to the drain holes or cross drains. 51-21-91 (k) Make sure that you have a good flow of air in the areas where the corrosion inhibiting compound was applied, as follows: NOTE: The air flow times are recommended minimum times. A longer air flow time to get a satisfactory evaporation is recommended for lower temperatures, high humidity, and when too much of the compound is applied. NOTE: You must keep the temperature within the application limits for the material used. 1) After you apply the BMS3–23 in enclosed areas, apply a good air flow to the area for a minimum of one hour before you close-up the area. NOTE: The one hour will let the volatile solvents in the compound to evaporate. 2) After you apply the BMS3-26, BMS3–29 or the BMS3-35 in enclosed areas, apply a good air flow to the area for a minimum of four hours before you close-up the area. 3) Do not remove the masking tape or applicable covers until the corrosion inhibiting compound has dried sufficiently. This will make sure that the compound will not rub off or move to another surface. a) When the masking tape or covers have been removed, do a touch-up of the corrosion inhibiting compound where it is necessary to prevent corrosion in the areas of a structural interface. (l) Do not contaminate the insulation blankets with the corrosion inhibiting compound. NOTE: These compounds can decrease the ability of the insulation blankets to repel water. WARNING DO NOT USE DETERGENTS OR SOLVENTS TO CLEAN THE INSULATION BLANKET . IT CAN REMOVE FLAME RETARDANTS AND CAUSE FLAMMABLE RESIDUES ON THE INSULATION BLANKET WHICH INCREASES THE RISK OF FIRE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . 1) If contamination occurs, the blanket must be replaced.

(0.152 mm) in thickness. 2) Push the polyethylene film, G00252 against the corrosion inhibiting compound with a light finger pressure. 3) Make a check to see if the corrosion inhibiting compound has moved to the polyethylene film, G00252 or lifted from the structure. (b) The table that follows will give you the approximate cure times. NOTE: Follow the manufacturers instruction for the applicable cure times. Table 702/51-21-91-993-802 Approximate Cure Times Compound Time BMS3-23 *[1] 1 Hour BMS3-26, Type I 6 Hours BMS3-26, Type II 6 Hours BMS3–29 4 Hours BMS3–35 2 Hours *[1] BMS3–23 Class 1, will not cure in 1 hour, however, this is a sufficient amount of time to allow solvents to flash off prior to installation of insulation blankets. BMS3–23 Class 1, does not cure to a tack free coating.

51-21-91-620-804Repair of Corrosion Inhibiting Compound CoatingPDF p. 353

5. Repair of Corrosion Inhibiting Compound Coating

A. General

(1) The limits of the damage or bubbles in the BMS3-23, BMS3-26, BMS3-29 or BMS3-35 corrosion inhibiting compound in the cured coating is as follows and must be repaired: (a) The coating damage dimension is more than 1 percent of a given 1 ft 2 (929 cm 2). (b) The coating damage dimension is larger than 1 in 2 (6 cm 2). (2) All damage or bubbles in the cured BMS3–23, BMS3-26, BMS3-29 and BMS3-35 coating must be repaired. NOTE: When BMS3-29 or BMS3-35 is specified as optional to BMS3-23, the damage permitted will be the same as that necessary for the BMS3-23.

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-21-91-620-004 (1) Do the steps that follow to repair the damaged or contaminated corrosion inhibiting compound. (a) Clean the damaged area with solvent, B00316 or Limonene solvent, B00634. 51-21-91 (b) Apply the applicable corrosion inhibiting compound, do this task: Application of Corrosion Inhibiting Compound, TASK 51-21-91-620-802. (c) Cure the corrosion inhibiting compound, do this task: Cure of Corrosion Inhibiting Compound, TASK 51-21-91-620-803.

51-21-92-600-801Seat Track Filler ApplicationPDF p. 355

2. Seat Track Filler Application (Figure 201, Figure 202)

A. General

(1) Seat track filler prevents corrosion in wet areas of the passenger compartment. (2) You can cut and remove parts of the seat track fillers when you remove and install galleys, lavs, and tie down fittings.

B. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification A02315 Sealant - Low Density, Synthetic Rubber. 2 Part BMS5-142 Type II C00308 Compound - Corrosion Preventive, Petrolatum Hot Application MIL-C-11796 G02304 T ape - Moisture Barrier, Adhesive One-side BMS8-346

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 200 Upper Half of Fuselage

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-21-92-620-001 (1) Apply filler sealant, A02315 in the seat tracks as follows: (a) Find the seat track locations in the wet areas of the airplane. (b) Cut the seat track filler [1] to fit in the seat tracks [3]. NOTE: The seat track filler is pre- formed and commercially available. NOTE: A gap of 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) is permitted at the skin splice areas. (c) Install the seat track filler [1] in the seat track [3]. (d) Fill the seat track [3] with corrosion preventive compound, C00308. (e) Install approximately 2.0 in. (5.1 cm) of sealant, A02315 at the end of the compound filled area to contain the compound. (f) Make sure the top surface of the seat track [3] is clean and free of compound. (g) Install moisture barrier tape, G02304 [2] on the compound filled seat track [3].

Zone Area 200 Upper Half of Fuselage

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-21-93-160-001 (1) Do this task: (Clean the Surface to be Painted, TASK 51-21-21-100-801). SUBTASK 51-21-93-370-005 WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH OR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM SOLVENTS. PUT ON A RESPIRATOR, PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLES, AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE SOLVENTS. KEEP THE SOLVENTS AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . SOLVENTS ARE POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE. SOLVENTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (2) Mix the primer, C00039 or the 911-P4 primer, C50117 per manufacturer instructions: SUBTASK 51-21-93-370-006 (3) Apply the primer, C00039 or the primer, C50117 on the surface with a spray gun. NOTE: For rivet and screw heads, brush apply primer and avoid application to surfaces with topcoat. SUBTASK 51-21-93-370-007 (4) Let the primer dry (minimum of 10 minutes and maximum of 60 minutes) at 70°F (21°C) to 90°F (32°C) before you apply the Alexit Suede 404-74 Topcoat coating, C50143. SUBTASK 51-21-93-370-008 (5) Mix the Alexit Suede 404-74 Topcoat coating, C50143 components as follows: (a) Pour desired amount of Alexit Suede 404-74 Topcoat coating, C50143 - 1 part (by volume). (b) Add base component I (405-28) - 8 parts (by volume) 51-21-93 (c) Add thinner (62) - 0.5 to 1.5 parts (by volume) NOTE: If the topcoat is to be applied to rivet and screw heads add 8 parts of thinner (by volume). (d) Identify the container with a label. Write the date and the hour when the mixture was mixed. Also, write the date and hour when the application time ends. NOTE: Potlife is 6 hours at 60°F (16°C) to 85°F (29°C) after mixing. SUBTASK 51-21-93-370-009 (6) Apply the Alexit Suede 404-74 Topcoat coating, C50143 on the primed surface with a spray gun. NOTE: Avoid dry spray. Dry spray will result in a rough surface. Additionally, heavy coats may result in color deviation (depending on pigmentation/color), runs/sagging and cracking of the dry film. In addition, varying amounts of thinner may cause color deviation. NOTE: For application of topcoat to rivet heads and screw heads, place stencil flush to the painted surface having a hole in it equal to the rivet or screw head being painted. Using an airbrush (or equivalent), spray apply the topcoat through the hole in the stencil until the dry finish matches the rest of the panel. SUBTASK 51-21-93-370-010 (7) Cure the Alexit Suede 404-74 Topcoat coating, C50143. Refer to (Figure 701) for the cure times. NOTE: Curing at 70°F (21°C) (minimum) is 4 hrs. (minimum).

C. Prepare the Surface

SUBTASK 51-21-94-180-001 (1) Prepare the aluminum surfaces. (a) Apply a layer of chromic acid anodizing or alodizing to all aluminum surfaces. (b) Apply a layer of primer, C00259, epoxy primer. (c) Let the primers dry before you apply the abrasion resistant finish. 1) Let the primers dry for a minimum of 1 hour at room temperature or 15 minutes at 150° ±15°F (65.6° ± 8.3°C). SUBTASK 51-21-94-180-002 (2) Prepare the painted surfaces. (a) If it is less than 48 hours since you applied the BMS 10-11 epoxy primer: 1) Clean the surface with solvent, B00094. 2) Dry the surface with a clean, dry cotton wiper, G00034. (b) If it is more than 48 hours since you applied the BMS 10-11 epoxy primer: 1) Clean the surface with solvent, B00094 or solvent, B00151. 2) Rub the surface with 320-grit (minimum) abrasive cloth, B00102 aluminum oxide paper. 3) Clean the surface again with Methyl Isobutyl Ketone. SUBTASK 51-21-94-100-001 (3) Prepare the steel surfaces. (a) Apply one layer of primer, C00259, epoxy primer on the surface. 51-21-94

D. Apply the Abrasion Resistant Finish

SUBTASK 51-21-94-370-001 WARNING DO NOT GET THE FINISHES, CLEANERS, THINNERS AND SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH OR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN OR CLOTHES. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THESE MATERIALS. MAKE SURE THE AIR FLOWS FREELY THROUGH THE WORK AREA. USE THE NECESSARY RESPIRATORY PROTECTION. KEEP THESE MATERIALS AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME AND HEAT . THESE MATERIALS ARE POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . WARNING DO NOT GET TERECO 155 ON YOUR SKIN. TERECO 155 CONTAINS DANGEROUS COMPOUNDS THAT CAN CAUSE INJURY . (1) Mix the abrasion resistant finish. NOTE: The abrasion resistant finish has T ereco 155 base material (part A) and T ereco 155 accelerator (part B). Mix each component fully before you mix parts A and B together. (a) If you apply the finish with a medium nylon bristle brush, STD-3911: 1) Add 25 parts (by weight) of part B to 100 parts (by weight) of part A. 2) To make the solution thin, add 9 parts (by weight) of solvent, B00094, toluene or solvent, B00344, xylene for each 125 parts (by weight) of the finish mixture. NOTE: The thinner is added to part B before you mix part A and B. (b) If you apply the finish with a spray paint spray gun with interchangeable nozzles, STD-1133: 1) Add 25 parts (by weight) of part B to 100 parts (by weight) of part A. 2) To make the solution thin, add 20 to 30 parts (by weight) of the toluene or xylene for each 125 parts (by weight) of the finish mixture. NOTE: The thinner is added to part B before you mix part A and B. (c) Do not touch or move the mixture for a minimum of 5 minutes before you use it. (d) Do not use T ereco 155 with the expired application time (Figure 701). (e) Remove material with the expired application time. (f) Do not mix more T ereco 155 than you can use (Figure 701). SUBTASK 51-21-94-950-001 (2) Apply tape or covers on areas adjacent to the work area. SUBTASK 51-21-94-370-002 (3) Apply the abrasion resistant finish. (a) Apply one or more layers of T ereco 155 with a brush or a spray gun. (b) Let the finish dry between each layer. (c) Make sure the dry layer is 0.003-0.020 inch (0.076-0.508 mm) thick. (d) Let the finish dry for a minimum of 8 hours at 70° ±5°F (21.1° 2.8°C) before you touch the surface or part. (e) Let the finish dry for a minimum of 12 hours before flight. 51-21-94 (f) Before assembly, use the time-temperature conditions shown in Curve A to dry the finish (Figure 702). (g) Before functional movement of parts, use the time-temperature conditions shown in Curve B to dry the finish (Figure 702). CAUTION DO NOT USE ABRASIVE PADS (SCOTCH-BRITE), OR ABRASIVE PAPER ON THE ALUMINUM SURFACE UNLESS THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS WERE MADE. ABRASIVE PADS CAN SMOOTH THE ALUMINUM SURFACE AND HIDE THE SCRIBE LINE MARKS. IF YOU USE ABRASIVE PADS TO REMOVE THE PAINT OR PRIMER BEFORE YOU DO THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS, YOU CAN BE REQUIRED TO DO REPEAT INSPECTIONS BASED ON THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTION SERVICE BULLETIN. CAUTION ONLY USE APPROVED SCRAPERS ON THE AIRPLANE SKIN. SCRAPERS THAT ARE NOT APPROVED CAN MAKE SCRATCHES ON THE SKIN, AND CAUSE FATIGUE CRACKS. (h) Remove all of the sharp paint edges with a sealant removal tool, COM-2481 with sealant removal tool handle, COM-4746. NOTE: The shelf life of T ereco 155 is 6 months from the manufacture date. NOTE: If you use abrasive pads before you do scribe line inspections, you can be required to do repeat inspections based on the scribe line inspection Service Bulletin 737-53A1289. (i) Make sure not to cause damage to the aluminum skin.

E. Repair and Rework Damaged Surfaces

SUBTASK 51-21-94-350-001 (1) Rework areas where it is necessary. (a) Clean the surfaces (Refer to SUBTASK 51-21-94-180-001, SUBTASK 51-21-94-180-002, or SUBTASK 51-21-94-100-001). (b) Apply the abrasion resistant finish (Refer to SUBTASK 51-21-94-370-001, SUBTASK 51-21-94-950-001, and SUBTASK 51-21-94-370-002). (c) Remove all of the sharp paint edges with sealant removal tool, COM-2481 or other applicable tool. SUBTASK 51-21-94-350-002 (2) Repair the damaged areas of the abrasion resistant finish. (a) Rub the surface with 280-grit (minimum) abrasive cloth, B00102 aluminum oxide paper. 1) If primer, C00259, has scratches after this step, apply the primer again. 2) Repair the aluminum surfaces that have scratches (Refer to SUBTASK 51-21-94-370-001, SUBTASK 51-21-94-950-001, SUBTASK 51-21-94-370-002, SUBTASK 51-21-94-350-001, and SUBTASK 51-21-94-350-002) (b) Clean the area with a wet cheesecloth that is moist with toluene. (c) Apply abrasion resistant finish (Refer to SUBTASK 51-21-94-370-001, SUBTASK 51-21-94-950-001, and SUBTASK 51-21-94-370-002).

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 51-21-95-110-001 (1) Remove corrosion preventative paint in the area where there is corrosion (PAINT STRIPPING - CLEANING/PAINTING, PAGEBLOCK 51-21-11/701). SUBTASK 51-21-95-110-002 (2) Remove primer, C00259 or coating, C00307 primers. (a) Lightly rub the primer smooth with abrasive cloth, B00102 to the area immediately adjacent to the corrosion. 51-21-95 SUBTASK 51-21-95-140-001 CAUTION DO NOT USE ABRASIVE PADS (SCOTCH-BRITE), OR ABRASIVE PAPER ON THE ALUMINUM SURFACE UNLESS THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS WERE MADE. ABRASIVE PADS CAN SMOOTH THE ALUMINUM SURFACE AND HIDE THE SCRIBE LINE MARKS. IF YOU USE ABRASIVE PADS TO REMOVE THE PAINT OR PRIMER BEFORE YOU DO THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTIONS, YOU CAN BE REQUIRED TO DO REPEAT INSPECTIONS BASED ON THE SCRIBE LINE INSPECTION SERVICE BULLETIN. CAUTION ONLY USE APPROVED SCRAPERS ON THE AIRPLANE SKIN. SCRAPERS THAT ARE NOT APPROVED CAN MAKE SCRATCHES ON THE SKIN, AND CAUSE FATIGUE CRACKS. (3) Remove the fastener sealant with a sealant removal tool, COM-2481 with sealant removal tool handle, COM-4746. NOTE: If you use abrasive pads before you do scribe line inspections, you can be required to do repeat inspections based on the scribe line inspection Service Bulletin 737-53A1289. SUBTASK 51-21-95-110-003 WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH, OR YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS ARE HAZARDOUS MATERIALS. REFER TO PRODUCT MATERIAL SAFETY DATA SHEETS (MSDS) AND LOCAL REQUIREMENTS FOR PROPER HANDLING PROCEDURES. (4) Remove fastener sealant with solvent, B00666. SUBTASK 51-21-95-950-001 (5) Apply 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291 to all fuel tank openings to prevent entry of grit. SUBTASK 51-21-95-160-001 (6) Remove rust and corrosion. (a) Use a portable blaster to remove rust from fastener heads and adjacent skin area. (b) Use a portable blaster to remove corrosion from the skin to an approved depth. (c) As an alternative, remove rust and corrosion with a 240-grit aluminum oxide abrasive cloth, B00102 paper or cloth. (d) Use a 5 to 10X magnifying glass to examine the countersunk area around the fastener heads for corrosion. CAUTION MAKE SURE TO REMOVE ONLY ONE ROW OF RIVETS AT A TIME IN A MORE-THAN-ONE ROW FASTENER CONFIGURATION. REPLACE THESE FASTENERS BEFORE YOU REMOVE THE FASTENERS FROM THE NEXT ROW TO PREVENT SKIN MOVEMENT . IN A ONE ROW CONFIGURATION, REMOVE AND INSTALL EACH SECOND FASTENERS. (e) Remove the fasteners with corrosion in the countersunk area. (f) Remove the corrosion from the fastener to an approved depth.

D. Prepare the Surface for treatment

NOTE: It is not necessary to clean all areas for chemical conversion coating treatment. Only clean the areas where skin or fasteners are open to the base metal during the removal of rust and corrosion. SUBTASK 51-21-95-580-001 (1) Park the airplane away from the sun and electrically ground (AIRPLANE GROUNDING - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES, PAGEBLOCK 20-40-11/201). 51-21-95 SUBTASK 51-21-95-160-002 (2) Clean the surface correctly to get a satisfactory coating. WARNING DO NOT GET THE ADHESIVES, FINISHES, CLEANERS, THINNERS, AND SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH, OR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATH THE FUMES FROM THESE MATERIALS. PUT ON RESPIRATOR, PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLES, AND PROTECTIVE GLOVES WHEN YOU USE THESE MATERIALS. KEEP THESE MATERIALS AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THESE MATERIALS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (a) Prepare the solution as follows: 1) Use one part (by volume) solvent alkaline cleaner to two parts water and five to six parts BMS 3-2 Type I solvent. (b) Apply the cleaner solution and let it soak for a minimum of 10 minutes. NOTE: The solution must be wet on the skins. Apply the cleaner again if it is necessary. (c) Clean the skins with a soft bristle brush, STD-123. 1) Make sure to clean the countersunk areas and around the rivet heads. (d) Flush the surface with water (100°F (37.8°C) maximum) at high pressure. (e) Examine the surface for water breaks. NOTE: A surface with no water breaks has a continuous layer of water for a minimum of 30 seconds. (f) Clean the skin again if there are water breaks.

E. Apply the coating treatment

SUBTASK 51-21-95-370-001 (1) Prepare Coating: NOTE: In areas where the chemical conversion coating may come in contact with BMS 10-20 primer, only Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862, should be used. NOTE: Keep the room temperature above 65°F (18.3°C). WARNING DO NOT GET CHEMICAL CONVERSION COATING SOLUTION IN YOUR MOUTH, IN YOUR EYES, ON YOUR SKIN, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THIS MATERIAL. AIR MUST FLOW FREELY THROUGH THE WORK AREA. USE THE NECESSARY RESPIRATORY PROTECTION. KEEP THIS MATERIAL AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THIS MATERIAL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (a) Put coating, C00064, on paper and use a roller to make the powder smooth. (b) Mix the solution in a stainless steel container (1 gal) (4 Liter), STD-1118 or acid resistant container, STD-1052. NOTE: Do not use lead or glass. (c) For Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862: Add 3 oz (85 g) of powder to water for each gallon (3.8 liters) of final solution. 1) Stir until the powder is dissolved. 51-21-95 2) Add up to 2% by volume of Bonderite M-AD 22 Toner Aero surface treatment, C50358, or ammonium hydroxide as required to adjust pH to between 1.5 and 2.0. (d) For Bonderite M-CR ALCRM1200 Aero coating, C50357: 3 oz (85 g) of powder to water for each gallon (3.8 liters) of final solution. 1) Stir until the powder is dissolved. 2) Keep the pH in the range of 1.50 - 1.90. 3) Adjust the pH down with nitric acid or ammonium hydroxide. (e) For Bonderite M-CR 1200S Aero coating, C50005: Add 1.9 oz (53.9 g) – 2.1 oz (59.5 g) of powder to water for each gallon (3.8 liters) of final solution. (f) For Bonderite M-CR 1600 Aero coating, C50447: Add 0.8 fl-oz (23.7 ml) of additive for each gallon (3.8 liters) of final solution. 1) Stir well to ensure a uniform mixture. 2) Add up to 2% by volume of Bonderite M-AD 22 Toner Aero surface treatment, C50358, as required to adjust the pH to between 1.5 - 2.0. (g) For Bonderite M-AD 1660 Aero coating Additive, C50448: Add 2.6 fl-oz (76.9 ml) of additive for each gallon (3.8 liters) of final solution. 1) Stir well to ensure a uniform mixture. 2) Add up to 2% by volume of Bonderite M-AD 22 Toner Aero surface treatment, C50358, as required to adjust the pH to between 1.5 - 2.0. (h) For other coating, C00064, refer to manufacturer's instructions for the correct preparation. (i) Fully mix the solution until the powder is dissolved. Ignore small quantities of material which do not dissolve. (j) Allow to stand for 1 hour before use. NOTE: Prepare the solution in small quantities. Discard the solution after you use it if a brush, sponge, or wiper was put into it or if contamination gets into the solution. Do not add wetting agents or other materials to this solution. (2) Apply coating, C00064. NOTE: In areas where the chemical conversion coating may come in contact with BMS 10-20 primer, only Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862, should be used. WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH OR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THESE MATERIALS. PUT ON A PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLE AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE THESE MATERIALS. KEEP THESE MATERIALS AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THESE MATERIALS ARE POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (a) apply coating, C00064, equally with a medium nylon bristle brush, STD-3911, or a cotton wiper, G00034, or a cellulose sponge, or mop (cotton). Start from the bottom. 51-21-95 (b) Let the solution stay on the surface until a given color is found (approximately 2 - 3 minutes). Keep the area wet. Apply small quantities of solution with a cotton wiper, G00034. NOTE: Do not let the coating, C00064, solution dry until the color of the surface changes. NOTE: If the color does not come, if the solution breaks up into beads, or if a powdery layer occurs, lightly sand area with 600-grit paper and apply the coating again. (c) Carefully flush the surface with a cotton wiper, G00034, that is moist with water. Start from the bottom. NOTE: Be careful when you rub or dry the surface. Do not remove the coating or cause scratches on the surface. (d) Lightly rub the surface with a clean dry cotton wiper, G00034, to remove unwanted liquid. Rub the surface until the liquid is gone. (e) Immediately after use, fully clean the cloths in water and keep them in a container filled with water. (f) Air dry the surface. NOTE: Dry at 120°F (48.9°C) (optimum), 130°F (54.4°C) (maximum). (g) Apply the last finish or start adhesive bonding (Chapter 51 of the Structural Repair Manual). Touch the parts or surface with rubber glove, STD-1086, and keep the parts or surface dry and clean to prevent surface contamination.
